sources.title: Prediction markets put Jensen Huang’s odds of returning at 11% on Sunday night—hours later he was back as Nvidia CEO - Fortune
passages: Prediction markets have proved prescient when it comes to forecasting elections and other events, but in the case of Jensen Huang’s abrupt return as Nvidia’s CEO, they appeared as much in the dark as everyone else.
A look at contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket tied to the company’s next CEO reveals an abrupt swing from long shots to near certainties when the board reinstated him Monday morning.
As of Sunday evening, Nvidia insider Ian Buck led with roughly 13%, followed by Huang at roughly 11%, with finance chief Colette Kress and former Apple CEO Tim Cook trailing.
By early Monday morning, Huang’s odds had risen to roughly 19%.
They then jumped to 97% when Nvidia confirmed his reinstatement.
Another contract, on whether President Donald Trump would publicly call for Huang’s reinstatement, drew more than $330,000 in volume.
Bettors gave it a 38% chance of happening before January 2027 and a 20% chance before December 2026.
Trump made such a post on Truth Social on Sunday night, and the contract was resolved.
The odds for the January window jumped to 83% and those for the December window to 74%.
Because the call came before December, both contracts paid out on “yes.”
A third option, that Huang would return, was trading at about 16% before the news broke.
But the Nvidia outcome, where the platforms’ odds diverged significantly from reality, has weakened that case.

At 5 a.m., traders gave an external hire roughly 57% odds and an internal one roughly 33%. A third option, that Huang would return, was trading at about 16% before the news broke. Traders then piled in, and it jumped to nearly 100% within minutes. Trump made such a post on Truth Social on Sunday night, and the contract was resolved. The odds for the January window jumped to 83% and those for the December window to 74%. Because the call came before December, both contracts paid out on “yes.” Polymarket saw even heavier trading. A contract on who would be Nvidia’s next CEO topped $11 million in volume. As of Sunday evening, Nvidia insider Ian Buck led with roughly 13%, followed by Huang at roughly 11%, with finance chief Colette Kress and former Apple CEO Tim Cook trailing. By early Monday morning, Huang’s odds had risen to roughly 19%. They then jumped to 97% when Nvidia confirmed his reinstatement. The misses come as prediction markets face growing attention over how well they forecast events, even as their popularity climbs. The platforms pitch themselves as a reference point for future events. Their case grew stronger after the 2024 election, when they called Trump’s return to the White House more accurately than traditional polls and surveys. Their most recent redemption came in this month’s midterms , when Kalshi and Polymarket correctly forecasted that Democrats would take control of both chambers of Congress. The platforms also called most House and Senate races correctly. But the Nvidia outcome, where the platforms’ odds diverged significantly from reality, has weakened that case. It wasn’t the first time they got an outcome wrong. During the midterms, prediction markets failed to foresee surprise victories like Democrat Annie Andrews’s win over Republican incumbent Darline Graham in South Carolina’s Senate race, and Democrat Gina Hinojosa’s win over Republican incumbent Greg Abbott in the Texas governor’s race. Before that, the markets also favored Flávio Bolsonaro over incumbent Lula da Silva in Brazil’s presidential runoff, where Lula eventually won.

The company’s board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive and a director after receiving input from senior US government officials that left directors confident his return posed no national security risk. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” board chairman Harvey Jones said in a statement. “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said, adding: “I can’t wait to get back to work.” Nvidia said its independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation would continue despite his reinstatement. Nvidia’s stunning reversal came without consulting the company’s senior executives, who learned of the decision to reinstate Huang only at the last minute, Bloomberg reported Monday , citing people familiar with the matter. The board reached its decision Sunday afternoon following pressure from President Trump, according to the report. Interim CEO Colette Kress and other top executives were excluded from the discussions, which unfolded over just a few hours. Complicating the search for Huang’s replacement, some prospective candidates had already withdrawn themselves from consideration, Bloomberg reported. Nvidia announced Huang’s comeback shortly before markets opened Monday, upending preparations for the company’s annual developer conference in Washington next week. The event, which executives had been planning without their longtime boss, is now expected to showcase his return. US intelligence agencies determined that Alice Huang, who is no relation to the billionaire executive, maintained contact with an official from China’s Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 until fall 2026, a period that overlapped with their affair, the report said. American intelligence also uncovered evidence that her business partner, Kang Wei , whom she reportedly introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency, raising suspicions that Jensen Huang had been targeted in an espionage operation. The pair have also come under scrutiny over their alleged involvement in a network of Southeast Asian companies, including Singapore-based Megaspeed , suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of US export restrictions. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing, while Beijing has dismissed the espionage allegations as unfounded. Trump was briefed about Alice Huang’s suspected intelligence ties as early as June 2025, according to the report, but has publicly questioned whether she was a spy. The president repeatedly urged Nvidia to bring Jensen Huang back , arguing that the company and the American economy needed his leadership. The scandal deepened after revelations that Huang had also been romantically involved with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reportedly answered directly to him, according to the Times. The pair were spotted behaving affectionately during Nvidia’s annual developer conference in San Jose in March, the newspaper reported. Axios separately reported that Huang’s security team allegedly offered a nondisclosure agreement to a bystander who recorded an interaction between the two. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” board chairman Harvey Jones said in a statement.

“The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the US government had no reason to believe Huang’s return posed a national security threat.

“The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct,” Trump added, while urging Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with US export controls.

The board reached its decision Sunday afternoon following pressure from President Trump, according to the report. Interim CEO Colette Kress and other top executives were excluded from the discussions, which unfolded over just a few hours.
Complicating the search for Huang’s replacement, some prospective candidates had already withdrawn themselves from consideration, Bloomberg reported.

However, after The New York Times reported there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, a board meeting that night ended with Huang’s resignation, and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was installed as the new interim CEO.

Bringing Huang back before that investigation ends reads as a message to shareholders that the board decided it would not wait for the final report, and it leaves the question that cost him the job 12 days ago still open.
The limit of that reading is the board’s own account: it voted unanimously, it said it was “satisfied with respect to Mr.

sources.title: Prediction markets put Jensen Huang’s odds of returning at 11% on Sunday night—hours later he was back as Nvidia CEO - Fortune
passages: Prediction markets have proved prescient when it comes to forecasting elections and other events, but in the case of Jensen Huang’s abrupt return as Nvidia’s CEO, they appeared as much in the dark as everyone else.
A look at contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket tied to the company’s next CEO reveals an abrupt swing from long shots to near certainties when the board reinstated him Monday morning.
As of Sunday evening, Nvidia insider Ian Buck led with roughly 13%, followed by Huang at roughly 11%, with finance chief Colette Kress and former Apple CEO Tim Cook trailing.
By early Monday morning, Huang’s odds had risen to roughly 19%.
They then jumped to 97% when Nvidia confirmed his reinstatement.
Another contract, on whether President Donald Trump would publicly call for Huang’s reinstatement, drew more than $330,000 in volume.
Bettors gave it a 38% chance of happening before January 2027 and a 20% chance before December 2026.
Trump made such a post on Truth Social on Sunday night, and the contract was resolved.
The odds for the January window jumped to 83% and those for the December window to 74%.
Because the call came before December, both contracts paid out on “yes.”
A third option, that Huang would return, was trading at about 16% before the news broke.
But the Nvidia outcome, where the platforms’ odds diverged significantly from reality, has weakened that case.

The misses come as prediction markets face growing attention over how well they forecast events, even as their popularity climbs. The platforms pitch themselves as a reference point for future events. Their case grew stronger after the 2024 election, when they called Trump’s return to the White House more accurately than traditional polls and surveys. Their most recent redemption came in this month’s midterms , when Kalshi and Polymarket correctly forecasted that Democrats would take control of both chambers of Congress. During the midterms, prediction markets failed to foresee surprise victories like Democrat Annie Andrews’s win over Republican incumbent Darline Graham in South Carolina’s Senate race, and Democrat Gina Hinojosa’s win over Republican incumbent Greg Abbott in the Texas governor’s race. Before that, the markets also favored Flávio Bolsonaro over incumbent Lula da Silva in Brazil’s presidential runoff, where Lula eventually won.

Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday in a stunning reversal that comes less than two weeks after his shocking resignation amid a sex scandal involving a suspected Chinese spy, sending shares of the chipmaking giant soaring 34%. The company’s board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive and a director after receiving input from senior US government officials that left directors confident his return posed no national security risk. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” board chairman Harvey Jones said in a statement. “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said, adding: “I can’t wait to get back to work.” Nvidia said its independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation would continue despite his reinstatement. President Trump hailed Huang’s reinstatement Monday, declaring that Nvidia’s board had made the “correct and proper decision” and calling the billionaire executive a “Great Patriot and National Treasure.” “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the US government had no reason to believe Huang’s return posed a national security threat. “The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct,” Trump added, while urging Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with US export controls. Nvidia’s stunning reversal came without consulting the company’s senior executives, who learned of the decision to reinstate Huang only at the last minute, Bloomberg reported Monday , citing people familiar with the matter. The board reached its decision Sunday afternoon following pressure from President Trump, according to the report. Interim CEO Colette Kress and other top executives were excluded from the discussions, which unfolded over just a few hours. Complicating the search for Huang’s replacement, some prospective candidates had already withdrawn themselves from consideration, Bloomberg reported. Nvidia announced Huang’s comeback shortly before markets opened Monday, upending preparations for the company’s annual developer conference in Washington next week. The event, which executives had been planning without their longtime boss, is now expected to showcase his return. Huang’s reinstatement comes amid fresh r evelations about his affair with Alice Huang , a Chinese businesswoman who was in contact with an officer of Beijing’s top spy agency while romantically involved with the Nvidia founder, according to a New York Times report. US intelligence agencies determined that Alice Huang, who is no relation to the billionaire executive, maintained contact with an official from China’s Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 until fall 2026, a period that overlapped with their affair, the report said. American intelligence also uncovered evidence that her business partner, Kang Wei , whom she reportedly introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency, raising suspicions that Jensen Huang had been targeted in an espionage operation. The pair have also come under scrutiny over their alleged involvement in a network of Southeast Asian companies, including Singapore-based Megaspeed , suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of US export restrictions. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing, while Beijing has dismissed the espionage allegations as unfounded. Trump was briefed about Alice Huang’s suspected intelligence ties as early as June 2025, according to the report, but has publicly questioned whether she was a spy. The president repeatedly urged Nvidia to bring Jensen Huang back , arguing that the company and the American economy needed his leadership. The scandal deepened after revelations that Huang had also been romantically involved with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reportedly answered directly to him, according to the Times. The pair were spotted behaving affectionately during Nvidia’s annual developer conference in San Jose in March, the newspaper reported. Axios separately reported that Huang’s security team allegedly offered a nondisclosure agreement to a bystander who recorded an interaction between the two. Wall Street analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives said Nvidia’s board had little choice but to bring Huang back, arguing that losing the billionaire founder posed a greater threat to shareholders than the controversy surrounding his departure. “At the end of the day despite this Jensen saga the Board knew it had no choice but to bring him back,” Ives wrote in a Monday research note, citing Huang’s critical relationships with suppliers, major AI customers and technology partners. Ives said Nvidia could be worth $300 a share with Huang at the helm, compared with $225 without him, underscoring the importance investors place on his leadership of the chipmaking giant. Nevertheless, the analyst maintained his official $225 price target and “Outperform” rating, warning that the company’s internal investigation, government inquiries and unresolved questions about compliance with US export controls remain significant obstacles.

sources.title: Bitcoin Tops $63,000 as Nvidia Brings Back Jensen Huang and Tech Shares Rally - unchainedcrypto.com
passages: Bitcoin rose above $63,000 on Monday, joining a rally in Nvidia shares and U.S. tech futures after the chipmaker’s board put Jensen Huang back in charge as president and CEO, less than a week after its chair said the board had no plans to bring him back.

Lumida CEO Ram Ahluwalia had made the case for Huang’s return. “There’s no one more qualified to lead Nvidia than its founder CEO, Jensen Huang,” he said on Unchained’s Bits + Bips last week, calling it “a significant loss not to have Jensen in the leadership position.”
Chief financial officer Colette Kress took over as interim CEO.
It traded between about $62,900 and $63,600 over the next 20 minutes, while Nvidia shares were up about 27% in premarket trading and Nasdaq 100 futures were up more than 6%.

It then held near that level for the next hour. Jones , the board’s chair, said in the company’s release, adding, “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company.” Huang said in the same release that he was taking on the role “with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.” Huang stepped down on Nov. 12, days after the board opened an independent investigation into reports that he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Apple’s latest smartwatch, the 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 with Wi-Fi and GPS connectivity, has dropped to a new all-time low of $299 ($100 off) at Amazon and Walmart, beating its most sale price by $30. For example, the watch can alert you when it detects sounds like a doorbell, alarm, or even a baby’s cry, while other upcoming features like Live Rewind and Siri Recap lets you look back at a transcript of the previous 15 seconds of conversation and get a high-level overview of the conversations you had that day. The Series 12 also features redesigned health sensors that can now track your heart rate every five seconds even when you’re not exercising, which is particularly help if you have a chronic condition and need to keep a closer eye on your heart rate. It also introduces a new readiness score to help you decide how prepared your body is for the day. Other highlights include easier navigation with simple pinch gestures, and faster charging, which helps to make up for the fact that battery life is rated at up to 24 hours on a single charge, just like the previous-generation model. In our testing, the watch went from 20 to 64 percent charge in just 20 minutes, making it relatively easy to top up while showering or getting ready for the day. Start your Independent Membership today. Jensen Huang is returning to lead Nvidia after he left in the wake of a run of scandals , the company has said. Mr Huang resigned from the company he helped found on 12 November, after reports of a number of affairs, including with one woman accused of being a Chinese spy. In the time since, Donald Trump and many tech leaders called for his return and a petition supporting him gathered hundreds of thousands of signatures – leading Mr Huang to report that he would return to the company if its board asked him to. Now, Nvidia says that its board has unanimously agreed that he should return. The decision followed “a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang”, which left it satisfied with his “candour and ability to lead”, the board said. Nvidia’s announcement came after a pressure campaign from people including Donald Trump, who had said hours before the announcement that rehiring Mr Huang would be “the best thing for the company, and also, for the USA”. The two are close, and the president has repeatedly backed Mr Huang throughout the scandal. In a Truth Social post immediately after Nvidia announced the decision to reappoint Mr Huang, Trump said it was “the correct and proper decision”. “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” he wrote. “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” the post continued, citing attorney general Todd Blanche’s statements that the government “does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct”. “On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure,” Trump added. In its announcement, Nvidia’s board said it had received “input from senior levels of the United States government” that had led it to be “confident” that Mr Huang does not pose a national security risk, it said. Critics had argued that Mr Huang’s relationship with an accused Chinese spy could undermine the US’s work to keep its chips, which are central to today’s AI technology, could be acquired by China . “The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C Jones, its chair. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company.” Mr Huang said he was “honoured” to return to Nvidia. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” he said in a statement. Nvidia had previously announced that it had launched an independent investigation into accusations that Mr Huang had been successfully targeted by a “foreign intelligence effort”. That will continue to its conclusion and Mr Huang is committed to co-operate with it, Nvidia said. It has also recently formed a new committee that will oversee Nvidia’s compliance with trade rules and national security risks. Nvidia will appoint a new chief compliance officer who will oversee that work, it said, and it committed to co-operate with ongoing government investigations. Those investigations are examining a host of allegations that have dogged Nvidia for some time, and became more widely discussed in the wake of the scandal and Mr Huang’s departure. Multiple investigations of the company ​are ⁠underway, including by the US SEC and the Department of Justice , related to everything from potential accounting issues to alleged chip smuggling. After Mr Huang resigned on 12 November, Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, to run the company. But that decision was met with immediate criticism, and reports that Mr Huang did not have confidence in her as his successor. In the days that followed, pressure had mounted on Nvidia’s board to reappoint Mr Huang. Trump repeatedly backed his return, alongside other tech leaders such as Elon Musk , and a petition supporting him now has more than 200,000 signatures, including people claiming to be employees of and investors in Nvidia. Last week, five days after his departure, Mr Huang posted his first public statement on the scandal. He said that he had seen “an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO” and that he would be “honoured” to return if the board decided it was in the best interest of the company and the country. In the days that followed, Nvidia repeatedly denied that it was looking to bring him back. In its quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, for instance, Ms Kress said that it was “business as usual” and Mr Jones, the chair of its board, confirmed that Nvidia was not considering bringing back Mr Huang. But Nvidia’s share price continued to fall, and has dropped more than 20 per cent since those earnings were announced. That provoked fears that concern about Nvidia and its falling share price could undermine the investment in the US’s AI industry, which in turn could have dramatic effects on the US economy. In the wake of Mr Huang’s reinstatement, however, the company’s share price jumped back up. Nvidia’s share price was up 31 per cent in the moments after the announcement. In the time since, Donald Trump and many tech leaders called for his return and a petition supporting him gathered hundreds of thousands of signatures – leading Mr Huang to report that he would return to the company if its board asked him to.

Now, Nvidia says that its board has unanimously agreed that he should return. The decision followed “a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang”, which left it satisfied with his “candour and ability to lead”, the board said.

The two are close, and the president has repeatedly backed Mr Huang throughout the scandal.

In a Truth Social post immediately after Nvidia announced the decision to reappoint Mr Huang, Trump said it was “the correct and proper decision”. “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” he wrote.

“The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” the post continued, citing attorney general Todd Blanche’s statements that the government “does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct”.
“On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure,” Trump added.

In its announcement, Nvidia’s board said it had received “input from senior levels of the United States government” that had led it to be “confident” that Mr Huang does not pose a national security risk, it said. Critics had argued that Mr Huang’s relationship with an accused Chinese spy could undermine the US’s work to keep its chips, which are central to today’s AI technology, could be acquired by China .

“The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C Jones, its chair. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company.”
Mr Huang said he was “honoured” to return to Nvidia. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” he said in a statement.

Nvidia had previously announced that it had launched an independent investigation into accusations that Mr Huang had been successfully targeted by a “foreign intelligence effort”. That will continue to its conclusion and Mr Huang is committed to co-operate with it, Nvidia said.

It has also recently formed a new committee that will oversee Nvidia’s compliance with trade rules and national security risks. Nvidia will appoint a new chief compliance officer who will oversee that work, it said, and it committed to co-operate with ongoing government investigations.

Those investigations are examining a host of allegations that have dogged Nvidia for some time, and became more widely discussed in the wake of the scandal and Mr Huang’s departure. Multiple investigations of the company ​are ⁠underway, including by the US SEC and the Department of Justice , related to everything from potential accounting issues to alleged chip smuggling.

After Mr Huang resigned on 12 November, Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, to run the company. But that decision was met with immediate criticism, and reports that Mr Huang did not have confidence in her as his successor.

In the days that followed, pressure had mounted on Nvidia’s board to reappoint Mr Huang. Trump repeatedly backed his return, alongside other tech leaders such as Elon Musk , and a petition supporting him now has more than 200,000 signatures, including people claiming to be employees of and investors in Nvidia.

Last week, five days after his departure, Mr Huang posted his first public statement on the scandal. He said that he had seen “an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO” and that he would be “honoured” to return if the board decided it was in the best interest of the company and the country.

But Nvidia’s share price continued to fall, and has dropped more than 20 per cent since those earnings were announced. That provoked fears that concern about Nvidia and its falling share price could undermine the investment in the US’s AI industry, which in turn could have dramatic effects on the US economy.

extraction.body: President Donald Trump said Monday that he personally convinced Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, revealing his direct involvement in the chipmaker's stunning leadership reversal less than two weeks after its co-founder's resignation. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview. "And I convinced them." Trump said Nvidia's directors sought assurances about whether Huang's reinstatement posed a national security risk. "And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot," he said. The president also revealed that he spoke with Huang on Sunday night, before Nvidia announced his return. The remarks follow Semafor's reporting that Trump personally dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang's reinstatement, citing a source familiar with the discussions. White House communications director Steven Cheung told the outlet that Trump was "totally involved" in the decision, adding, "We have to protect our geniuses." Trump separately celebrated Huang's return on Truth Social , calling the decision "correct and proper" and describing the Nvidia co-founder as a "Great Patriot and National Treasure." He said Attorney General Todd Blanche had confirmed that the federal government possessed no evidence Huang engaged in unlawful conduct. The president's intervention sheds new light on Nvidia's abrupt reversal after its board declared last Tuesday that it had no intention of reinstating Huang. The company announced his return Monday, saying it had received input from senior U.S. government officials before concluding his reinstatement posed no national security risk. Its independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation remains ongoing. passages: Washington — Jensen Huang is still scheduled to testify before lawmakers next week, congressional committees confirmed, after he was reinstated as Nvidia's CEO following his resignation earlier this month.After Huang stepped down less than two weeks ago, amid reports of extramarital affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy — Nvidia's board of directors said Monday that it had reinstated Huang as president and CEO.

Pete Ricketts of Nebraska argued that Huang's behavior "does not support reinstatement," citing his own experience serving on a public company board."Nvidia's decision today doesn't excuse Jensen Huang from testifying before Congress," Ricketts added.

Lawmakers from both parties expressed alarm Monday about Huang's reinstatement, which is taking place as the focus shifts to questions about the chipmaker's compliance with export restrictions.Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer vowed that Democrats "will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives." And Sen.

Robert Garcia of California, who is set to chair the House Oversight Committee in the new Congress, argued that President Trump's alleged involvement in Huang's reinstatement "raises serious national security and corruption questions," which he said must be investigated."No president who has invested in a private company should be involved in their board decisions," Garcia said in a statement.

Kevin Cramer of North Dakota said the "risk of extortion by a Chinese asset who's been banned by Singapore is risk enough to not rehire Huang," while urging Congress to "immediately pass the strictest export controls possible.""The legal and reputational risk of hiring a CEO who may very well be convicted in the United States or other nations of violating espionage and export control laws is now born by the board of Nvidia, but the national security risk is passed along to the United States military and its citizens," Cramer said.

Jim Himes of Connecticut, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, added, "We expect to see him on Capitol Hill next week." The Senate Banking Committee also sent out a notice Monday announcing that Huang would still appear before the panel to testify on Dec.
Just 11 days after Nvidia announced his departure, the board brought him back while its own independent investigation was still underway.
"Congress must come together in swift bipartisan action and demand answers immediately."On the GOP side, Sen.
"It also doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips.

The board's move, for which President Trump claimed some credit, sent shockwaves through the political sphere, with lawmakers on both sides of the aisle expressing concern, and threw into question whether the congressional hearings would proceed.

Jim Himes of Connecticut, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, added, "We expect to see him on Capitol Hill next week." "It also doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips. extraction.body: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday hosted his third cryptocurrency gala for top holders of his meme coin, $TRUMP, which has plummeted to below $1 a coin after reaching a high of $75 the day before Trump's second inauguration, on Jan. 19, 2025. The dinner, held at the Trump National golf club in Sterling, Virginia, comes as some Democrats say they will investigate potential conflicts of interest and accuse Trump of using the presidency to boost his personal wealth. At Sunday's dinner, Trump maintained that his support for cryptocurrencies was to boost American economic competitiveness. "I'm doing it for the United States ... If we don't do it, China's going to do it," he told attendees, The Guardian reported. The event also featured speeches from boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, "Shark Tank" investor Kevin O'Leary and NBA champion Tristan Thompson. A total of 185 "wallets" met the criteria for entry to the gala, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just 130 wallets. The wallets listed on the leaderboard held $8.6 million in $TRUMP tokens, a sharp decline from the May 2025 gala, which featured 220 attendees holding a combined $148 million. Crypto billionaire Justin Sun's wallet alone held $18.5 million at the 2025 event — more than the combined holdings of this year's attendees. Eligibility was based on time-weighted holdings of Trump's meme coins from Sept. 30 to Nov. 16, according to the organizer's website. The top 29 holders were invited to a VIP reception with the president, with the top four receiving an 18-karat, Trump-branded gold watch. More than half of the wallets that qualified for the event were linked to crypto exchanges that bar U.S.-based users, according to data gathered by consumer advocacy group Public Citizen for Reuters , suggesting they belong to foreign nationals. The $TRUMP token has earned the Trump family at least $635 million, according to the president's June financial disclosure. Including the meme coins, the Trump family has earned $2.3 billion from its four main crypto-related businesses since the president's second term began, through to April of this year, according to a Reuters report. This is despite the ventures' falling value, which, according to the report, they invest little to no money in. Trump's stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group , is worth about $430 million as of Friday's close. Bitcoin climbed back to over $61,000 on Monday in line with the U.S. stock futures bounce , after an AI-related stock sell-off spilled over into other riskier assets last week. Bitcoin fell as low as $55,130 on Saturday, its lowest level since September 2024. The sell-off wiped out $1.8 billion in leveraged crypto positions, largely from bets on prices rising. Leveraged buyers were forced out as prices fell, then returned after the price stabilized. The world's largest cryptocurrency is still trading at less than half of its October 2025 value. extraction.body: Concerns over presidential financial interests intensified after Donald Trump hosted a private cryptocurrency dinner Sunday, November 22, 2026, at Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia. The gathering brought together major holders of his $TRUMP meme coin as its market value dropped below $1, attracting scrutiny over foreign investors and access to the US president.According to CNBC, the token previously reached more than $75 on January 19, 2025, one day before Trump's second inauguration. Its dramatic decline contrasts with the financial benefits the cryptocurrency venture has generated for the president's family.The event was the third gala organized for major $TRUMP token holders. CNBC reported that 185 cryptocurrency wallets qualified for admission, although the official leaderboard displayed only 130 wallets holding a combined $8.6 million in tokens.That figure represents a substantial decline from the May 2025 dinner, when 220 attendees collectively held $148 million in $TRUMP cryptocurrency. The organizer calculated eligibility using time-weighted token holdings between September 30 and November 16, 2026.The top 29 holders received invitations to a VIP reception, while the four highest-ranked participants qualified for 18-karat Trump-branded gold watches. Other VIP guests received Trump-branded watches and Trump Victory perfume, according to CBS News.During his address, Trump defended his cryptocurrency agenda by connecting digital assets with American economic competitiveness and technological leadership."We have to remain number one in everything we do. If we are not going to do it, China is going to do it," Trump told attendees, according to CBS News.He also discussed artificial intelligence, semiconductor technology and the importance of maintaining oversight of the rapidly expanding industry."There should be some checks and balances," Trump said about the AI industry.His remarks included comments about prominent technology executives. Trump expressed support for Jensen Huang returning to Nvidia's leadership and described Elon Musk as an unusually talented individual. He also praised Anthropic's chief executive.Beyond the public remarks, the composition of the guest list raised questions about international participation. A CBS News investigation found that more than half of the wallets associated with qualifying attendees used cryptocurrency exchanges that prohibit US customers.Reuters separately reported that data collected by consumer advocacy organization Public Citizen indicated a similar concentration of wallets connected to exchanges serving customers outside the United States.One attendee identified as Addy, who leads Singapore-linked company FastX, described her organization's cryptocurrency holdings before the gathering."We are the number one Trump holder now. We have over 2 million tokens," Addy said in a video published on X before the event.She also described the planned VIP appearance as an important occasion for the company and its community."So later this month our team will attend a VIP reception with President Trump. So it's a big moment for us and the FastX community," she said.CBS News traced FastX's promotional video to an office building in Singapore but found neither Addy nor other company representatives there. The company did not respond to requests for comment.Corey Frayer, an investor protection specialist at the Consumer Federation of America, questioned whether the arrangement adequately separated presidential responsibilities from private financial interests."He's not making choices about public policy and what's in the best interest of the United States. He's making choices about what is most profitable to him," Frayer told CBS News.Trump previously addressed concerns about his family's cryptocurrency activities during an interview with 60 Minutes. He said his sons manage the businesses through a trust while he concentrates on presidential responsibilities."My sons run the company. It's hard to say to them, 'Don't do anything anymore for four years because I'm president,'" Trump said.According to his June financial disclosure, the $TRUMP token issuer had generated at least $635 million for the Trump family. A Reuters report cited by CNBC estimated that the family's four principal cryptocurrency-related businesses generated $2.3 billion between the beginning of Trump's second term and April 2026.Meanwhile, cryptocurrency markets experienced significant volatility. Bitcoin recovered above $61,000 on Monday, November 23, after falling to approximately $55,130 on Saturday, its weakest level since September 2024.CNBC reported that the decline eliminated $1.8 billion in leveraged cryptocurrency positions. US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds also recorded $1.24 billion in withdrawals during the previous week, marking their third consecutive week of outflows.The White House, FastX and Fight Fight Fight LLC, the company organizing the gala, did not respond to CBS News requests for comment. The event's website stated that attendees would not receive private meet-and-greet sessions with Trump.

extraction.body: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday hosted his third cryptocurrency gala for top holders of his meme coin, $TRUMP, which has plummeted to below $1 a coin after reaching a high of $75 the day before Trump's second inauguration, on Jan. 19, 2025. The dinner, held at the Trump National golf club in Sterling, Virginia, comes as some Democrats say they will investigate potential conflicts of interest and accuse Trump of using the presidency to boost his personal wealth. At Sunday's dinner, Trump maintained that his support for cryptocurrencies was to boost American economic competitiveness. "I'm doing it for the United States ... If we don't do it, China's going to do it," he told attendees, The Guardian reported. The event also featured speeches from boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, "Shark Tank" investor Kevin O'Leary and NBA champion Tristan Thompson. A total of 185 "wallets" met the criteria for entry to the gala, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just 130 wallets. The wallets listed on the leaderboard held $8.6 million in $TRUMP tokens, a sharp decline from the May 2025 gala, which featured 220 attendees holding a combined $148 million. Crypto billionaire Justin Sun's wallet alone held $18.5 million at the 2025 event — more than the combined holdings of this year's attendees. Eligibility was based on time-weighted holdings of Trump's meme coins from Sept. 30 to Nov. 16, according to the organizer's website. The top 29 holders were invited to a VIP reception with the president, with the top four receiving an 18-karat, Trump-branded gold watch. More than half of the wallets that qualified for the event were linked to crypto exchanges that bar U.S.-based users, according to data gathered by consumer advocacy group Public Citizen for Reuters , suggesting they belong to foreign nationals. The $TRUMP token has earned the Trump family at least $635 million, according to the president's June financial disclosure. Including the meme coins, the Trump family has earned $2.3 billion from its four main crypto-related businesses since the president's second term began, through to April of this year, according to a Reuters report. This is despite the ventures' falling value, which, according to the report, they invest little to no money in. Trump's stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group , is worth about $430 million as of Friday's close. Bitcoin climbed back to over $61,000 on Monday in line with the U.S. stock futures bounce , after an AI-related stock sell-off spilled over into other riskier assets last week. Bitcoin fell as low as $55,130 on Saturday, its lowest level since September 2024. The sell-off wiped out $1.8 billion in leveraged crypto positions, largely from bets on prices rising. Leveraged buyers were forced out as prices fell, then returned after the price stabilized. The world's largest cryptocurrency is still trading at less than half of its October 2025 value. President Donald Trump said Monday that he personally convinced Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, revealing his direct involvement in the chipmaker’s stunning leadership reversal less than two weeks after its co-founder’s resignation.
“I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC’s Eamon Javers in a phone interview. “And I convinced them.”

Trump said Nvidia’s directors sought assurances about whether Huang’s reinstatement posed a national security risk. “And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot,” he said. The president also revealed that he spoke with Huang on Sunday night, before Nvidia announced his return.

The remarks follow Semafor’s reporting that Trump personally dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang’s reinstatement, citing a source familiar with the discussions. White House communications director Steven Cheung told the outlet that Trump was “totally involved” in the decision, adding, “We have to protect our geniuses.”

Trump separately celebrated Huang’s return on Truth Social , calling the decision “correct and proper” and describing the Nvidia co-founder as a “Great Patriot and National Treasure.” He said Attorney General Todd Blanche had confirmed that the federal government possessed no evidence Huang engaged in unlawful conduct.

The president’s intervention sheds new light on Nvidia’s abrupt reversal after its board declared last Tuesday that it had no intention of reinstating Huang. The company announced his return Monday, saying it had received input from senior U.S. government officials before concluding his reinstatement posed no national security risk. Its independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation remains ongoing.

extraction.body: The president tells CNBC he provided national security assurances to directors, saying he spoke with the board “directly and indirectly” President Donald Trump said Monday that he personally convinced Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, revealing his direct involvement in the chipmaker’s stunning leadership reversal less than two weeks after its co-founder’s resignation. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC’s Eamon Javers in a phone interview. “And I convinced them.” Trump said Nvidia’s directors sought assurances about whether Huang’s reinstatement posed a national security risk. “And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot,” he said. The president also revealed that he spoke with Huang on Sunday night, before Nvidia announced his return. The remarks follow Semafor’s reporting that Trump personally dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang’s reinstatement, citing a source familiar with the discussions. White House communications director Steven Cheung told the outlet that Trump was “totally involved” in the decision, adding, “We have to protect our geniuses.” Trump separately celebrated Huang’s return on Truth Social , calling the decision “correct and proper” and describing the Nvidia co-founder as a “Great Patriot and National Treasure.” He said Attorney General Todd Blanche had confirmed that the federal government possessed no evidence Huang engaged in unlawful conduct. The president’s intervention sheds new light on Nvidia’s abrupt reversal after its board declared last Tuesday that it had no intention of reinstating Huang. The company announced his return Monday, saying it had received input from senior U.S. government officials before concluding his reinstatement posed no national security risk. extraction.body: Returning Jensen Huang to Nvidia's top job was hailed in Silicon Valley as essential to the future of the AI trade, and on Monday his supporters got their wish. But the embattled CEO's road back to the job may prove easier than the one awaiting him in Washington. Huang's reinstatement comes less than two weeks after revelations of his relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative forced his resignation, setting off a political firestorm over Nvidia's dealings with China and its influence within the Trump administration. Now back atop the company he co-founded more than three decades ago, Huang faces a growing list of congressional inquiries, federal and state scrutiny, and lawmakers on both sides of the aisle demanding answers about whether his relationship compromised US national security. "All the questions that people have been raising in the press and in social media, all those questions are still out there," Martijn Rasser, vice president of technology leadership at the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP), told Yahoo Finance. "That aspect of the story is still very much in play," said Rasser, a former officer at the Central Intelligence Agency and former director of the technology and national security program at the Center for a New American Security. Nvidia's board of directors said on Monday that the decision to reinstate Huang came after they "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk." President Trump, who had pushed for Huang's reinstatement since his ouster on Nov. 12, confirmed that he had called the company's board of directors to personally lobby for Huang, telling CNBC that he had been speaking to the board "directly and indirectly" and had offered assurances on national security. The president noted in a Truth Social post that the US government "has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," and that "the Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." Lawmakers, including prominent members from the president's own party, have disputed those assertions. Republican Sen. John Cornyn, who sits on the Senate Foreign Affairs Committee and the Select Committee on Intelligence, wrote shortly after the news broke Monday, "No national security risk? Based on what?" Republican Representatives Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter last week requesting Huang's testimony before their respective House committees, saying that "recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information." Democrats made similar calls on Monday, following on prior statements condemning potential national security violations at Nvidia ( NVDA ). "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and NVIDIA still owe Congress answers," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, wrote on Monday . "Huang's return only increases the urgency to pass bipartisan export control bills and make sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk." In a similar tone to Cornyn, Delaware Democratic Sen. Chris Coons wrote on X , "No national security risk? The guy who was having an affair with a Chinese spy while working relentlessly to help China get access to as many AI chips as possible? Really?" Calls for change at Nvidia came from inside the White House as well, despite the president's statements. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News last week that Nvidia's board needed to "go outside the company" as it searched for a new leader, arguing that the company needed a "dramatic shake-up." Bessent, however, softened his tone in interviews on Sunday. Republicans have also pushed on wider questions surrounding the US government's involvement with Nvidia, including coming congressional interrogations of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whom Huang has called "the person I talk to most in the administration." "If Howard Lutnick wanted my support, perhaps he should have responded to my many letters warning about these Chinese communist front companies and, more importantly, taking the threats of communist China more seriously," Arkansas Sen. Tom Cotton said in an interview with the Wall Street Journal. Nvidia has said in multiple quarterly reports that it projects no compute revenue from China in forward-looking estimates, stating in its fiscal second quarter report, "Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for wide distribution in China's data center market with the approval from both the USG and the Chinese government." Huang's first major test will come next week on Dec. 1, when he is scheduled to appear before three House committees investigating his ties to the suspected Chinese operative, Alice Huang, and the potential diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to China. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is also set to face questioning alongside senior Commerce Department officials responsible for enforcing restrictions on chip exports. An inquiry by the Commerce Department into Singapore-based Megaspeed — the company Alice Huang was once associated with — over alleged violations of US semiconductor export controls was transferred to the Justice Department after Teter asked the Commerce Department for information on the investigation, The New York Times reported." Huang has separately agreed to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3, setting up an appearance alongside Lutnick, who has also agreed to testify and is facing scrutiny over reports he slowed investigations into companies suspected of funneling controlled semiconductors into China. Amid a feud with Lutnick that has spilled into public light over the past two weeks, Bessent said investigators would need to ask about any potential export control violations by Nvidia or its customers such as Megaspeed, were they "a low-level fail, was it in the middle, or was it up in the C-suite? Who knew?" The controversy has also drawn investigators beyond Capitol Hill. California's attorney general has subpoenaed Nvidia as part of an investigation connected to Huang's affair. The Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating Nvidia over accounting violations , per Reuters. Proposed national legislation could also present further complications for Nvidia's business. The so-called AI Overwatch Act would tighten export controls on shipments of advanced dual-use AI chips to foreign nations such as China, while the Chip Security Act would impose new verification measures on the locations of chips exported abroad. The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act would impose more restrictive export controls on the equipment needed to make advanced AI chips. "I think the news of the past few weeks has underscored in the mind of many legislators on Capitol Hill that not enough is being done to ensure that critical US technologies stay out of the hands of our adversaries," SCSP's Rasser told Yahoo Finance. As Huang prepares to appear before Congress, he will have an important ally in Trump, who has repeatedly referred to Huang as a close associate. The president said on Monday that he personally weighed in on the Nvidia board's decision to reinstate Huang and believes his intervention was "very important" to the decision, telling CNBC, "I convinced them." "If I thought he did something wrong, I wouldn't be recommending to his board to hire him," Trump said. Follow Jake Conley on X @byjakeconley or email him at jake.conley@yahooinc.com .

This article is an automated aggregation of coverage from news outlets. Our editorials offer in-depth analysis curated by the NewsCord team.

Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid extramarital relations, including with a Chinese-linked suspect. The affair fallout prompts scrutiny of President Trump’s links to Nvidia and U.S.-China chip exports.

Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia has triggered a political fight over how closely he worked with President Donald Trump and how much access the United States should allow for advanced artificial intelligence chips to reach China. Huang “met with Trump on multiple occasions, traveled with him to the United Kingdom, and in May accompanied him on Air Force One during his visit to China,” placing his role at the center of Washington’s export-control debate. Washington’s export restrictions since 2022 have been described as difficult to enforce because customers can buy chips in countries like Singapore and Malaysia and then ship them to China.
Aşiatic cloud providers use third-party routes to preserve Nvidia access

The Washington Post framed the controversy as a “shadow war for Trump’s ear on China,” describing how Huang “secured his blessing to sell artificial intelligence chips to China” and fueled backlash among “national security hawks.” The dispute has expanded from chip sales to questions about what the U.S. government knew and what it did, after the BBC reported allegations that a supposed romantic relationship involved “Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company.”
U.S. intelligence suspicions have focused on Alice Huang, and the BBC reported that “U.S. intelligence suspects Alice Huang has ties to Chinese intelligence,” while Beijing rejects the allegations.
Nvidia’s board has denied any compromise, and the BBC said “there is no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised.”

The BBC described the export-control responsibility of U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick and said his department was “pressured to act on concerns about Megaspeed, a Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China.”
Lutnick “received a highly classified memorandum” and “resisted taking action against the company,” a decision now under scrutiny.
The Washington Post said Rubio’s intervention “helped topple” a corporate voice on China, and it tied that shift to momentum for “tougher restrictions” on advanced technology reaching Beijing.

House members from both parties have demanded answers about how the Commerce Department evaluated Chinese companies allowed to buy AI chips, and the BBC said Democrats launched an inquiry into that evaluation. The BBC reported that Republicans also questioned the government’s approach and that pressure is mounting politically as House members demand explanations. Jensen Huang’s team told Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he “plans to cooperate with their request to testify in a closed session,” keeping the dispute focused on what was known inside government.

A continuing gap in export controls has been described, with Senator Elizabeth Warren saying Huang’s resignation does not absolve him and urging Lutnick to explain why there are still gaps in export controls. The Washington Post linked the controversy to the administration’s China policy direction, describing how Huang’s access and “blessing” for chip sales to China became a flashpoint for officials pushing to keep powerful technology out of Beijing’s hands.

extraction.body: Returning Jensen Huang to Nvidia's top job was hailed in Silicon Valley as essential to the future of the AI trade, and on Monday his supporters got their wish. But the embattled CEO's road back to the job may prove easier than the one awaiting him in Washington. Huang's reinstatement comes less than two weeks after revelations of his relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative forced his resignation, setting off a political firestorm over Nvidia's dealings with China and its influence within the Trump administration. Now back atop the company he co-founded more than three decades ago, Huang faces a growing list of congressional inquiries, federal and state scrutiny, and lawmakers on both sides of the aisle demanding answers about whether his relationship compromised US national security. "All the questions that people have been raising in the press and in social media, all those questions are still out there," Martijn Rasser, vice president of technology leadership at the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP), told Yahoo Finance. "That aspect of the story is still very much in play," said Rasser, a former officer at the Central Intelligence Agency and former director of the technology and national security program at the Center for a New American Security. Nvidia's board of directors said on Monday that the decision to reinstate Huang came after they "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk." President Trump, who had pushed for Huang's reinstatement since his ouster on Nov. 12, confirmed that he had called the company's board of directors to personally lobby for Huang, telling CNBC that he had been speaking to the board "directly and indirectly" and had offered assurances on national security. The president noted in a Truth Social post that the US government "has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," and that "the Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." Lawmakers, including prominent members from the president's own party, have disputed those assertions. Republican Sen. John Cornyn, who sits on the Senate Foreign Affairs Committee and the Select Committee on Intelligence, wrote shortly after the news broke Monday, "No national security risk? Based on what?" Republican Representatives Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter last week requesting Huang's testimony before their respective House committees, saying that "recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information." Democrats made similar calls on Monday, following on prior statements condemning potential national security violations at Nvidia ( NVDA ). "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and NVIDIA still owe Congress answers," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, wrote on Monday . "Huang's return only increases the urgency to pass bipartisan export control bills and make sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk." In a similar tone to Cornyn, Delaware Democratic Sen. Chris Coons wrote on X , "No national security risk? The guy who was having an affair with a Chinese spy while working relentlessly to help China get access to as many AI chips as possible? Really?" Calls for change at Nvidia came from inside the White House as well, despite the president's statements. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News last week that Nvidia's board needed to "go outside the company" as it searched for a new leader, arguing that the company needed a "dramatic shake-up." Bessent, however, softened his tone in interviews on Sunday. Republicans have also pushed on wider questions surrounding the US government's involvement with Nvidia, including coming congressional interrogations of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whom Huang has called "the person I talk to most in the administration." "If Howard Lutnick wanted my support, perhaps he should have responded to my many letters warning about these Chinese communist front companies and, more importantly, taking the threats of communist China more seriously," Arkansas Sen. Tom Cotton said in an interview with the Wall Street Journal. Nvidia has said in multiple quarterly reports that it projects no compute revenue from China in forward-looking estimates, stating in its fiscal second quarter report, "Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for wide distribution in China's data center market with the approval from both the USG and the Chinese government." Huang's first major test will come next week on Dec. 1, when he is scheduled to appear before three House committees investigating his ties to the suspected Chinese operative, Alice Huang, and the potential diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to China. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is also set to face questioning alongside senior Commerce Department officials responsible for enforcing restrictions on chip exports. An inquiry by the Commerce Department into Singapore-based Megaspeed — the company Alice Huang was once associated with — over alleged violations of US semiconductor export controls was transferred to the Justice Department after Teter asked the Commerce Department for information on the investigation, The New York Times reported." Huang has separately agreed to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3, setting up an appearance alongside Lutnick, who has also agreed to testify and is facing scrutiny over reports he slowed investigations into companies suspected of funneling controlled semiconductors into China. Amid a feud with Lutnick that has spilled into public light over the past two weeks, Bessent said investigators would need to ask about any potential export control violations by Nvidia or its customers such as Megaspeed, were they "a low-level fail, was it in the middle, or was it up in the C-suite? Who knew?" The controversy has also drawn investigators beyond Capitol Hill. California's attorney general has subpoenaed Nvidia as part of an investigation connected to Huang's affair. The Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating Nvidia over accounting violations , per Reuters. Proposed national legislation could also present further complications for Nvidia's business. The so-called AI Overwatch Act would tighten export controls on shipments of advanced dual-use AI chips to foreign nations such as China, while the Chip Security Act would impose new verification measures on the locations of chips exported abroad. The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act would impose more restrictive export controls on the equipment needed to make advanced AI chips. "I think the news of the past few weeks has underscored in the mind of many legislators on Capitol Hill that not enough is being done to ensure that critical US technologies stay out of the hands of our adversaries," SCSP's Rasser told Yahoo Finance. As Huang prepares to appear before Congress, he will have an important ally in Trump, who has repeatedly referred to Huang as a close associate. The president said on Monday that he personally weighed in on the Nvidia board's decision to reinstate Huang and believes his intervention was "very important" to the decision, telling CNBC, "I convinced them." "If I thought he did something wrong, I wouldn't be recommending to his board to hire him," Trump said. Follow Jake Conley on X @byjakeconley or email him at jake.conley@yahooinc.com .

Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia has triggered a political fight over how closely he worked with President Donald Trump and how much access the United States should allow for advanced artificial intelligence chips to reach China. Huang “met with Trump on multiple occasions, traveled with him to the United Kingdom, and in May accompanied him on Air Force One during his visit to China,” placing his role at the center of Washington’s export-control debate. Washington’s export restrictions since 2022 have been described as difficult to enforce because customers can buy chips in countries like Singapore and Malaysia and then ship them to China.
Aşiatic cloud providers use third-party routes to preserve Nvidia access

The Washington Post framed the controversy as a “shadow war for Trump’s ear on China,” describing how Huang “secured his blessing to sell artificial intelligence chips to China” and fueled backlash among “national security hawks.” The dispute has expanded from chip sales to questions about what the U.S. government knew and what it did, after the BBC reported allegations that a supposed romantic relationship involved “Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company.”
U.S. intelligence suspicions have focused on Alice Huang, and the BBC reported that “U.S. intelligence suspects Alice Huang has ties to Chinese intelligence,” while Beijing rejects the allegations.
Nvidia’s board has denied any compromise, and the BBC said “there is no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised.”

The BBC described the export-control responsibility of U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick and said his department was “pressured to act on concerns about Megaspeed, a Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China.”
Lutnick “received a highly classified memorandum” and “resisted taking action against the company,” a decision now under scrutiny.
The Washington Post said Rubio’s intervention “helped topple” a corporate voice on China, and it tied that shift to momentum for “tougher restrictions” on advanced technology reaching Beijing.

House members from both parties have demanded answers about how the Commerce Department evaluated Chinese companies allowed to buy AI chips, and the BBC said Democrats launched an inquiry into that evaluation. The BBC reported that Republicans also questioned the government’s approach and that pressure is mounting politically as House members demand explanations. Jensen Huang’s team told Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he “plans to cooperate with their request to testify in a closed session,” keeping the dispute focused on what was known inside government.

A continuing gap in export controls has been described, with Senator Elizabeth Warren saying Huang’s resignation does not absolve him and urging Lutnick to explain why there are still gaps in export controls. The Washington Post linked the controversy to the administration’s China policy direction, describing how Huang’s access and “blessing” for chip sales to China became a flashpoint for officials pushing to keep powerful technology out of Beijing’s hands.

extraction.body: After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.” “You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate. It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director. “There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC. Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air. Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility. Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.” But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration. The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation. The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added. Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the Nvidia CEO — worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. But on Sunday evening, Trump still argued for Huang’s return and managed to continue flipping Nvidia’s board in his favor after a weekend’s worth of efforts. If the board maintained any hang-ups about bringing Huang back as CEO, Trump’s power over the executive branch — and the pressure he could exert with it — might have offered a compelling counterargument. The Securities and Exchange Commission had previously opened an investigation into whether Nvidia “misled investors,” according to The Wall Street Journal. But in a post on Truth Social Monday, Trump said that the attorney general “has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” Reached for comment, the DOJ did not provide an on-the-record response in line with The Verge’s editorial policy. Key Democrats have indicated that both Nvidia and the Trump administration will be under fire when the new Congress is sworn in — and momentum has built behind GPU export controls, which Huang lobbied extensively to loosen. “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.” Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said in a post on X, adding they’d work “on a bipartisan basis to continue advancing policies that stop the flow of our most powerful technology to the Chinese military and other adversaries.” Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) called the board’s decision “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible” and pledged to investigate “business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce.” He called for “traditional Republicans” to join in the effort.
