extraction.body: US President Donald Trump has publicly backed Jensen Huang's reported bid to return to Nvidia's top leadership, even as allegations involving a woman linked to the former CEO and a suspected Chinese espionage network bring the company under increased scrutiny. In a post on Truth Social, Trump urged Nvidia's board to reconsider Huang's position, saying his return would benefit both the company and the United States. “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A,” Trump said. The endorsement comes amid a report by *The New York Times* alleging that Alice Huang, described as a suspected Chinese spy, maintained contact with an official from China's Ministry of State Security for more than a year while she was reportedly involved in a secret relationship with Jensen Huang. Alleged links to China's intelligence network Citing multiple people familiar with US intelligence reports, The New York Times reported that Alice Huang was in contact with China's Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 until autumn 2026. The report also alleged that her business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, had worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. The allegations have prompted scrutiny from US authorities. Director of US National Intelligence Jay Clayton has confirmed that investigations into Alice Huang and her company, Megaspeed, are underway. In an interview with Fox News, Clayton said investigations into both the individual and the company were progressing alongside regulatory proceedings. He also said he expected Nvidia's board to examine the matter. “There is an investigation into her company, and there is an investigation into her. That is going to play out,” Clayton said, adding that the American public would receive answers as the process moves forward. Nvidia board faces pressure over leadership decision Trump's public support comes at a time when Nvidia's leadership and the company's board are facing questions over the reported developments. Huang is expected to testify before three House committees on December 1, adding to the scrutiny surrounding the matter. However, the Nvidia board and interim CEO Colette Kress have reportedly ruled out his reinstatement at the top of the company. With congressional attention growing and investigations continuing, Trump's endorsement may not be enough to secure Huang's return. The board's position and the outcome of the ongoing proceedings are likely to remain central to any decision on the company's leadership.

He told CNBC in a phone interview Monday about his call to the board. "I spoke to them and I convinced them," he said. "And it was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week ago." The president also claimed in a Truth Social post Monday that the U.S. government "has no reason to believe" that Huang's return to Nvidia as CEO "poses any risk to national security," although he did not elaborate. His social media comment went up shortly after Nvidia announced its board had reinstated Huang. Huang resigned less than two weeks ago over an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies suspected of spying for China. The president said Nvidia's board asked "for assurance on the national security threat" and he gave them "assurance." The president told CNBC he believes his intervention was essential to getting Huang reinstated. Trump told CNBC Huang "did nothing wrong."He also said in the interview that he spoke with Huang Sunday night "after the deal was done" and told him to "work hard."Mr. Trump said in Truth Social his post that U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." A Justice Department official told CBS News that Mr. Trump did speak to Blanche over the weekend, and the official said the has no evidence of any wrongdoing by either Jensen Huang or Nvidia.Mr. Trump has been a vocal proponent of returning Huang to the company, after Nvidia's stock tanked in the wake of his resignation. Since his reinstatement was announced Monday morning, the stock has surged over 30%.Huang has built Nvidia into one of the world's most valuable companies, with its high-powered chips emerging as integral to the race for AI dominance between the U.S. and China. A White House official told CBS News on Monday that the decision to reinstate Huang "will preserve America's technological edge over China, strengthen our national security" and ensure the future of AI will be built in the U.S. "The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO," Mr. "The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.""On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," he continued. "Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security."Huang had publicly advocated for his return to Nvidia, along with others in the tech industry, including SpaceX's Elon Musk. Trump has said he was not told that Alice Huang was suspected of being a spy, although The New York Times reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio circulated a highly classified memo in May about the counterintelligence risk posed by Jensen Huang's affair. Jensen Huang has agreed to publicly testify before Congress, although the date has not been set, a Senate Banking spokesperson told CBS News last week. Republicans and Democrats are applying increasing pressure to make Huang testify about Nvidia chips making their way into Chinese hands. On Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was asked if the president understood the national security and regulatory risks Nvidia and Huang face, after Bessent had said Nvidia's board of directors needed "to go to the outside" to find a new CEO."Well, Jensen is on the outside now, so you know," Bessent said. "I know the president said he should come back," "Face the Nation" moderator Margaret Brennan said. Bessent then said of Jensen Huang, "Well, I said they should go to the outside, but he's on the outside now."

coreStoryFacts.text: “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.” Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said in a post on X, adding they’d work “on a bipartisan basis to continue advancing policies that stop the flow of our most powerful technology to the Chinese military and other adversaries.” Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) called the board’s decision “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible” and pledged to investigate “business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce.” He called for “traditional Republicans” to join in the effort.
Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang.

Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.” “You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate.
It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so.

News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility.
“We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.” But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence.

Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.

Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the Nvidia CEO — worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency.
In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air.
Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker.
Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return.

US President Donald Trump has publicly backed Jensen Huang's reported bid to return to Nvidia's top leadership, even as allegations involving a woman linked to the former CEO and a suspected Chinese espionage network bring the company under increased scrutiny.
“I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang.

Alleged links to China's intelligence network Citing multiple people familiar with US intelligence reports, The New York Times reported that Alice Huang was in contact with China's Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 until autumn 2026.
With congressional attention growing and investigations continuing, Trump's endorsement may not be enough to secure Huang's return.
It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A,” Trump said.
He also said he expected Nvidia's board to examine the matter.
However, the Nvidia board and interim CEO Colette Kress have reportedly ruled out his reinstatement at the top of the company.
Huang is expected to testify before three House committees on December 1, adding to the scrutiny surrounding the matter.

Donald Trump also wrote on Truth Social post (23 November 2026), praising Jensen's comeback.“The Nvidia Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.
Jensen Huang is back running Nvidia after a whirlwind few weeks that felt more like a streaming drama than corporate America.

In early November, reports surfaced that Jensen Huang had been involved in extramarital affairs.One of the women named was Alice Huang, a businesswoman and former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International.

The board brought the co-founder back as president, CEO, and director on 23 November, effective immediately.He had stepped down earlier in the month after personal affairs and security questions blew up.

extraction.body: After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.” “You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate. It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director. “There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC. Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air. Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility. Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.” But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration. The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation. The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added. Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the Nvidia CEO — worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. But on Sunday evening, Trump still argued for Huang’s return and managed to continue flipping Nvidia’s board in his favor after a weekend’s worth of efforts. If the board maintained any hang-ups about bringing Huang back as CEO, Trump’s power over the executive branch — and the pressure he could exert with it — might have offered a compelling counterargument. The Securities and Exchange Commission had previously opened an investigation into whether Nvidia “misled investors,” according to The Wall Street Journal. But in a post on Truth Social Monday, Trump said that the attorney general “has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” Reached for comment, the DOJ did not provide an on-the-record response in line with The Verge’s editorial policy. Key Democrats have indicated that both Nvidia and the Trump administration will be under fire when the new Congress is sworn in — and momentum has built behind GPU export controls, which Huang lobbied extensively to loosen. “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.” Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said in a post on X, adding they’d work “on a bipartisan basis to continue advancing policies that stop the flow of our most powerful technology to the Chinese military and other adversaries.” Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) called the board’s decision “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible” and pledged to investigate “business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce.” He called for “traditional Republicans” to join in the effort.

The allegations have prompted scrutiny from US authorities. Director of US National Intelligence Jay Clayton has confirmed that investigations into Alice Huang and her company, Megaspeed, are underway. In an interview with Fox News, Clayton said investigations into both the individual and the company were progressing alongside regulatory proceedings. He also said he expected Nvidia's board to examine the matter. “There is an investigation into her company, and there is an investigation into her. That is going to play out,” Clayton said, adding that the American public would receive answers as the process moves forward. Huang is expected to testify before three House committees on December 1, adding to the scrutiny surrounding the matter. extraction.body: Washington — President Trump says that he spoke to Nvidia's board and helped win Jensen Huang's reinstatement as the company's CEO. He told CNBC in a phone interview Monday about his call to the board. "I spoke to them and I convinced them," he said. "And it was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week ago." The president also claimed in a Truth Social post Monday that the U.S. government "has no reason to believe" that Huang's return to Nvidia as CEO "poses any risk to national security," although he did not elaborate. His social media comment went up shortly after Nvidia announced its board had reinstated Huang. Huang resigned less than two weeks ago over an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies suspected of spying for China. The president said Nvidia's board asked "for assurance on the national security threat" and he gave them "assurance." The president told CNBC he believes his intervention was essential to getting Huang reinstated. Trump told CNBC Huang "did nothing wrong."He also said in the interview that he spoke with Huang Sunday night "after the deal was done" and told him to "work hard."Mr. Trump said in Truth Social his post that U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." A Justice Department official told CBS News that Mr. Trump did speak to Blanche over the weekend, and the official said the has no evidence of any wrongdoing by either Jensen Huang or Nvidia.Mr. Trump has been a vocal proponent of returning Huang to the company, after Nvidia's stock tanked in the wake of his resignation. Since his reinstatement was announced Monday morning, the stock has surged over 30%.Huang has built Nvidia into one of the world's most valuable companies, with its high-powered chips emerging as integral to the race for AI dominance between the U.S. and China. A White House official told CBS News on Monday that the decision to reinstate Huang "will preserve America's technological edge over China, strengthen our national security" and ensure the future of AI will be built in the U.S. "The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO," Mr. "The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.""On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," he continued. "Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security."Huang had publicly advocated for his return to Nvidia, along with others in the tech industry, including SpaceX's Elon Musk. Trump has said he was not told that Alice Huang was suspected of being a spy, although The New York Times reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio circulated a highly classified memo in May about the counterintelligence risk posed by Jensen Huang's affair. Jensen Huang has agreed to publicly testify before Congress, although the date has not been set, a Senate Banking spokesperson told CBS News last week. Republicans and Democrats are applying increasing pressure to make Huang testify about Nvidia chips making their way into Chinese hands. On Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was asked if the president understood the national security and regulatory risks Nvidia and Huang face, after Bessent had said Nvidia's board of directors needed "to go to the outside" to find a new CEO."Well, Jensen is on the outside now, so you know," Bessent said. "I know the president said he should come back," "Face the Nation" moderator Margaret Brennan said. Bessent then said of Jensen Huang, "Well, I said they should go to the outside, but he's on the outside now."

extraction.body: The stunning decision by Nvidia 's board to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO was sealed by a personal promise from President Donald Trump on Sunday that Huang had not broken national security laws, three people familiar with the board's thinking told CNBC. Several other factors also set the stage for Huang's return and accelerated discussions with him over the weekend, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal deliberations close to Nvidia's board. A sharp stock price drop after his resignation and questions about the leadership of interim CEO Colette Kress also spurred the board's decision, the people said. "I convinced them," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview Monday morning , shortly after Nvidia announced Huang's return. "I made the deal," the president said. "It was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago. Trump said Nvidia's board asked for guarantees that Huang, who resigned less than two weeks ago, was not a threat to national security. "And we gave them assurances, at least with everything we know," the president said. "We believe he's fine. He's absolutely fine." Senior Trump administration officials reached out to the board overnight Friday to inform them that Huang had not violated U.S. national security laws, people familiar with the board's actions said. After the White House outreach, the board contacted Huang, who joined meetings on Saturday and Sunday to discuss his potential return, the people said. Huang's spokesman did not respond to a request for comment when asked about his contact with the board and other events leading up to his return. The Nvidia founder resigned on Nov. 12 after reports that he had an affair with an Nvidia employee and with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is suspected of being a spy for China. A report of an affair with a second Nvidia employee broke right after he quit. Nvidia's board named Kress, the company's chief financial officer, as the interim CEO while it searched for a permanent successor. But within days of Kress taking over, some employees and investors who spoke to CNBC questioned her stewardship, as many of them clamored for Huang's return. Kress' performances at an all-hands company meeting on Wednesday and on Nvidia's earnings call with analysts a day earlier were seen by some investors as uninspiring and underwhelming. As the board faced those concerns amid a stock drop of more than 25% over the past week, Huang was aggressively working the phones with major tech CEOs who wanted to see him return to Nvidia, according to sources close to Huang. In the days after he resigned, Huang spoke with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , OpenAI President Greg Brockman , and Elon Musk , CEO of SpaceX and Tesla , one of the sources said. On Nov. 17, less than a week after quitting, Huang issued a public statement saying he was open to returning as CEO. "I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," he said. "NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company," he added. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO." On the same day, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, Harvey Jones, told analysts on the company's earnings call that the board did "not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Kress, the following day, told company employees at the all-hands meeting, "Let's move forward." Nvidia's public stance against Huang returning came as members of Congress moved ahead with plans to interview him at hearings and as criticism grew over the company's business in Asia. The Department of Justice and the Commerce Department, in an unusual joint public statement on Nov. 17, said they were investigating Megaspeed for possible diversion of advanced Nvidia semiconductor chips to China in violation of U.S. export control law. "Sensitive technologies like semiconductors are among the most valuable and strategic assets of the U.S. economy," the departments said. But days later, senior Trump administration officials contacted Nvidia's board to tell them that Jensen Huang himself was not a risk, according to the sources. The Department of Commerce added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist later Monday. Trump, during his interview Monday with CNBC, was asked what Attorney General Todd Blanche had told him about potential criminal liability for Huang and the question of whether Nvidia chips had ended up in China in violation of U.S. export laws. "They did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he, himself, was exonerated," Trump said . Both Trump and Vice President JD Vance became convinced that Huang was a singular figure who is preventing closed-source model AI companies, such as Anthropic, from getting too powerful, according to a person familiar with the matter, who spoke on condition of anonymity to disclose private discussions. The person said Trump and Vance were briefed on the national security elements of the situation and saw no evidence that Huang did anything illegal or untoward in that regard. Trump believes his administration's close working relationship with Huang gives the U.S. its best opportunity to protect national security and prevent cutting-edge AI chips from reaching banned customers, according to the person. Trump said he spoke with Huang on Sunday, after Nvidia had voted unanimously to reinstate him. "I called him up, and I said: 'I ask you to do one thing, Jensen. Work hard,'" Trump said. "He knows what to do and what not to do," Trump said. "But I just said work hard because if you work hard, there's nobody that can capture what you've done. Nobody, nobody close." — CNBC's Kevin Breuninger and Kif Leswing contributed to this article.

“I think the [Nvidia] board acted really responsibly” in deciding to bring Huang back.
“And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot,” Trump said.

“I’m very, very happy that the company had the courage and the board had the courage to do the right thing, and they suffered for two weeks, and the company suffered greatly,” the president said.

Huang's affair with the suspected spy, Alice Huang, raised concerns due to her role as an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed and whether she was facilitating the diversion of Nvidia’s most advanced semiconductor chip to China.

When asked if the broad stock market selloff following Huang’s resignation was a factor in his push for the CEO’s reinstatement, Trump said, “Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term.” “The bigger impact was, you know, he’s got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about,” he added.
His affairs reportedly included one with an alleged Chinese spy and two with Nvidia employees.

extraction.body: US President Donald Trump has called on Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as its CEO. Trump's appeal adds to growing calls for Huang's return, including a petition with more than 200,000 signatures that Elon Musk has signed. Huang, who co-founded the AI chip giant in 1993, is due to answer lawmakers' questions in Congress on 1 December. "I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the company, and also, for the U.S.A.," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform on Sunday. Trump has stepped up his support over the past week for Huang's return. Last Monday, he said he "would not mind" seeing Huang reinstated. On Friday, he told reporters at the White House that he "would love to see Jensen be given a second chance". Huang resigned on 12 November after it emerged that he had two extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy. Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations and US authorities said they have not reached a conclusion. The "Stand with Jensen" petition, an open letter to Nvidia's board, had more than 206,000 signatures as of Monday morning, according to its website. More than 10,000 signatories claim to be current Nvidia employees. The letter asked the board to "bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts". It also highlighted that Nvidia and Huang have not endorsed it. "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too," Musk wrote on X on 13 November. Tobi Lütke, CEO of e-commerce platform Shopify, and Tim Sweeney, CEO of Fortnite developer Epic Games, have also signed it. Huang said on 17 November that he would be "honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO" if the board judged that best for the company, its staff, its shareholders, and America. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on 15 November that Nvidia needed "a dramatic shake-up" and a CEO from outside the company. However, in an interview with CBS on Sunday, he stated: "I said they should go to the outside, but he's on the outside now". Thus far, Nvidia's board does not plan to bring him back. Chair Harvey Jones told analysts during the company's earnings call last Tuesday that the board had "unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO". Colette Kress, Nvidia's finance chief, has taken over as interim CEO during the search for a permanent replacement. An outside law firm is currently undertaking an investigation. Nvidia's shares closed around $125.5 on Friday, representing a 48% collapse since their intraday all-time high price of roughly $243.3 on 6 October. They lost over 20% just last week, their seventh weekly decline in a row and the longest losing streak since 2008. The slide continued despite Nvidia beating earnings forecasts last Tuesday. Friday's 14% drop followed a Reuters report, citing two people briefed on the matter, that the Securities and Exchange Commission, the US markets regulator, was examining possible accounting issues at Nvidia. Huang will answer questions from three House committees behind closed doors on 1 December: Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party. The committees are looking into the possible diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese businesses. The session will be a transcribed interview and will not be open to the public. Huang's public testimony will come before the Senate Banking Committee, according to the office of its chair, Republican Senator Tim Scott. No date has been set, though Scott had originally asked for 3 December. Two Nvidia shareholders, the investment firms Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management, have asked the board to keep Huang's return open and to hold off on a permanent CEO until all the facts are known.

extraction.body: The stunning decision by Nvidia 's board to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO was sealed by a personal promise from President Donald Trump on Sunday that Huang had not broken national security laws, three people familiar with the board's thinking told CNBC. Several other factors also set the stage for Huang's return and accelerated discussions with him over the weekend, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal deliberations close to Nvidia's board. A sharp stock price drop after his resignation and questions about the leadership of interim CEO Colette Kress also spurred the board's decision, the people said. "I convinced them," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview Monday morning , shortly after Nvidia announced Huang's return. "I made the deal," the president said. "It was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago. Trump said Nvidia's board asked for guarantees that Huang, who resigned less than two weeks ago, was not a threat to national security. "And we gave them assurances, at least with everything we know," the president said. "We believe he's fine. He's absolutely fine." Senior Trump administration officials reached out to the board overnight Friday to inform them that Huang had not violated U.S. national security laws, people familiar with the board's actions said. After the White House outreach, the board contacted Huang, who joined meetings on Saturday and Sunday to discuss his potential return, the people said. Huang's spokesman did not respond to a request for comment when asked about his contact with the board and other events leading up to his return. The Nvidia founder resigned on Nov. 12 after reports that he had an affair with an Nvidia employee and with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is suspected of being a spy for China. A report of an affair with a second Nvidia employee broke right after he quit. Nvidia's board named Kress, the company's chief financial officer, as the interim CEO while it searched for a permanent successor. But within days of Kress taking over, some employees and investors who spoke to CNBC questioned her stewardship, as many of them clamored for Huang's return. Kress' performances at an all-hands company meeting on Wednesday and on Nvidia's earnings call with analysts a day earlier were seen by some investors as uninspiring and underwhelming. As the board faced those concerns amid a stock drop of more than 25% over the past week, Huang was aggressively working the phones with major tech CEOs who wanted to see him return to Nvidia, according to sources close to Huang. In the days after he resigned, Huang spoke with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , OpenAI President Greg Brockman , and Elon Musk , CEO of SpaceX and Tesla , one of the sources said. On Nov. 17, less than a week after quitting, Huang issued a public statement saying he was open to returning as CEO. "I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," he said. "NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company," he added. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO." On the same day, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, Harvey Jones, told analysts on the company's earnings call that the board did "not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Kress, the following day, told company employees at the all-hands meeting, "Let's move forward." Nvidia's public stance against Huang returning came as members of Congress moved ahead with plans to interview him at hearings and as criticism grew over the company's business in Asia. The Department of Justice and the Commerce Department, in an unusual joint public statement on Nov. 17, said they were investigating Megaspeed for possible diversion of advanced Nvidia semiconductor chips to China in violation of U.S. export control law. "Sensitive technologies like semiconductors are among the most valuable and strategic assets of the U.S. economy," the departments said. But days later, senior Trump administration officials contacted Nvidia's board to tell them that Jensen Huang himself was not a risk, according to the sources. The Department of Commerce added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist later Monday. Trump, during his interview Monday with CNBC, was asked what Attorney General Todd Blanche had told him about potential criminal liability for Huang and the question of whether Nvidia chips had ended up in China in violation of U.S. export laws. "They did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he, himself, was exonerated," Trump said . Both Trump and Vice President JD Vance became convinced that Huang was a singular figure who is preventing closed-source model AI companies, such as Anthropic, from getting too powerful, according to a person familiar with the matter, who spoke on condition of anonymity to disclose private discussions. The person said Trump and Vance were briefed on the national security elements of the situation and saw no evidence that Huang did anything illegal or untoward in that regard. Trump believes his administration's close working relationship with Huang gives the U.S. its best opportunity to protect national security and prevent cutting-edge AI chips from reaching banned customers, according to the person. Trump said he spoke with Huang on Sunday, after Nvidia had voted unanimously to reinstate him. "I called him up, and I said: 'I ask you to do one thing, Jensen. Work hard,'" Trump said. "He knows what to do and what not to do," Trump said. "But I just said work hard because if you work hard, there's nobody that can capture what you've done. Nobody, nobody close." — CNBC's Kevin Breuninger and Kif Leswing contributed to this article.

extraction.body: US President Donald Trump has called on Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as its CEO. Trump's appeal adds to growing calls for Huang's return, including a petition with more than 200,000 signatures that Elon Musk has signed. Huang, who co-founded the AI chip giant in 1993, is due to answer lawmakers' questions in Congress on 1 December. "I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the company, and also, for the U.S.A.," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform on Sunday. Trump has stepped up his support over the past week for Huang's return. Last Monday, he said he "would not mind" seeing Huang reinstated. On Friday, he told reporters at the White House that he "would love to see Jensen be given a second chance". Huang resigned on 12 November after it emerged that he had two extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy. Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations and US authorities said they have not reached a conclusion. The "Stand with Jensen" petition, an open letter to Nvidia's board, had more than 206,000 signatures as of Monday morning, according to its website. More than 10,000 signatories claim to be current Nvidia employees. The letter asked the board to "bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts". It also highlighted that Nvidia and Huang have not endorsed it. "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too," Musk wrote on X on 13 November. Tobi Lütke, CEO of e-commerce platform Shopify, and Tim Sweeney, CEO of Fortnite developer Epic Games, have also signed it. Huang said on 17 November that he would be "honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO" if the board judged that best for the company, its staff, its shareholders, and America. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on 15 November that Nvidia needed "a dramatic shake-up" and a CEO from outside the company. However, in an interview with CBS on Sunday, he stated: "I said they should go to the outside, but he's on the outside now". Thus far, Nvidia's board does not plan to bring him back. Chair Harvey Jones told analysts during the company's earnings call last Tuesday that the board had "unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO". Colette Kress, Nvidia's finance chief, has taken over as interim CEO during the search for a permanent replacement. An outside law firm is currently undertaking an investigation. Nvidia's shares closed around $125.5 on Friday, representing a 48% collapse since their intraday all-time high price of roughly $243.3 on 6 October. They lost over 20% just last week, their seventh weekly decline in a row and the longest losing streak since 2008. The slide continued despite Nvidia beating earnings forecasts last Tuesday. Friday's 14% drop followed a Reuters report, citing two people briefed on the matter, that the Securities and Exchange Commission, the US markets regulator, was examining possible accounting issues at Nvidia. Huang will answer questions from three House committees behind closed doors on 1 December: Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party. The committees are looking into the possible diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese businesses. The session will be a transcribed interview and will not be open to the public. Huang's public testimony will come before the Senate Banking Committee, according to the office of its chair, Republican Senator Tim Scott. No date has been set, though Scott had originally asked for 3 December. Two Nvidia shareholders, the investment firms Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management, have asked the board to keep Huang's return open and to hold off on a permanent CEO until all the facts are known.

passages: Amna Nawaz: Well, for a closer look now at Huang's return to Nvidia and the national security implications, I'm joined by Dmitri Alperovitch.

extraction.body: The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as president and CEO of Nvidia is turbocharging congressional oversight plans and training lawmakers’ bipartisan focus on a central question: how the Trump administration came to the conclusion that Huang’s return posed no national security risk. The move — and President Donald Trump’s involvement in it — is inflaming tensions between the president and his own party. Several Republicans had joined Democrats in planning to scrutinize Huang and chip export controls on China in the wake of the scandal. After being ousted as Nvidia’s CEO earlier this month, Huang had agreed to testify privately before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, House Intelligence Committee, and House China Select Committee next month as well as publicly before the Senate Banking Committee. Trump has said that Attorney General Todd Blanche had affirmed no national security risk from Huang’s rehiring, but the Justice Department is currently conducting ongoing investigations that could affect that question. Huang’s closed-door appearance before the House panels is currently expected to move forward as planned, people familiar with the plans said, but spokespeople for the panels did not respond to requests for comment. Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., who leads the Senate Banking Committee, announced later Monday that Huang would appear at a public hearing on Dec. 3. “I’ve served on a public company board. His behavior does not support reinstatement,” Sen. Pete Ricketts, R-Neb., said of Huang, adding that the company needs to be “answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips.” Huang’s return to the company is also likely to affect his legal representation before Congress. In its statement Monday, Nvidia’s board cited “input from senior levels of the United States government” that left them “confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Trump dialed into a board meeting to push for Huang’s return, Semafor first reported. The Hill’s plans to bring Huang to testify set up a potential collision course with the Trump administration in the final weeks of the lame-duck session, just as the GOP must reckon with its last opportunity to push through its party-line agenda. Congressional Republicans have taken a more hawkish approach to restrictions on chip exports to China in the last month, with leadership in both parties leaning towards using upcoming defense legislation to close gaps in US-China chip-export policy at the center of the Nvidia fallout. “No national security risk?” Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, wrote on X . “Based on what?” A White House official told Semafor that Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Huang “will preserve America’s technological edge over China, strengthen our national security, and ensure the future of SI continues to be built in America,” using a moniker for super intelligence, Trump’s preferred term for AI. Even if Republicans adjust their plans to grill Huang, he’s sure to face considerable scrutiny when Democrats take over control of Congress next year. So, too, will the Trump administration face Democrats’ questions about its interactions with and investigations related to Nvidia as well as its export control policy. “We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia’s own board has completed its investigation,” the top Democrat on the House China Select Committee, Rep. Ro Khanna of California, wrote on X . “Huang must testify at a full public congressional hearing, with every member of the relevant committees allowed to question him.” Democrats also want to hear more about “what ‘input’ was given and by which senior officials,” as Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., put it. Warren, who’s poised to chair the Senate Banking Committee next Congress, said the move “only increases the urgency” of passing more stringent restrictions on chip exports. Trump’s direct involvement is further fueling Democrats’ outrage. “The President is selling out our national security to keep the stock market high and probably for some f*cking donation to his ballroom,” Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., wrote on X .

passages: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton is raising four separate allegations surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s return to the company, describing the unfolding controversy as a potential national security, corruption, insider trading and market manipulation scandal.

Clinton’s reference to “Supergate” connects the controversy to Trump’s repeated promotion of artificial intelligence and what he has called “super intelligence.” Her statement raises questions about the intersection of national security investigations, presidential influence over a major technology company and the potential financial consequences of decisions involving one of the world’s most valuable AI businesses.

Her November 23 statement comes after Nvidia reversed its decision not to reinstate Huang, following public pressure from President Donald Trump and reported involvement by senior administration officials.

On November 20, Trump told reporters that he had discussed Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting in China and expressed support for giving the Nvidia executive another opportunity.
On November 22, Trump used Truth Social to directly urge Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back.

Associated Press reported that administration officials contacted Nvidia board members and pressed for Huang’s reinstatement, while the president cited the importance of Nvidia to American technological competitiveness and concerns about declining AI stock prices.
Corporate leadership decisions, government investigations and sensitive national security information can all influence the value of publicly traded companies.

The House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and other congressional committees also sought information from Huang regarding his reported interactions with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s protections against foreign espionage.
It is important to distinguish between the circumstances of Huang’s departure and a formal dismissal.
The president also addressed the national security concerns publicly after the reinstatement.

The Justice Department’s investigation and the congressional inquiries do not establish that Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence operative or that Jensen Huang knowingly participated in unlawful activity.
The following day, the board announced that Huang had been reinstated, reversing its earlier position.
Her third allegation, involving insider trading, raises a separate financial-market question.

Her November 23 statement comes after Nvidia reversed its decision not to reinstate Huang, following public pressure from President Donald Trump and reported involvement by senior administration officials. Clinton’s reference to “Supergate” connects the controversy to Trump’s repeated promotion of artificial intelligence and what he has called “super intelligence.” Her statement raises questions about the intersection of national security investigations, presidential influence over a major technology company and the potential financial consequences of decisions involving one of the world’s most valuable AI businesses. Clinton’s complete statement : Is it a national security scandal? If it’s “super intelligence,” call it Supergate. Why Jensen Huang’s return is attracting scrutiny The controversy surrounding Huang began with his departure from Nvidia on November 12, following reports of personal relationships that raised questions about potential connections to Chinese intelligence. One reported relationship involved Alice Huang, a businesswoman associated with Singapore-based Megaspeed, who has been suspected by U.S. authorities of having links to Chinese intelligence. The allegations have also intensified scrutiny of Nvidia’s business dealings and the potential diversion of advanced artificial intelligence chips to China. Huang subsequently expressed a willingness to return to the company if its board determined that doing so would serve Nvidia, its employees, shareholders and the United States. That position changed on November 23, when Nvidia announced that Huang had been restored as president and chief executive officer and returned to the company’s board. It is important to distinguish between the circumstances of Huang’s departure and a formal dismissal. His reinstatement on November 23 was subsequently confirmed in Nvidia’s regulatory filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Trump’s involvement in bringing Huang back The presidential involvement is a central part of Clinton’s corruption allegation. Trump publicly supported Huang’s return after the Nvidia board initially indicated that it would not reinstate him. On November 20, Trump told reporters that he had discussed Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting in China and expressed support for giving the Nvidia executive another opportunity. On November 22, Trump used Truth Social to directly urge Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back. The president argued that reinstating him would benefit both Nvidia and the United States. The following day, the board announced that Huang had been reinstated, reversing its earlier position. The president also addressed the national security concerns publicly after the reinstatement. Trump said the government had no reason to believe Huang’s return posed a national security risk and stated that the attorney general had confirmed the government did not possess evidence that Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. He nevertheless said Nvidia should continue its internal investigation into compliance with U.S. export controls. The involvement of Trump and Vice President JD Vance has attracted additional scrutiny because the decision involved a company central to America’s artificial intelligence infrastructure and its competition with China. Associated Press reported that administration officials contacted Nvidia board members and pressed for Huang’s reinstatement, while the president cited the importance of Nvidia to American technological competitiveness and concerns about declining AI stock prices. The national security investigation Clinton’s first allegation concerns the national security implications of the controversy. Nvidia manufactures advanced processors used in artificial intelligence systems, data centers and other strategically important technologies. U.S. export restrictions are designed to prevent sensitive American technology from reaching foreign adversaries, particularly China, without appropriate authorization. The questions surrounding Megaspeed and its reported connections to Chinese intelligence have prompted congressional scrutiny. In November, House committees requested information from Nvidia and the Department of Commerce about the company’s security procedures, its interactions with Alice Huang and the potential exposure of sensitive American technology to foreign intelligence operations. The House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and other congressional committees also sought information from Huang regarding his reported interactions with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s protections against foreign espionage. A November 4 congressional letter specifically requested a closed-door briefing addressing the company’s security protocols and the potential implications of Chinese intelligence access to advanced American technology. The Justice Department’s investigation and the congressional inquiries do not establish that Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence operative or that Jensen Huang knowingly participated in unlawful activity. Those questions remain subject to investigation. The distinction is significant because Clinton’s national security characterization is a political assessment of the circumstances, not a finding that the CEO committed an espionage-related offense. Corruption, insider trading and market manipulation allegations Clinton’s second allegation concerns corruption and the relationship between Trump’s presidential authority and his intervention in the affairs of a major private company. Her third allegation, involving insider trading, raises a separate financial-market question. Corporate leadership decisions, government investigations and sensitive national security information can all influence the value of publicly traded companies.

That position changed on November 23, when Nvidia announced that Huang had been restored as president and chief executive officer and returned to the company’s board.
It is important to distinguish between the circumstances of Huang’s departure and a formal dismissal.
His reinstatement on November 23 was subsequently confirmed in Nvidia’s regulatory filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Trump’s involvement in bringing Huang back The presidential involvement is a central part of Clinton’s corruption allegation.
Trump publicly supported Huang’s return after the Nvidia board initially indicated that it would not reinstate him.

On November 20, Trump told reporters that he had discussed Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting in China and expressed support for giving the Nvidia executive another opportunity.
On November 22, Trump used Truth Social to directly urge Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back.
The president argued that reinstating him would benefit both Nvidia and the United States.
The following day, the board announced that Huang had been reinstated, reversing its earlier position.
The president also addressed the national security concerns publicly after the reinstatement.

Associated Press reported that administration officials contacted Nvidia board members and pressed for Huang’s reinstatement, while the president cited the importance of Nvidia to American technological competitiveness and concerns about declining AI stock prices.
The national security investigation Clinton’s first allegation concerns the national security implications of the controversy.
Nvidia manufactures advanced processors used in artificial intelligence systems, data centers and other strategically important technologies.
U.S. export restrictions are designed to prevent sensitive American technology from reaching foreign adversaries, particularly China, without appropriate authorization.
The questions surrounding Megaspeed and its reported connections to Chinese intelligence have prompted congressional scrutiny.

In November, House committees requested information from Nvidia and the Department of Commerce about the company’s security procedures, its interactions with Alice Huang and the potential exposure of sensitive American technology to foreign intelligence operations.

The House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and other congressional committees also sought information from Huang regarding his reported interactions with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s protections against foreign espionage.

A November 4 congressional letter specifically requested a closed-door briefing addressing the company’s security protocols and the potential implications of Chinese intelligence access to advanced American technology.

The Justice Department’s investigation and the congressional inquiries do not establish that Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence operative or that Jensen Huang knowingly participated in unlawful activity.
Those questions remain subject to investigation.
The distinction is significant because Clinton’s national security characterization is a political assessment of the circumstances, not a finding that the CEO committed an espionage-related offense.

Corruption, insider trading and market manipulation allegations Clinton’s second allegation concerns corruption and the relationship between Trump’s presidential authority and his intervention in the affairs of a major private company.
Her third allegation, involving insider trading, raises a separate financial-market question.
Corporate leadership decisions, government investigations and sensitive national security information can all influence the value of publicly traded companies.

He's now with the Tech Policy Program at the Center for European Policy Analysis. He's co-founded and was chief technology officer of the cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike. He's now co-founder and chairman of Silverado Policy Accelerator. He's a former diplomat with extensive intelligence experience. He's now with the tech policy program at the Center for European Policy Analysis, another Washington think tank. Amna Nawaz: Dmitri, less than two weeks ago when we spoke after Huang was ousted, you said the board had to act immediately after revelations of his affairs. Dmitri Alperovitch: It is incomprehensible, because, of course, there's still allegations here that are going to be investigated. But, beyond that, this gentleman Jensen Huang has lied to the board. He's lied potentially about other things, in terms of interference with investigation by the Commerce Department into the smuggling activity of the company led by his mistress. And to now reinstate him before the independent investigation is concluded put them in a buy, in case the investigation might return troubling information. Geoff Bennett: Jim, you heard the president Liz's reporting there referred to Huang as a genius. James Lewis: No, it's like Henry Ford and Ford. So it must have been pretty persuasive, whatever Trump said. Amna Nawaz: Dmitri, we saw how investors have reacted, how the markets have reacted. We know tech leaders were calling for him to be reinstated. Dmitri Alperovitch: I don't think anyone's replaceable. Charles de Gaulle once said that the cemetery is full of irreplaceable people. The reality is that, yes, he's done a lot of great things for the company. You don't need Jensen wan to keep selling those chips. Suddenly, if you are a genius, you can break the law, you can violate corporate policy? James Lewis: I'd say that it's unusual, and I would have waited for the investigation to be completed before I fired him, right? But I do think, if you look at the deals, the financial deals that create AI capabilities that he's at the center of,irreplaceable is a kind of strange word, but he is -- he was central to the casting for the AI movement here in the U.S. Amna Nawaz: Let's talk a little more about some national security concerns that you raised. Her husband apparently had longstanding relationships with this as well. If that's the case, and for anyone that knows MSS in China, they would have absolutely used her as a co-optee effectively to tell her to ask questions, to solicit information from Jensen. So we don't know what information he may have passed, either about Nvidia, maybe about U.S. government policy here, whether he was knowingly involved in the smuggling of these chips that she was involved in.

extraction.body: The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as president and CEO of Nvidia is turbocharging congressional oversight plans and training lawmakers’ bipartisan focus on a central question: how the Trump administration came to the conclusion that Huang’s return posed no national security risk. The move — and President Donald Trump’s involvement in it — is inflaming tensions between the president and his own party. Several Republicans had joined Democrats in planning to scrutinize Huang and chip export controls on China in the wake of the scandal. After being ousted as Nvidia’s CEO earlier this month, Huang had agreed to testify privately before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, House Intelligence Committee, and House China Select Committee next month as well as publicly before the Senate Banking Committee. Trump has said that Attorney General Todd Blanche had affirmed no national security risk from Huang’s rehiring, but the Justice Department is currently conducting ongoing investigations that could affect that question. Huang’s closed-door appearance before the House panels is currently expected to move forward as planned, people familiar with the plans said, but spokespeople for the panels did not respond to requests for comment. Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., who leads the Senate Banking Committee, announced later Monday that Huang would appear at a public hearing on Dec. 3. “I’ve served on a public company board. His behavior does not support reinstatement,” Sen. Pete Ricketts, R-Neb., said of Huang, adding that the company needs to be “answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips.” Huang’s return to the company is also likely to affect his legal representation before Congress. In its statement Monday, Nvidia’s board cited “input from senior levels of the United States government” that left them “confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Trump dialed into a board meeting to push for Huang’s return, Semafor first reported. The Hill’s plans to bring Huang to testify set up a potential collision course with the Trump administration in the final weeks of the lame-duck session, just as the GOP must reckon with its last opportunity to push through its party-line agenda. Congressional Republicans have taken a more hawkish approach to restrictions on chip exports to China in the last month, with leadership in both parties leaning towards using upcoming defense legislation to close gaps in US-China chip-export policy at the center of the Nvidia fallout. “No national security risk?” Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, wrote on X . “Based on what?” A White House official told Semafor that Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Huang “will preserve America’s technological edge over China, strengthen our national security, and ensure the future of SI continues to be built in America,” using a moniker for super intelligence, Trump’s preferred term for AI. Even if Republicans adjust their plans to grill Huang, he’s sure to face considerable scrutiny when Democrats take over control of Congress next year. So, too, will the Trump administration face Democrats’ questions about its interactions with and investigations related to Nvidia as well as its export control policy. “We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia’s own board has completed its investigation,” the top Democrat on the House China Select Committee, Rep. Ro Khanna of California, wrote on X . “Huang must testify at a full public congressional hearing, with every member of the relevant committees allowed to question him.” Democrats also want to hear more about “what ‘input’ was given and by which senior officials,” as Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., put it. Warren, who’s poised to chair the Senate Banking Committee next Congress, said the move “only increases the urgency” of passing more stringent restrictions on chip exports. Trump’s direct involvement is further fueling Democrats’ outrage. “The President is selling out our national security to keep the stock market high and probably for some f*cking donation to his ballroom,” Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., wrote on X .

sources.title: Hillary Clinton Accuses Trump Of Four Potential Scandals In Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s Return — “National Security,” “Corruption,” “Insider Trading” And “Market Manipulation” - NewsBreak
passages: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton is raising four separate allegations surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s return to the company, describing the unfolding controversy as a potential national security, corruption, insider trading and market manipulation scandal.

Clinton’s reference to “Supergate” connects the controversy to Trump’s repeated promotion of artificial intelligence and what he has called “super intelligence.” Her statement raises questions about the intersection of national security investigations, presidential influence over a major technology company and the potential financial consequences of decisions involving one of the world’s most valuable AI businesses.

Her November 23 statement comes after Nvidia reversed its decision not to reinstate Huang, following public pressure from President Donald Trump and reported involvement by senior administration officials.

On November 20, Trump told reporters that he had discussed Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting in China and expressed support for giving the Nvidia executive another opportunity.
On November 22, Trump used Truth Social to directly urge Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back.

Associated Press reported that administration officials contacted Nvidia board members and pressed for Huang’s reinstatement, while the president cited the importance of Nvidia to American technological competitiveness and concerns about declining AI stock prices.
Corporate leadership decisions, government investigations and sensitive national security information can all influence the value of publicly traded companies.

The House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and other congressional committees also sought information from Huang regarding his reported interactions with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s protections against foreign espionage.
It is important to distinguish between the circumstances of Huang’s departure and a formal dismissal.
The president also addressed the national security concerns publicly after the reinstatement.

The Justice Department’s investigation and the congressional inquiries do not establish that Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence operative or that Jensen Huang knowingly participated in unlawful activity.
The following day, the board announced that Huang had been reinstated, reversing its earlier position.
Her third allegation, involving insider trading, raises a separate financial-market question.

extraction.body: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton is raising four separate allegations surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s return to the company, describing the unfolding controversy as a potential national security, corruption, insider trading and market manipulation scandal. Her November 23 statement comes after Nvidia reversed its decision not to reinstate Huang, following public pressure from President Donald Trump and reported involvement by senior administration officials. Clinton’s reference to “Supergate” connects the controversy to Trump’s repeated promotion of artificial intelligence and what he has called “super intelligence.” Her statement raises questions about the intersection of national security investigations, presidential influence over a major technology company and the potential financial consequences of decisions involving one of the world’s most valuable AI businesses. Clinton’s complete statement : Is it a national security scandal? If it’s “super intelligence,” call it Supergate. Why Jensen Huang’s return is attracting scrutiny The controversy surrounding Huang began with his departure from Nvidia on November 12, following reports of personal relationships that raised questions about potential connections to Chinese intelligence. One reported relationship involved Alice Huang, a businesswoman associated with Singapore-based Megaspeed, who has been suspected by U.S. authorities of having links to Chinese intelligence. The allegations have also intensified scrutiny of Nvidia’s business dealings and the potential diversion of advanced artificial intelligence chips to China. Huang subsequently expressed a willingness to return to the company if its board determined that doing so would serve Nvidia, its employees, shareholders and the United States. That position changed on November 23, when Nvidia announced that Huang had been restored as president and chief executive officer and returned to the company’s board. It is important to distinguish between the circumstances of Huang’s departure and a formal dismissal. His reinstatement on November 23 was subsequently confirmed in Nvidia’s regulatory filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Trump’s involvement in bringing Huang back The presidential involvement is a central part of Clinton’s corruption allegation. Trump publicly supported Huang’s return after the Nvidia board initially indicated that it would not reinstate him. On November 20, Trump told reporters that he had discussed Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting in China and expressed support for giving the Nvidia executive another opportunity. On November 22, Trump used Truth Social to directly urge Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back. The president argued that reinstating him would benefit both Nvidia and the United States. The following day, the board announced that Huang had been reinstated, reversing its earlier position. The president also addressed the national security concerns publicly after the reinstatement. Trump said the government had no reason to believe Huang’s return posed a national security risk and stated that the attorney general had confirmed the government did not possess evidence that Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. He nevertheless said Nvidia should continue its internal investigation into compliance with U.S. export controls. The involvement of Trump and Vice President JD Vance has attracted additional scrutiny because the decision involved a company central to America’s artificial intelligence infrastructure and its competition with China. Associated Press reported that administration officials contacted Nvidia board members and pressed for Huang’s reinstatement, while the president cited the importance of Nvidia to American technological competitiveness and concerns about declining AI stock prices. The national security investigation Clinton’s first allegation concerns the national security implications of the controversy. Nvidia manufactures advanced processors used in artificial intelligence systems, data centers and other strategically important technologies. U.S. export restrictions are designed to prevent sensitive American technology from reaching foreign adversaries, particularly China, without appropriate authorization. The questions surrounding Megaspeed and its reported connections to Chinese intelligence have prompted congressional scrutiny. In November, House committees requested information from Nvidia and the Department of Commerce about the company’s security procedures, its interactions with Alice Huang and the potential exposure of sensitive American technology to foreign intelligence operations. The House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and other congressional committees also sought information from Huang regarding his reported interactions with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s protections against foreign espionage.
