extraction.body: President Trump said Monday that he personally persuaded the board of AI giant Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, an extraordinary intervention that raises questions about how the administration is handling national security concerns tied to Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The move, which came after the company's stock had dropped over the last month and prompted alarm about the U.S. economy, signals how far the president is willing to go for the tech billionaires who have lined up behind him in his second term — even when their conduct may undermine national security. It also compounds concerns about corruption within the Trump administration, which was a key driver of Democratic victories in the midterm elections. Trump owned at least $12 million worth of Nvidia shares at the end of last year, and the company has donated $25 million to his White House ballroom project. A bipartisan backlash swiftly materialized Monday, as lawmakers of both parties questioned Huang's reinstatement and called for investigations. Congressional inquiries into Huang's relationship with the alleged spy and allegations that Nvidia's restricted advanced AI chips were smuggled into China via Malaysia have already been set in motion. Huang is scheduled to speak in closed-door interviews with three House committees on Dec. Trump praised the board's decision and said in an interview with CNBC that "investors should be very happy," as the company's stock shot up more than 30% and boosted the market Monday. The president added that his administration has no reason to believe Huang's return will pose a risk to national security. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct," Trump wrote on X. The president also tapped Vice President JD Vance to act as an emissary to Nvidia's board and try to ease concerns about the reinstatement. Without an independent investigation, Americans "can't have confidence that all the risks have been identified," said Matt Pearl, an expert on national security and technology. "This leaves Congress, Nvidia shareholders, and the public unable to judge whether such risks were adequately addressed," said Pearl, a director at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. In addition to the affair with the alleged spy, Huang was also reported to have had a relationship with a subordinate and to have fostered a workplace culture marked with humiliation rituals. As other tech leaders including Elon Musk and Sam Altman celebrated Huang's reinstatement, Trump — whose political career has been beset by his own sexual misconduct scandals — sought to minimize concerns around Huang's affair. He told CNBC that he didn't believe the woman was a spy, though he did not back up that speculation, and later posted an apparently AI-generated image on social media that lionized Huang, showing him holding up a red bra in an imitation of the images of Trump pumping his fist after the 2024 assassination attempt against him. The president, who has sought to protect the AI industry for months even as safety concerns have mounted over its rapid rate of advancement, argued in the CNBC interview that Huang was key to America's ability to compete on the global stage. “I can tell you the biggest threat would be losing the brainpower of somebody like Jensen. “To me, that would be a far bigger threat than anything we’re talking about.” Trump, who has argued that America needs to "protect our brilliant people" when defending Huang, also suggested China could have tried to recruit Huang had his administration not swayed Nvidia to bring him back. "If we didn't do this, I could see China coming in and saying to Jensen, 'Hey, how would you like to come to China," Trump told CNBC. You know, he's got a little blood there." Ramesh Srinivasan, director of the UC Center for Global Digital Cultures, said the episode reflects how central Nvidia has become to the AI economy and thus the economy overall — in part thanks to the federal government’s investments in it — and the Trump administration’s attempt to reassure markets in order to keep backstopping it. The reinstatement of Huang is also a result of Trump “trying to inject himself as the central factor and character and kingmaker” in the tech and AI space, even as tech leaders have begun to back away from him and his party since Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress earlier this month, Srinivasan said. As investment and tech leaders telegraphed jubilation, Trump said on CNBC that "sex sells." He predicted that the scandal would be a “net positive” for Huang and suggested the situation had helped the public see "how advanced" Huang's company is. “This is why America is the greatest country on Earth,” Gavin Baker, chief investment officer of Atreides Management, wrote on X, comparing Huang to the "Lord of the Rings" wizard Gandalf coming back from the dead in a more powerful state. “Every part of Jensen’s story would have only been possible in America.” Critics said Huang’s reinstatement was an example of the type of corruption that voters repudiated in this month’s midterm elections. “How come a certain class of people are able to get what they want and somehow shortcut the process?” Chia said. Jensen Huang became Trump’s ‘friend’ to the point where Trump goes to bat for the guy in the most difficult of circumstances. Who else has that kind of relationship?” Politicians from both parties said the reinstatement underscored the urgent need for congressional hearings to get answers on the degree to which national security may have been compromised. Nvidia's decision will not "excuse Huang from testifying before Congress" in December, Sen. "It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips." Sen. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) called for Congress to investigate Nvidia’s chip sales, diversions of its advanced chips to China and what the Trump administration and Huang knew about China’s effort to acquire Nvidia’s advanced chip technology. He said Congress should “follow the trail of who financially benefited” from the sales and diversions. “Donald Trump was told more than a year ago that China was targeting NVIDIA to undermine our AI advantage,” Schiff said on X. “Instead of responding to the threat, Trump and the Commerce Department greenlit the company’s sale of advanced AI chips to China. … Meanwhile, the president watched his personal NVIDIA investments soar to as much as $62 million.” Chia said the abrupt reversal by the board, after it had indicated last week that it was not considering reinstating Huang, signaled that “something very strange” was going on. The idea that the government could have interfered directly with a private enterprise is troubling and without direct modern precedent, he said. “Since when does the president of the United States get to call up the board of a public company and just say, ‘Do this’ ?” Chia said.

Trump said he had been in touch with the board since Huang stepped down Nov 12 following revelations about his extramarital affairs with subordinates and with Chinese national Alice Huang, ​a suspected spy of no relation. Trump, who counts Huang as among his closest friends in Silicon Valley, had pushed for his reinstatement despite the revelations in an extraordinarily public intervention by a US president into a company’s decision-making. “The board decided to do what we wanted to do. And one of the things the board wanted to know is there a national security problem?” Trump said in an interview with CNBC after the board’s decision to reinstate Huang as CEO was announced. “And after a lot of research... we said, ‘No, it’s not a problem,’” Trump said in the interview. “We feel very strongly that he’s in good shape, very good shape.” “I called him up and I said, I ask you to do one thing, Jensen: work hard,” Trump told CNBC. “I didn’t talk about other things because he understands that.... I just said work hard because if you work hard, there’s nobody that can capture what you’ve done.” Trump also expressed concern that China could poach Jensen Huang in the nearly hour-long CNBC interview, saying “we have to protect our geniuses.” “Jensen could take the next plane to China, and I guarantee you they would give him whatever he wanted,” he said. Trump would not say if he attended any Nvidia board meeting, but told CNBC he was represented there. In a social media post earlier on Nov 23, Trump welcomed the board’s decision and called Jensen Huang a “great patriot and a national treasure.” He said Attorney-General Todd Blanche has confirmed that the federal government has no evidence that Jensen Huang engaged in unlawful conduct. “The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. Asked what the CIA had told him about the issue, Trump said, “Let me just say, I have clearance. And If I didn’t have clearance, I wouldn’t have done the deal,” he told CNBC. Trump said Jensen Huang’s leadership at Nvidia was needed to ensure the continued success of the company, as well as the US economy. The US government is investigating whether Alice Huang was a Chinese asset , Trump has said. He told CNBC he did not ask Chinese President Xi Jinping if Alice Huang was a spy when the two leaders met last week. The New York Times reported on Nov 22 that Alice Huang kept in contact with an official ​from China’s top spy agency for more than a year during her affair with ‌the Nvidia chief executive. “Well, who isn’t in contact?” Trump said when asked about the report on CNBC. Trump later in the day posted a manipulated image on Truth Social showing Jensen Huang, raising a red bra, in place of Trump in the famous photo of the bloodied president raising his fist after a 2024 assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania. US lawmakers have been asking questions about Trump’s knowledge of Huang’s personal life. Democrats on the House of Representatives Foreign Affairs Committee were not informed about the reinstatement decision, an aide said on Nov 23. Texas Republican Senator John Cornyn raised questions about the board’s determination that Huang’s reinstatement poses no security concerns. “No national security risk? Based on what?” Cornyn said in an X post. As he left Washington last week for an Asia trip, the US president said he would not mind seeking Huang’s return to the company, saying, “I think he learned a big lesson.” Trump’s language grew more forceful at a White House briefing after the trip on Nov 20. He said he’d like to see the former Nvidia chief “make a big apology and go back,” adding: “I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, ‘Oh, brilliant, brilliant – he’s a brilliant man.’ He is.” On the night of Nov 22, Trump posted on Truth Social that he hoped Nvidia’s board would rehire Huang: “It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.” The reversal sent Nvidia’s shares soaring 33%, boosting shares of other chip-related companies as well. Trump bought as much as US$265,000 (S$342,000) in Nvidia ​stock and sold as much as US$15,000 worth of the stock in September, weeks before reports surfaced of Huang’s ties to the alleged Chinese spy, according to Trump’s latest financial disclosure released on Nov 19. “Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with US export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect US National Security,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. Trump, who counts Huang as among his closest friends in Silicon Valley, had pushed for his reinstatement despite the revelations in an extraordinarily public intervention by a US president into a company’s decision-making.

“The board decided to do what we wanted to do. And one of the things the board wanted to know is there a national security problem?” Trump said in an interview with CNBC after the board’s decision to reinstate Huang as CEO was announced.
“And after a lot of research... we said, ‘No, it’s not a problem,’” Trump said in the interview. “We feel very strongly that he’s in good shape, very good shape.”

“I called him up and I said, I ask you to do one thing, Jensen: work hard,” Trump told CNBC. “I didn’t talk about other things because he understands that.... I just said work hard because if you work hard, there’s nobody that can capture what you’ve done.”
Trump also expressed concern that China could poach Jensen Huang in the nearly hour-long CNBC interview, saying “we have to protect our geniuses.”
“Jensen could take the next plane to China, and I guarantee you they would give him whatever he wanted,” he said.
Trump would not say if he attended any Nvidia board meeting, but told CNBC he was represented there.

In a social media post earlier on Nov 23, Trump welcomed the board’s decision and called Jensen Huang a “great patriot and a national treasure.” He said Attorney-General Todd Blanche has confirmed that the federal government has no evidence that Jensen Huang engaged in unlawful conduct.
“The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.
Asked what the CIA had told him about the issue, Trump said, “Let me just say, I have clearance. And If I didn’t have clearance, I wouldn’t have done the deal,” he told CNBC.
Trump said Jensen Huang’s leadership at Nvidia was needed to ensure the continued success of the company, as well as the US economy.

The US government is investigating whether Alice Huang was a Chinese asset , Trump has said. He told CNBC he did not ask Chinese President Xi Jinping if Alice Huang was a spy when the two leaders met last week.

Trump later in the day posted a manipulated image on Truth Social showing Jensen Huang, raising a red bra, in place of Trump in the famous photo of the bloodied president raising his fist after a 2024 assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania.

As he left Washington last week for an Asia trip, the US president said he would not mind seeking Huang’s return to the company, saying, “I think he learned a big lesson.”

Trump’s language grew more forceful at a White House briefing after the trip on Nov 20. He said he’d like to see the former Nvidia chief “make a big apology and go back,” adding: “I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, ‘Oh, brilliant, brilliant – he’s a brilliant man.’ He is.”
On the night of Nov 22, Trump posted on Truth Social that he hoped Nvidia’s board would rehire Huang: “It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.”
The reversal sent Nvidia’s shares soaring 33%, boosting shares of other chip-related companies as well.

passages: US President Donald Trump personally lobbied Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, describing the semiconductor company's founder as indispensable to America's artificial intelligence ambitions and arguing that losing his expertise posed a greater national security threat than retaining him.Trump said he had spoken to the board directly and indirectly before Nvidia announced Huang's return on Monday, marking an extraordinary intervention in the leadership of one of the world's most valuable technology companies.Also read: The rise, fall and return of Jensen Huang: Inside Nvidia's extraordinary leadership saga“I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview on Monday.

“And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot,” he added.The President also defended the board's decision, saying it had acted responsibly in bringing Huang back.“I think the [Nvidia] board acted really responsibly,” Trump said, adding that retaining the executive was more important than allowing him to leave the company.“People say, is it a threat to have him?

The White House has maintained that his investments are managed by outside advisers and do not present a conflict of interest.Trump, meanwhile, has urged Nvidia to continue its internal investigation into compliance with US export controls, even as he has publicly backed Huang's return.

The announcement represented a significant reversal, particularly as the board had previously indicated that it was not considering bringing him back.Trump also said Attorney General Todd Blanche had confirmed that the government did not possess evidence of unlawful conduct by Huang.

Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the Administration’s inexplicable desire to save Huang,” Bacon wrote on X, while calling for Congress to investigate approvals for high-end computing chip sales to China.Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren also called on the administration to explain what role senior government officials played in supporting Huang's reinstatement.The administration must disclose “what input was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement,”

extraction.body: The decision to bring Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang back in a surprise move after U.S. President Donald Trump intervened has sparked questions about the independence of the company's board and its oversight of management. Nvidia's board initially accepted Huang's resignation after a scandal involving the CEO emerged, but reappointed him after the company's shares plunged and Trump's team called for his return, CNN and other major U.S. news outlets reported on the 23rd, local time. Trump reportedly enlisted Vice President JD Vance to tell Nvidia's board that Huang's return would not pose a threat to national security. Trump also said in an interview with CNBC that day that he had contacted Nvidia's board directly. "I convinced them and got it done," he said. Ann Lipton, a law professor at the University of Colorado Boulder, told The New York Times (NYT) that the board was likely concerned it could face legal liability if it failed to properly fulfill its oversight duties after the scandal involving Huang, but was also likely influenced by the Trump administration's intervention. "What the Trump administration did was give the board confidence that it could be protected legally," Lipton said. Others have also questioned the board's effectiveness. Charles Elson, a corporate governance expert and former University of Delaware professor, told U.S. online news outlet Axios, "This episode shows that the board has no conviction whatsoever." He added, "It defies every principle of corporate management and will ultimately harm the company and its shareholders." Peter Jaworski, a business ethics professor at Georgetown University, said, "Just because Jensen Huang is indispensable doesn't mean he shouldn't be held accountable." He asked, "If he can get through this without any accountability, how can the board control his conduct going forward?" Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, a Yale University professor known as an "adviser to CEOs," said the board should have removed Huang from his duties and conducted an investigation from the outset. "Every single member of the board should resign," he said.

extraction.body: President Trump said Monday that he personally persuaded the board of AI giant Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, an extraordinary intervention that raises questions about how the administration is handling national security concerns tied to Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The move, which came after the company's stock had dropped over the last month and prompted alarm about the U.S. economy, signals how far the president is willing to go for the tech billionaires who have lined up behind him in his second term — even when their conduct may undermine national security. It also compounds concerns about corruption within the Trump administration, which was a key driver of Democratic victories in the midterm elections. Trump owned at least $12 million worth of Nvidia shares at the end of last year, and the company has donated $25 million to his White House ballroom project. A bipartisan backlash swiftly materialized Monday, as lawmakers of both parties questioned Huang's reinstatement and called for investigations. Congressional inquiries into Huang's relationship with the alleged spy and allegations that Nvidia's restricted advanced AI chips were smuggled into China via Malaysia have already been set in motion. Huang is scheduled to speak in closed-door interviews with three House committees on Dec. Trump praised the board's decision and said in an interview with CNBC that "investors should be very happy," as the company's stock shot up more than 30% and boosted the market Monday. The president added that his administration has no reason to believe Huang's return will pose a risk to national security. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct," Trump wrote on X. The president also tapped Vice President JD Vance to act as an emissary to Nvidia's board and try to ease concerns about the reinstatement. Without an independent investigation, Americans "can't have confidence that all the risks have been identified," said Matt Pearl, an expert on national security and technology. "This leaves Congress, Nvidia shareholders, and the public unable to judge whether such risks were adequately addressed," said Pearl, a director at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. In addition to the affair with the alleged spy, Huang was also reported to have had a relationship with a subordinate and to have fostered a workplace culture marked with humiliation rituals. As other tech leaders including Elon Musk and Sam Altman celebrated Huang's reinstatement, Trump — whose political career has been beset by his own sexual misconduct scandals — sought to minimize concerns around Huang's affair. He told CNBC that he didn't believe the woman was a spy, though he did not back up that speculation, and later posted an apparently AI-generated image on social media that lionized Huang, showing him holding up a red bra in an imitation of the images of Trump pumping his fist after the 2024 assassination attempt against him. The president, who has sought to protect the AI industry for months even as safety concerns have mounted over its rapid rate of advancement, argued in the CNBC interview that Huang was key to America's ability to compete on the global stage. “I can tell you the biggest threat would be losing the brainpower of somebody like Jensen. “To me, that would be a far bigger threat than anything we’re talking about.” Trump, who has argued that America needs to "protect our brilliant people" when defending Huang, also suggested China could have tried to recruit Huang had his administration not swayed Nvidia to bring him back. "If we didn't do this, I could see China coming in and saying to Jensen, 'Hey, how would you like to come to China," Trump told CNBC. You know, he's got a little blood there." Ramesh Srinivasan, director of the UC Center for Global Digital Cultures, said the episode reflects how central Nvidia has become to the AI economy and thus the economy overall — in part thanks to the federal government’s investments in it — and the Trump administration’s attempt to reassure markets in order to keep backstopping it. The reinstatement of Huang is also a result of Trump “trying to inject himself as the central factor and character and kingmaker” in the tech and AI space, even as tech leaders have begun to back away from him and his party since Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress earlier this month, Srinivasan said. As investment and tech leaders telegraphed jubilation, Trump said on CNBC that "sex sells." He predicted that the scandal would be a “net positive” for Huang and suggested the situation had helped the public see "how advanced" Huang's company is. “This is why America is the greatest country on Earth,” Gavin Baker, chief investment officer of Atreides Management, wrote on X, comparing Huang to the "Lord of the Rings" wizard Gandalf coming back from the dead in a more powerful state. “Every part of Jensen’s story would have only been possible in America.” Critics said Huang’s reinstatement was an example of the type of corruption that voters repudiated in this month’s midterm elections. “How come a certain class of people are able to get what they want and somehow shortcut the process?” Chia said. Jensen Huang became Trump’s ‘friend’ to the point where Trump goes to bat for the guy in the most difficult of circumstances. Who else has that kind of relationship?” Politicians from both parties said the reinstatement underscored the urgent need for congressional hearings to get answers on the degree to which national security may have been compromised. Nvidia's decision will not "excuse Huang from testifying before Congress" in December, Sen. "It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips." Sen. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) called for Congress to investigate Nvidia’s chip sales, diversions of its advanced chips to China and what the Trump administration and Huang knew about China’s effort to acquire Nvidia’s advanced chip technology. He said Congress should “follow the trail of who financially benefited” from the sales and diversions. “Donald Trump was told more than a year ago that China was targeting NVIDIA to undermine our AI advantage,” Schiff said on X. “Instead of responding to the threat, Trump and the Commerce Department greenlit the company’s sale of advanced AI chips to China. … Meanwhile, the president watched his personal NVIDIA investments soar to as much as $62 million.” Chia said the abrupt reversal by the board, after it had indicated last week that it was not considering reinstating Huang, signaled that “something very strange” was going on. The idea that the government could have interfered directly with a private enterprise is troubling and without direct modern precedent, he said. “Since when does the president of the United States get to call up the board of a public company and just say, ‘Do this’ ?” Chia said.

Nvidia's board initially accepted Huang's resignation after a scandal involving the CEO emerged, but reappointed him after the company's shares plunged and Trump's team called for his return, CNN and other major U.S. news outlets reported on the 23rd, local time. Trump reportedly enlisted Vice President JD Vance to tell Nvidia's board that Huang's return would not pose a threat to national security. Trump also said in an interview with CNBC that day that he had contacted Nvidia's board directly. "I convinced them and got it done," he said. Ann Lipton, a law professor at the University of Colorado Boulder, told The New York Times (NYT) that the board was likely concerned it could face legal liability if it failed to properly fulfill its oversight duties after the scandal involving Huang, but was also likely influenced by the Trump administration's intervention. "What the Trump administration did was give the board confidence that it could be protected legally," Lipton said. Others have also questioned the board's effectiveness. Charles Elson, a corporate governance expert and former University of Delaware professor, told U.S. online news outlet Axios, "This episode shows that the board has no conviction whatsoever." He added, "It defies every principle of corporate management and will ultimately harm the company and its shareholders." Peter Jaworski, a business ethics professor at Georgetown University, said, "Just because Jensen Huang is indispensable doesn't mean he shouldn't be held accountable." He asked, "If he can get through this without any accountability, how can the board control his conduct going forward?" Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, a Yale University professor known as an "adviser to CEOs," said the board should have removed Huang from his duties and conducted an investigation from the outset. "Every single member of the board should resign," he said.

Jones, said the move “is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.” Nvidia stock rose more than 30% following the news. Nvidia’s board has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president, CEO and board director, “effective immediately,” the chipmaker’s board announced Monday, noting the decision was made after consultation with “senior levels of the United States government.” “The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA,” it said in a statement . “In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” it went on. The decision was reportedly made with guidance from President Donald Trump , who Semafor first reported dialed in to a board meeting to argue for his return. Trump later confirmed in a 50-minute phone interview with CNBC that he’d spoken “directly and indirectly” to the board to urge it to reinstate Huang. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” he told the outlet’s Eamon Javers. “And I convinced them.” The president also said the board “did ask for assurance on the national security threat,” and that the U.S. gave “assurance at least with everything we know, and we know a lot.” The board’s chair, Harvey C. Jones, said the move “is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.” Nvidia stock rose more than 30% following the news. Huang resigned Nov. 12 after admitting to having an extramarital affair with a woman who was reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy. Last week, he released a public statement acknowledging he’d made “serious mistakes” but said he would be “honored” to return if asked. “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” he said in a post on X. Video posted on social media on Monday appeared to show Nvidia employees greeting Huang with loud applause and chants of his name after his return. “I’ve made some very terrible mistakes, and I’m going to work on coming back,” he said, according to The New York Times . “Thank you all for the second chance,” he said in one video shared by CNBC. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.” The board said Monday that an investigation into Huang being “the target of a foreign intelligence effort” remains ongoing with Huang’s full support and cooperation and that his reinstatement, according to unidentified U.S. officials, “poses no national security risk.” “I think the board acted really responsibly” in bringing Huang back into the company, Trump said, adding that the AI leader “did nothing wrong.” “As far as the woman is concerned, every time you have a Chinese woman that’s good-looking or beautiful, they say she’s a spy,” he said. Despite his return, Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter remain scheduled to testify on Capitol Hill early next month, a House Foreign Affairs Committee spokesperson told Punchbowl News , saying Huang’s return “changes nothing.” Lawmakers are looking into Chinese-based companies’ ability to access advanced AI chips and whether the companies have been able to skirt U.S. export control laws. “Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang is outrageous. We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia’s own board has completed its investigation,” Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.), who serves on the House Intelligence Committee and is the top Democrat on the Select Committee on China, posted on X . “Huang must testify at a full public congressional hearing, with every member of the relevant committees allowed to question him,” he continued. Trump hailed Huang’s reinstatement in a Truth Social post Monday as beneficial to not just the company “but the American Economy.” “The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security,” he said, adding that the U.S. attorney general also said there is no evidence Huang engaged in any unlawful conduct. “Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security,” he said. Trump appeared to have had advanced knowledge of the announcement, having told a PBS News reporter earlier on Monday that Huang is “back where he should be.” He also said he called Huang after speaking with the board and “the deal was finished.” “I called him up, and I said: ‘I ask you to do one thing, Jensen. Work hard,’” he told CNBC. Trump told reporters Friday that he’d discussed Huang with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and that Xi had called Huang a “brilliant man.” The president also said Monday that Xi might have asked Huang to lead a Chinese company if he wasn’t reinstated at Nvidia.

“The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA,” it said in a statement .

“In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” it went on.

Trump later confirmed in a 50-minute phone interview with CNBC that he’d spoken “directly and indirectly” to the board to urge it to reinstate Huang.

The president also said the board “did ask for assurance on the national security threat,” and that the U.S. gave “assurance at least with everything we know, and we know a lot.”
The board’s chair, Harvey C. Jones, said the move “is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.” Nvidia stock rose more than 30% following the news.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” he said in a post on X.
Video posted on social media on Monday appeared to show Nvidia employees greeting Huang with loud applause and chants of his name after his return.
“I’ve made some very terrible mistakes, and I’m going to work on coming back,” he said, according to The New York Times .
“Thank you all for the second chance,” he said in one video shared by CNBC. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”

The board said Monday that an investigation into Huang being “the target of a foreign intelligence effort” remains ongoing with Huang’s full support and cooperation and that his reinstatement, according to unidentified U.S. officials, “poses no national security risk.”
“I think the board acted really responsibly” in bringing Huang back into the company, Trump said, adding that the AI leader “did nothing wrong.”
“As far as the woman is concerned, every time you have a Chinese woman that’s good-looking or beautiful, they say she’s a spy,” he said.

Despite his return, Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter remain scheduled to testify on Capitol Hill early next month, a House Foreign Affairs Committee spokesperson told Punchbowl News , saying Huang’s return “changes nothing.”
Lawmakers are looking into Chinese-based companies’ ability to access advanced AI chips and whether the companies have been able to skirt U.S. export control laws.

“Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang is outrageous. We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia’s own board has completed its investigation,” Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.), who serves on the House Intelligence Committee and is the top Democrat on the Select Committee on China, posted on X .
“Huang must testify at a full public congressional hearing, with every member of the relevant committees allowed to question him,” he continued.
Trump hailed Huang’s reinstatement in a Truth Social post Monday as beneficial to not just the company “but the American Economy.”

“The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security,” he said, adding that the U.S. attorney general also said there is no evidence Huang engaged in any unlawful conduct.

“Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security,” he said.

Trump appeared to have had advanced knowledge of the announcement, having told a PBS News reporter earlier on Monday that Huang is “back where he should be.” He also said he called Huang after speaking with the board and “the deal was finished.”
“I called him up, and I said: ‘I ask you to do one thing, Jensen. Work hard,’” he told CNBC.

Trump told reporters Friday that he’d discussed Huang with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and that Xi had called Huang a “brilliant man.” The president also said Monday that Xi might have asked Huang to lead a Chinese company if he wasn’t reinstated at Nvidia.

The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Muang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work," he noted. sources.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
passages: Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship.
On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship , a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.
The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now.

Anthropic says teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.
With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.
“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line.
But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”
Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub.
Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.
This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.
Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first.
Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.

The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team. The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available , and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed. Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. extraction.body: Anthropic has introduced Claude Ship , a new artificial intelligence platform designed to automate some of the most time-consuming tasks in software development, including reviewing code, resolving conflicts and approving changes before they are incorporated into production software. Announced Monday and available in beta, Claude Ship represents an expansion of Anthropic’s strategy to move beyond AI-assisted code generation toward managing the broader software development process. The platform combines an existing code-review product with two new AI agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, to help engineering teams move software changes from development to deployment more efficiently. The central objective is to eliminate bottlenecks that occur after developers finish writing code but before that code becomes part of a company’s software. Anthropic describes the goal as enabling companies to release software as quickly as their engineers can develop it. Claude Ship focuses on managing pull requests , a fundamental component of modern software development. A pull request, commonly called a PR, is a proposal to incorporate changes made by a developer into a shared software repository. Before those changes are accepted, they typically undergo several checks, including automated testing, code review, security analysis and approval by other engineers. For large organizations, this process can become a significant operational bottleneck. Developers may spend hours or days waiting for colleagues to review code, resolve conflicting changes or approve relatively routine updates. Claude Ship is designed to automate portions of that workflow while allowing companies to establish their own rules governing which changes require human oversight. The platform integrates with GitHub, one of the world’s most widely used software development platforms. Anthropic’s new offering combines three capabilities: The existing, generally available tool examines proposed code changes and identifies potential issues before they are merged. It provides findings that developers or other automated agents can use to address problems. This new agent helps keep pull requests in a merge-ready condition by addressing review feedback, handling merge conflicts and responding to issues identified by automated tools or human reviewers. PR Steward does not independently approve or merge pull requests. Its role is to prepare changes for the next step. This new agent evaluates pull requests against approval policies established by individual engineering teams. Policies are stored in the software repository and can incorporate code-review findings, company-defined classifications and other criteria expressed in natural language. The system is intended to distinguish routine changes that qualify for automated approval from more consequential modifications requiring human review. How Claude Ship Could Change Software Development The significance of Claude Ship extends beyond automated code reviews. AI coding assistants have already accelerated the process of writing software. Products such as Anthropic’s Claude Code and competing development tools allow programmers to generate, modify and troubleshoot code using natural-language instructions. However, faster code generation can create a new problem: engineering teams may produce changes more quickly than their existing review and approval processes can handle. Such policies could reduce repetitive administrative work while preserving oversight of higher-risk changes. The potential benefits include faster software releases, fewer unresolved pull requests, reduced developer workload and more consistent enforcement of engineering standards. However, automated approvals also introduce risks. Companies will need to ensure that their policies are appropriately restrictive and that AI-generated assessments do not overlook security vulnerabilities, operational dependencies or subtle software defects. Claude Ship places Anthropic deeper into competition with Microsoft-owned GitHub and other companies developing AI-powered software engineering platforms. The competitive opportunity is substantial because software development involves far more than writing code. Testing, reviewing, documenting, approving and deploying changes consume considerable engineering resources. As AI makes code generation faster, companies offering automation across the entire development lifecycle could capture a larger share of enterprise technology spending. Anthropic disclosed several additional details about Claude Ship’s capabilities and early performance. The company said its own Claude Code engineering team more than doubled the number of merged pull requests between June and September, while the proportion of changes subsequently reverted declined by more than 40%. Those figures reflect Anthropic’s broader development process, rather than an independently verified measure of Claude Ship’s effectiveness. Developers can also access the new functionality through a /ship command in Claude Code. The command can push changes, open a pull request, initiate reviews and address failing checks. Engineering administrators can select among three review levels—Quick, Standard and Deep—and configure spending limits for individual repositories. Claude Ship is billed according to token usage, with costs varying based on the volume and complexity of pull requests and the amount of automated work performed. Anthropic recommends that organizations initially run automated approvals in an observation-only mode before allowing them to influence production approval decisions. The company also announced that eligible Claude Enterprise organizations can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits , subject to terms, by January 15, 2027. Early customers include TELUS Digital and Carvana, whose engineering executives reported benefits from automating review feedback and reducing repetitive development tasks.

extraction.body: Anthropic has introduced Claude Ship , a new artificial intelligence platform designed to automate some of the most time-consuming tasks in software development, including reviewing code, resolving conflicts and approving changes before they are incorporated into production software. Announced Monday and available in beta, Claude Ship represents an expansion of Anthropic’s strategy to move beyond AI-assisted code generation toward managing the broader software development process. The platform combines an existing code-review product with two new AI agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, to help engineering teams move software changes from development to deployment more efficiently. The central objective is to eliminate bottlenecks that occur after developers finish writing code but before that code becomes part of a company’s software. Anthropic describes the goal as enabling companies to release software as quickly as their engineers can develop it. Claude Ship focuses on managing pull requests , a fundamental component of modern software development. A pull request, commonly called a PR, is a proposal to incorporate changes made by a developer into a shared software repository. Before those changes are accepted, they typically undergo several checks, including automated testing, code review, security analysis and approval by other engineers. For large organizations, this process can become a significant operational bottleneck. Developers may spend hours or days waiting for colleagues to review code, resolve conflicting changes or approve relatively routine updates. Claude Ship is designed to automate portions of that workflow while allowing companies to establish their own rules governing which changes require human oversight. The platform integrates with GitHub, one of the world’s most widely used software development platforms. Anthropic’s new offering combines three capabilities: The existing, generally available tool examines proposed code changes and identifies potential issues before they are merged. It provides findings that developers or other automated agents can use to address problems. This new agent helps keep pull requests in a merge-ready condition by addressing review feedback, handling merge conflicts and responding to issues identified by automated tools or human reviewers. PR Steward does not independently approve or merge pull requests. Its role is to prepare changes for the next step. This new agent evaluates pull requests against approval policies established by individual engineering teams. Policies are stored in the software repository and can incorporate code-review findings, company-defined classifications and other criteria expressed in natural language. The system is intended to distinguish routine changes that qualify for automated approval from more consequential modifications requiring human review. How Claude Ship Could Change Software Development The significance of Claude Ship extends beyond automated code reviews. AI coding assistants have already accelerated the process of writing software. Products such as Anthropic’s Claude Code and competing development tools allow programmers to generate, modify and troubleshoot code using natural-language instructions. However, faster code generation can create a new problem: engineering teams may produce changes more quickly than their existing review and approval processes can handle. Such policies could reduce repetitive administrative work while preserving oversight of higher-risk changes. The potential benefits include faster software releases, fewer unresolved pull requests, reduced developer workload and more consistent enforcement of engineering standards. However, automated approvals also introduce risks. Companies will need to ensure that their policies are appropriately restrictive and that AI-generated assessments do not overlook security vulnerabilities, operational dependencies or subtle software defects. Claude Ship places Anthropic deeper into competition with Microsoft-owned GitHub and other companies developing AI-powered software engineering platforms. The competitive opportunity is substantial because software development involves far more than writing code. Testing, reviewing, documenting, approving and deploying changes consume considerable engineering resources. As AI makes code generation faster, companies offering automation across the entire development lifecycle could capture a larger share of enterprise technology spending. Anthropic disclosed several additional details about Claude Ship’s capabilities and early performance. The company said its own Claude Code engineering team more than doubled the number of merged pull requests between June and September, while the proportion of changes subsequently reverted declined by more than 40%. Those figures reflect Anthropic’s broader development process, rather than an independently verified measure of Claude Ship’s effectiveness. Developers can also access the new functionality through a /ship command in Claude Code. The command can push changes, open a pull request, initiate reviews and address failing checks. Engineering administrators can select among three review levels—Quick, Standard and Deep—and configure spending limits for individual repositories. Claude Ship is billed according to token usage, with costs varying based on the volume and complexity of pull requests and the amount of automated work performed. Anthropic recommends that organizations initially run automated approvals in an observation-only mode before allowing them to influence production approval decisions. The company also announced that eligible Claude Enterprise organizations can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits , subject to terms, by January 15, 2027. Early customers include TELUS Digital and Carvana, whose engineering executives reported benefits from automating review feedback and reducing repetitive development tasks.

Cybersecurity experts say attacks on infrastructure are not always aimed at a specific facility. Instead, hackers often look for vulnerable systems. "Smaller municipal and regional facilities often run older equipment with tight budgets making them very attractive for proving a point, for example, causing disruption or testing vulnerabilities," said Sudip Mazumder, a professor of electrical and computer engineering at the University of Illinois Chicago. Experts said the potential consequences of a successful cyberattack on water infrastructure can extend beyond computer systems. Although the Algonquin Dam is a relatively small, low-head dam, it uses movable gates to manage river levels, particularly during periods of high water or when ice jams form. "If you have a flood for instance, and all of a sudden you need to have that capacity to pass water through, and all of a sudden somebody shuts down the gates, and you can't open them. Well what is going to happen with the water?" said Marcelo Garcia, a professor of civil and environmental engineering at the University of Illinois. According to experts, water levels could rise upstream if dam gates could not be operated, potentially causing flooding. The Fox River also serves as a source of drinking water for downstream communities, including Elgin and Aurora. Concerns about the security of water infrastructure extend beyond the Algonquin facility. In July, the FBI warned that cyberattacks on water utilities in at least seven states had disrupted operations, including reports of flooding and lost water pressure. "It's something to prepare for, without, you know, being alarmed. Well, you know, you want to get to the bottom of it and figure out why did this happen, who might be the culprit then, and then just prepare," Garcia said. The Illinois Department of Natural Resources said state and federal agencies are investigating the incident. ABC7 contacted the department for additional information but did not receive a response. So far, officials have not identified a suspect or disclosed what systems may have been targeted. They also said there is no indication the attempted breach is connected to other recent cyber incidents.

extraction.body: Our latest holiday cheat sheet is jam-packed with our favorite tech, along with Play-Doh, vinyl, and plenty of analog picks. If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed. If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. Gift-giving isn’t just about grabbing something solid under a determined spending limit. It’s an expression of love, a way to show someone how well you really know them. That doesn’t mean you have to do it all on your own, though. Sometimes you just need a push in the right direction to get things rolling. This year, we spent hours collecting our favorites to help you get ahead of your holiday shopping. This list has everything: minimalist smart rings , Play-Doh flowers , sleek beat machines — you name it. Whatever your needs, no matter how demanding the recipient, you’ll find something exceptional below for that special someone on your list. If you’re a fan of Apple’s open-ear standard AirPods, the AirPods 5 are the best model yet. The higher-end pair (there are two models) offers upgraded sound, better noise cancellation, and swipe-based volume controls, bringing some Pro-level features to the buds that started the wire-free revolution. It’s rare for a product to boast that it’s “hacker-friendly,” but the Busy Bar isn’t your average device. Equipped with a pixelated LED screen, fantastically fun buttons, and intriguing ways to play, Flipper’s open-source productivity tool breeds efficiency by, among other things, keeping coworkers from interrupting your flow with their weekend plans. Espresso in the woods? Yes, please. The GR2’s magical mechanics make it possible, letting you turn 12 ounces of grounds into espresso without power. Its carrying case houses all the accessories needed to get that sweet shot of bean, making real coffee available virtually anywhere. For those who love travel but hate the constraints of a hotel TV, Belkin’s ConnectAir is a slick solution. Plug the transmitter into any device with a USB-C video-out port and the receiver into the TV’s HDMI port, and voilà, you’re easily (and wirelessly) connected. The company that brought gaming to the masses still defies the odds, thanks in large part to its creative roots. Those roots run deep, and journalist Keza MacDonald’s fascinating book traces them to their source, from a simple card game company to the minds behind the biggest hits of all time. You can give the gift of creativity with this do-it-all digital music maker. Akai’s portable sampler, beat maker, and all-around sound machine blends tactile quick keys and pads with an onboard screen so musicians can build it all in a box and send the results to their DAW of choice. For those in smaller dwellings, efficient living means maximizing space. That’s where combo appliances like Ninja’s newest microwave / air fryer combo come in. The handy countertop gadget lets you zap your food, then crisp it at the end so your pizza or French fries don’t turn into a soggy mess. Perhaps no game in history is more anticipated than the latest entry in Rockstar’s sprawling, intricate, and absolutely bonkers open-world series. Grand Theft Auto VI is said to offer a more obsessively dense map, more realism in details like weather and passing time, and more realistic NPCs (non-player characters) than ever before. Here’s hoping those 13 years were worth the wait. Open-style earbuds aren’t just for the sporty; they’re an entirely different way to listen that keeps you environmentally aware without the plugged-up feeling of traditional buds. The OpenFit Pro take a balanced approach, with seamless open-ear performance and even a touch of noise reduction to dampen the din on crowded commutes. The old Ironman Timex was a staple for ’80s and ’90s kids, and while you can’t bring back those carefree days, remakes like the Retroware can bring back that carefree feeling. No smarts, no notifications, just a takes-a-licking Timex watch with tactile keys, 50 meters of water resistance, and totally tubular digital graphics. Serious gamers need a serious controller, and few take gaming more seriously than 8BitDo’s Elite-style Xbox gamepad. From its drift-proof TMR joysticks and motion support to its customizable buttons and remappable bumpers, the Ultimate 3E is the gift for that lovable control freak in your life. There’s regular Play-Doh for kids, but did you know that Play-Doh makes kits for adults, too? We’re not scoffing. The new Blooms sets take on Lego’s floral bouquets with more realistic-looking flower arrangements, and they include a vase. They’re equal parts nostalgic kitsch and stylish decor. For on-the-go creators, it’s all about capturing the moment in the highest video quality possible. Insta360’s Luna Pro steadycam offers plenty of features to get the job done right, including 4K vertical video, swift file transfers, four hours of battery life, and a detachable touchscreen that doubles as a remote. The new Fitbit Air provides the same great fitness tracking we’ve come to expect in a comfortable design that virtually disappears on your wrist. Google’s AI Coach can be overly assertive, but the tracker’s great battery life and metrics for everything from sleep to blood oxygen make it an excellent gift for anyone who needs a healthy hand. Most mobile controllers have a serious size limit. Not Razer’s Kishi V3 Pro XL, which lets you throw a big ol’ tablet between the handles for a major visual upgrade. It also has high-quality joysticks, great grips, and customizable keys for USB-C tablets, along with haptics for Android models. So what if you’ve heard “Golden” more times than you can count? Netflix’s massive animated hit is a lot easier to gift now that it’s officially available on 4K Blu-ray disc. The story about three pop stars who band together to save humanity from a demonic boy band is an instant classic, with fantastic music and striking animation. If you’re contemplating a pricey pair of sleep buds for your loved one, we urge you to halt and consider a softer (and cheaper) alternative. Piercing pillows, designed with pockets for freshly pierced ears, also work great for regular earbuds. Blissbury’s comfy and adjustable Ear Pillow is our favorite. Problem — and sleep issues — solved. We all do it: pay a ton for a monthly streaming service for just a few series. It’s better to own the real thing, and Hacks , a hilarious drama that follows a comedian (Jean Smart) and her young writer (Hannah Einbinder) in the tumultuous “biz,” is one of HBO’s best series in years. Hoto’s soldering iron is super cool — and by that we mean hot, as it’s able to reach nearly 400 degrees Fahrenheit in about three seconds. The cordless, adjustable iron makes the perfect gift for your favorite DIYer, especially since it features customizable presets for virtually any job. For the person on your list whose hatred for smart glasses runs deep, Knockaround’s hip, tech-free sunglasses should hit the spot. They’re available in a variety of fun styles and offer lightweight frames and polarized lenses, with both UVA and UVB shielding for attractive eye protection. For the coffee or tea lover in your life who’s always headed to the microwave for a heat zap, Ember’s fancy-schmancy smart mug is a luxurious way to keep things toasty. With the ability to set the temperature on the mug or in the app, the Mug 3 makes it simple to keep liquids perfectly hot indefinitely. Not all reusable water bottles are created equal. Give the gift of a narrow-mouthed bottle, like this 16-ounce Nalgene pick, which makes it easy to take measured sips on the go. Take this advice from someone (me) who bought the wide-mouthed version and regularly spills water all over themself. If your giftee is into New York City memorabilia or wants a more unique way to light up a room, this cube-shaped lamp, designed around the old MTA entrance beacons, is sure to delight. Locals will recognize the vintage symbol, which still survives in the wild, and everyone will dig the old-school vibe. Sure. You could put iced tea in them, but no one’s stopping you from sipping pulpy OJ or rich chocolate milk from Kinto’s stylish glassware, which was crafted with an “uninterfering design” in mind. Needless to say, a full set makes a lovely addition to any minimalist’s ensemble. The hippest thing in audio right now is… the hippest thing from a long time ago. Enter the modded iPod Classic from Player Mods, which refreshes Apple’s media player with some 21st-century upgrades. The 5th-gen model can be customized with several color options (including a transparent case) and up to 2TB of storage. For those tired of experiencing Joy-Con drift with their Nintendo Switch (or stick drift on any controller), there’s the TT Pro. Loaded with the latest anti-drift tech for joysticks and customizable triggers that let picky gamers have it their way, GuliKit’s customizable wireless controllers work with PlayStation, Nintendo, PC, iOS, and Android devices. The Pocket Scion is unlike any musical instrument you’ve witnessed before, one that uses the “biofeedback” from plants to trigger built-in synths. The device offers MIDI-out to send digital signals to outboard synths, and it includes an app for both macOS and Windows, finally giving you a way to make your favorite fern a rockstar. Your favorite gamer needs an awesome monitor, but there are 10 billion options. Alienware’s 34-inch Penta Tandem QD-OLED delivers top-end picture quality, with vibrant colors and perfect blacks, plus a swift 280Hz refresh rate. Best of all, it’s not nearly as expensive as you might think. Few devices evoke more sheer nostalgic joy than Sony’s OG PlayStation console from ’94. If you know a gamer, Lego’s latest replica brings it all flooding back with several brick-ified details, including a pop-up hinge, a gamepad, and a number of hidden surprises waiting to be discovered. For those in smaller dwellings, efficient living means maximizing space. That’s where combo appliances like Ninja’s newest microwave / air fryer combo come in. The handy countertop gadget lets you zap your food, then crisp it at the end so your pizza or French fries don’t turn into a soggy mess.

Perhaps no game in history is more anticipated than the latest entry in Rockstar’s sprawling, intricate, and absolutely bonkers open-world series. Grand Theft Auto VI is said to offer a more obsessively dense map, more realism in details like weather and passing time, and more realistic NPCs (non-player characters) than ever before. Here’s hoping those 13 years were worth the wait.

Open-style earbuds aren’t just for the sporty; they’re an entirely different way to listen that keeps you environmentally aware without the plugged-up feeling of traditional buds. The OpenFit Pro take a balanced approach, with seamless open-ear performance and even a touch of noise reduction to dampen the din on crowded commutes.

The old Ironman Timex was a staple for ’80s and ’90s kids, and while you can’t bring back those carefree days, remakes like the Retroware can bring back that carefree feeling. No smarts, no notifications, just a takes-a-licking Timex watch with tactile keys, 50 meters of water resistance, and totally tubular digital graphics.

Serious gamers need a serious controller, and few take gaming more seriously than 8BitDo’s Elite-style Xbox gamepad. From its drift-proof TMR joysticks and motion support to its customizable buttons and remappable bumpers, the Ultimate 3E is the gift for that lovable control freak in your life.

There’s regular Play-Doh for kids, but did you know that Play-Doh makes kits for adults, too? We’re not scoffing. The new Blooms sets take on Lego’s floral bouquets with more realistic-looking flower arrangements, and they include a vase. They’re equal parts nostalgic kitsch and stylish decor.

For on-the-go creators, it’s all about capturing the moment in the highest video quality possible. Insta360’s Luna Pro steadycam offers plenty of features to get the job done right, including 4K vertical video, swift file transfers, four hours of battery life, and a detachable touchscreen that doubles as a remote.

The new Fitbit Air provides the same great fitness tracking we’ve come to expect in a comfortable design that virtually disappears on your wrist. Google’s AI Coach can be overly assertive, but the tracker’s great battery life and metrics for everything from sleep to blood oxygen make it an excellent gift for anyone who needs a healthy hand.

Most mobile controllers have a serious size limit. Not Razer’s Kishi V3 Pro XL, which lets you throw a big ol’ tablet between the handles for a major visual upgrade. It also has high-quality joysticks, great grips, and customizable keys for USB-C tablets, along with haptics for Android models.

So what if you’ve heard “Golden” more times than you can count? Netflix’s massive animated hit is a lot easier to gift now that it’s officially available on 4K Blu-ray disc. The story about three pop stars who band together to save humanity from a demonic boy band is an instant classic, with fantastic music and striking animation.

If you’re contemplating a pricey pair of sleep buds for your loved one, we urge you to halt and consider a softer (and cheaper) alternative. Piercing pillows, designed with pockets for freshly pierced ears, also work great for regular earbuds. Blissbury’s comfy and adjustable Ear Pillow is our favorite. Problem — and sleep issues — solved.

We all do it: pay a ton for a monthly streaming service for just a few series. It’s better to own the real thing, and Hacks , a hilarious drama that follows a comedian (Jean Smart) and her young writer (Hannah Einbinder) in the tumultuous “biz,” is one of HBO’s best series in years.

Hoto’s soldering iron is super cool — and by that we mean hot, as it’s able to reach nearly 400 degrees Fahrenheit in about three seconds. The cordless, adjustable iron makes the perfect gift for your favorite DIYer, especially since it features customizable presets for virtually any job.

For the person on your list whose hatred for smart glasses runs deep, Knockaround’s hip, tech-free sunglasses should hit the spot. They’re available in a variety of fun styles and offer lightweight frames and polarized lenses, with both UVA and UVB shielding for attractive eye protection.

For the coffee or tea lover in your life who’s always headed to the microwave for a heat zap, Ember’s fancy-schmancy smart mug is a luxurious way to keep things toasty. With the ability to set the temperature on the mug or in the app, the Mug 3 makes it simple to keep liquids perfectly hot indefinitely.

Not all reusable water bottles are created equal. Give the gift of a narrow-mouthed bottle, like this 16-ounce Nalgene pick, which makes it easy to take measured sips on the go. Take this advice from someone (me) who bought the wide-mouthed version and regularly spills water all over themself.

If your giftee is into New York City memorabilia or wants a more unique way to light up a room, this cube-shaped lamp, designed around the old MTA entrance beacons, is sure to delight. Locals will recognize the vintage symbol, which still survives in the wild, and everyone will dig the old-school vibe.

Sure. You could put iced tea in them, but no one’s stopping you from sipping pulpy OJ or rich chocolate milk from Kinto’s stylish glassware, which was crafted with an “uninterfering design” in mind. Needless to say, a full set makes a lovely addition to any minimalist’s ensemble.

The hippest thing in audio right now is… the hippest thing from a long time ago. Enter the modded iPod Classic from Player Mods, which refreshes Apple’s media player with some 21st-century upgrades. The 5th-gen model can be customized with several color options (including a transparent case) and up to 2TB of storage.

For those tired of experiencing Joy-Con drift with their Nintendo Switch (or stick drift on any controller), there’s the TT Pro. Loaded with the latest anti-drift tech for joysticks and customizable triggers that let picky gamers have it their way, GuliKit’s customizable wireless controllers work with PlayStation, Nintendo, PC, iOS, and Android devices.

The Pocket Scion is unlike any musical instrument you’ve witnessed before, one that uses the “biofeedback” from plants to trigger built-in synths. The device offers MIDI-out to send digital signals to outboard synths, and it includes an app for both macOS and Windows, finally giving you a way to make your favorite fern a rockstar.

Your favorite gamer needs an awesome monitor, but there are 10 billion options. Alienware’s 34-inch Penta Tandem QD-OLED delivers top-end picture quality, with vibrant colors and perfect blacks, plus a swift 280Hz refresh rate. Best of all, it’s not nearly as expensive as you might think.

Few devices evoke more sheer nostalgic joy than Sony’s OG PlayStation console from ’94. If you know a gamer, Lego’s latest replica brings it all flooding back with several brick-ified details, including a pop-up hinge, a gamepad, and a number of hidden surprises waiting to be discovered.

extraction.body: With Christmas creeping ever closer, Disney has unveiled a selection of gifts for adults that bring together some of the biggest names from its much-loved worlds, including Mickey Mouse, Winnie the Pooh, Marvel and Star Wars. Whether you’re shopping for a Disney fan, a Marvel collector or someone who simply loves a cosy Christmas gift, the Disney Holiday 2026 collection features plenty of options for him and her. From practical travel accessories and slippers to collectible LEGO sets, books and fitness bundles, here are some of the standout Disney gifts to add to your Christmas shopping list. For the Disney fan who is always planning their next getaway, the Mickey Magic 55cm Cabin Luggage Bag combines practical travel design with a classic Mickey Mouse look. Priced at £99, the cabin-sized suitcase comes from American Tourister and is a fun way to bring a little Disney magic to your next trip. For a more relaxed present, the Disney Winnie the Pooh Piglet Inspired Candle makes a cosy addition to any Christmas gift pile. Priced at £19, the candle is available through Amazon . Give the gift of cosy feet this Christmas with the Skinnydip Disney Mickey Bow Slippers , priced at £24 . The playful Mickey-inspired design is ideal for Disney fans looking for something practical while still bringing a little character to their winter wardrobe. Winnie the Pooh fans can also cosy up with the Skinnydip Disney Winnie the Pooh Slippers , also priced at £24 . They’re another easy Christmas gift option for anyone who would rather spend the festive season relaxing at home. Beauty lovers can add some Hundred Acre Wood inspiration to their makeup collection with the Winnie the Pooh Eyeshadow Palette from Mad Beauty . Also launching on 1 September, it’s a charming winter accessory for keeping warm during those colder evenings. For something a little more practical, the Disney Tile Tracker – Mickey & Friends combines Disney characters with everyday tech. Priced at £24.99, the tracker comes from Life360 and is designed to help keep track of important belongings. The books are available from all good book retailers, making them an easy addition to a Star Wars-themed Christmas gift. Fitness fans can channel their inner Hulk with the Myprotein Marvel Bundle – Hulk , priced at £48.49 . The Marvel-themed bundle combines the world of superheroes with Myprotein , making it a potential gift for gym-goers and Marvel fans alike. Prefer Spider-Man to the Hulk? The Myprotein Marvel Bundle – Spider-Man is another option at £48.49 . For the ultimate Star Wars fan, the Mandalorian & Grogu Darts Set offers something a little different. Priced at £299.95 , the set brings characters from The Mandalorian into a full-sized entertainment gift and is available through Amazon. From Winnie the Pooh and Mickey Mouse to Marvel and Star Wars, the Disney Holiday 2026 range offers plenty of options for adult fans, whether you’re looking for something cosy, practical, collectible or a little more extravagant. With prices starting at £14.99 , there are gifts to suit a range of budgets — while some of the larger statement pieces could make particularly memorable presents for dedicated Disney, Marvel and Star Wars fans. For more products from the Disney Holiday 2026 range, shoppers can explore the official Disney image bank and retailer websites linked above.
