Megaspeed's addition to the Commerce Department's entity list bars U.S. tech companies from providing goods, software and technology to Megaspeed without receiving a license. The Singapore-based company specializes in providing computing power for data centers training AI models. Nvidia's website lists Megaspeed as a preferred cloud partner. The company's addition to the Commerce Department's entity list comes after former executive Alice Huang, who is alleged to be a spy for Beijing, had an extramarital relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who was reinstated to his role on Monday. SHORT SELLER FLAGGED JENSEN HUANG'S 'UNCOMFORTABLY CLOSE' TIES TO ALLEGED CHINESE SPY MONTHS AGO Megaspeed previously faced an investigation by the U.S. government as regulators probed whether the company was helping Chinese customers obtain advanced AI chips made by Nvidia that are covered by export controls. FOX Business reached out to Megaspeed and the Commerce Department for comment. The Commerce Department and Justice Department released a joint statement on Nov. 16 explaining that Commerce opened its probe into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations. WHAT JENSEN HUANG'S RETURN MEANS FOR NVIDIA – AND WALL STREET In May 2025, the agency's investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed, and a month later, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list. Also in June 2025, agents from Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security worked with Singaporean law enforcement officials to conduct an onsite, in-person end-use check at Megaspeed and interviewed Alice Huang, who was CEO at the time. Following those actions, the Justice Department took the lead in a criminal investigation of Megaspeed and the agencies are working together to "bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred." Bringing Huang back before that investigation ends reads as a message to shareholders that the board decided it would not wait for the final report, and it leaves the question that cost him the job 12 days ago still open. The limit of that reading is the board’s own account: it voted unanimously, it said it was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA,” and it said input from “senior levels of the United States government” left it confident his return “poses no national security risk.” Is NVIDIA a Buy After Jensen Huang's Departure? Six days ago the board’s chair, Harvey Jones, said the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” President Trump urged the board to rehire Huang early Monday, The Washington Post reported, and Nvidia’s release followed at 8:55 a.m. ET. Besides the job title, the release makes three changes. A new board committee. Nvidia is forming a National Security and Export Control Committee made up of independent directors. Export rules already decide which chips Nvidia may sell in China, and that subject now gets its own group of directors. For shareholders, the thing to watch is who sits on it. A chief compliance officer, still to be hired. Nvidia is searching for a new chief compliance officer who will report to the board’s Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. Jones said on Nov. 17 that Huang resigned “after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” The person who enforces that code will now answer to directors. Until someone takes the job, it is a promise. An investigation with no verdict yet. A committee of independent directors is examining reporting that Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The release says that work continues “to conclusion” and that Huang supports it and will cooperate. Nvidia also said it “will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.” Reuters reported on Nov. 20 that Securities and Exchange Commission enforcement staff were examining potential accounting issues at the company, which we covered that day in “Nvidia Stock Just Lost $900 Billion in Its Worst Week Since 2008.” An inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing. Six months later the audit committee concluded that four fiscal years of results “should no longer be relied upon.” Dell spent $260 million on the investigations over two fiscal years. A look at contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket tied to the company’s next CEO reveals an abrupt swing from long shots to near certainties when the board reinstated him Monday morning.

Trump made such a post on Truth Social on Sunday night, and the contract was resolved.

Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday in a stunning reversal that comes less than two weeks after his shocking resignation amid a sex scandal involving a suspected Chinese spy, sending shares of the chipmaking giant soaring 34%. The company’s board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive and a director after receiving input from senior US government officials that left directors confident his return posed no national security risk. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” board chairman Harvey Jones said in a statement. “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said, adding: “I can’t wait to get back to work.” Nvidia said its independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation would continue despite his reinstatement. President Trump hailed Huang’s reinstatement Monday, declaring that Nvidia’s board had made the “correct and proper decision” and calling the billionaire executive a “Great Patriot and National Treasure.” “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the US government had no reason to believe Huang’s return posed a national security threat. “The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct,” Trump added, while urging Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with US export controls. Nvidia’s stunning reversal came without consulting the company’s senior executives, who learned of the decision to reinstate Huang only at the last minute, Bloomberg reported Monday , citing people familiar with the matter. The board reached its decision Sunday afternoon following pressure from President Trump, according to the report. Interim CEO Colette Kress and other top executives were excluded from the discussions, which unfolded over just a few hours. Complicating the search for Huang’s replacement, some prospective candidates had already withdrawn themselves from consideration, Bloomberg reported. Nvidia announced Huang’s comeback shortly before markets opened Monday, upending preparations for the company’s annual developer conference in Washington next week. The event, which executives had been planning without their longtime boss, is now expected to showcase his return. Huang’s reinstatement comes amid fresh r evelations about his affair with Alice Huang , a Chinese businesswoman who was in contact with an officer of Beijing’s top spy agency while romantically involved with the Nvidia founder, according to a New York Times report. US intelligence agencies determined that Alice Huang, who is no relation to the billionaire executive, maintained contact with an official from China’s Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 until fall 2026, a period that overlapped with their affair, the report said. American intelligence also uncovered evidence that her business partner, Kang Wei , whom she reportedly introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency, raising suspicions that Jensen Huang had been targeted in an espionage operation. The pair have also come under scrutiny over their alleged involvement in a network of Southeast Asian companies, including Singapore-based Megaspeed , suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of US export restrictions. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing, while Beijing has dismissed the espionage allegations as unfounded. Trump was briefed about Alice Huang’s suspected intelligence ties as early as June 2025, according to the report, but has publicly questioned whether she was a spy. The president repeatedly urged Nvidia to bring Jensen Huang back , arguing that the company and the American economy needed his leadership. The scandal deepened after revelations that Huang had also been romantically involved with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reportedly answered directly to him, according to the Times. The pair were spotted behaving affectionately during Nvidia’s annual developer conference in San Jose in March, the newspaper reported. Axios separately reported that Huang’s security team allegedly offered a nondisclosure agreement to a bystander who recorded an interaction between the two. Wall Street analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives said Nvidia’s board had little choice but to bring Huang back, arguing that losing the billionaire founder posed a greater threat to shareholders than the controversy surrounding his departure. “At the end of the day despite this Jensen saga the Board knew it had no choice but to bring him back,” Ives wrote in a Monday research note, citing Huang’s critical relationships with suppliers, major AI customers and technology partners. Ives said Nvidia could be worth $300 a share with Huang at the helm, compared with $225 without him, underscoring the importance investors place on his leadership of the chipmaking giant. Nevertheless, the analyst maintained his official $225 price target and “Outperform” rating, warning that the company’s internal investigation, government inquiries and unresolved questions about compliance with US export controls remain significant obstacles.

Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday in a stunning reversal that comes less than two weeks after his shocking resignation amid a sex scandal involving a suspected Chinese spy, sending shares of the chipmaking giant soaring 34%.

The company’s board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive and a director after receiving input from senior US government officials that left directors confident his return posed no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” board chairman Harvey Jones said in a statement.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said, adding: “I can’t wait to get back to work.” Nvidia said its independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation would continue despite his reinstatement.

President Trump hailed Huang’s reinstatement Monday, declaring that Nvidia’s board had made the “correct and proper decision” and calling the billionaire executive a “Great Patriot and National Treasure.”

“The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the US government had no reason to believe Huang’s return posed a national security threat.

“The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct,” Trump added, while urging Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with US export controls.

Nvidia’s stunning reversal came without consulting the company’s senior executives, who learned of the decision to reinstate Huang only at the last minute, Bloomberg reported Monday , citing people familiar with the matter.

The board reached its decision Sunday afternoon following pressure from President Trump, according to the report. Interim CEO Colette Kress and other top executives were excluded from the discussions, which unfolded over just a few hours.
Complicating the search for Huang’s replacement, some prospective candidates had already withdrawn themselves from consideration, Bloomberg reported.
Nvidia announced Huang’s comeback shortly before markets opened Monday, upending preparations for the company’s annual developer conference in Washington next week.
The event, which executives had been planning without their longtime boss, is now expected to showcase his return.

Huang’s reinstatement comes amid fresh r evelations about his affair with Alice Huang , a Chinese businesswoman who was in contact with an officer of Beijing’s top spy agency while romantically involved with the Nvidia founder, according to a New York Times report.

US intelligence agencies determined that Alice Huang, who is no relation to the billionaire executive, maintained contact with an official from China’s Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 until fall 2026, a period that overlapped with their affair, the report said.

American intelligence also uncovered evidence that her business partner, Kang Wei , whom she reportedly introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency, raising suspicions that Jensen Huang had been targeted in an espionage operation.

The pair have also come under scrutiny over their alleged involvement in a network of Southeast Asian companies, including Singapore-based Megaspeed , suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of US export restrictions. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing, while Beijing has dismissed the espionage allegations as unfounded.
Trump was briefed about Alice Huang’s suspected intelligence ties as early as June 2025, according to the report, but has publicly questioned whether she was a spy.
The president repeatedly urged Nvidia to bring Jensen Huang back , arguing that the company and the American economy needed his leadership.

The scandal deepened after revelations that Huang had also been romantically involved with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reportedly answered directly to him, according to the Times.
The pair were spotted behaving affectionately during Nvidia’s annual developer conference in San Jose in March, the newspaper reported.
Axios separately reported that Huang’s security team allegedly offered a nondisclosure agreement to a bystander who recorded an interaction between the two.

Wall Street analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives said Nvidia’s board had little choice but to bring Huang back, arguing that losing the billionaire founder posed a greater threat to shareholders than the controversy surrounding his departure.

“At the end of the day despite this Jensen saga the Board knew it had no choice but to bring him back,” Ives wrote in a Monday research note, citing Huang’s critical relationships with suppliers, major AI customers and technology partners.
Ives said Nvidia could be worth $300 a share with Huang at the helm, compared with $225 without him, underscoring the importance investors place on his leadership of the chipmaking giant.

Nevertheless, the analyst maintained his official $225 price target and “Outperform” rating, warning that the company’s internal investigation, government inquiries and unresolved questions about compliance with US export controls remain significant obstacles.

extraction.body: Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO on Monday morning, and the same press release says the board’s investigation of him will continue “to conclusion.” The stock was at about $163 in the first minutes of trading, up about 30% from Friday’s close of $125.53. Bringing Huang back before that investigation ends reads as a message to shareholders that the board decided it would not wait for the final report, and it leaves the question that cost him the job 12 days ago still open. The limit of that reading is the board’s own account: it voted unanimously, it said it was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA,” and it said input from “senior levels of the United States government” left it confident his return “poses no national security risk.” Is NVIDIA a Buy After Jensen Huang's Departure? Plus 3 New Buys and the RSI Race Heats Up Take a retiree who has held 1,000 Nvidia shares for years. The shares were worth $239,240 at the record close on Oct. 6 and $125,530 on Friday. At $163 they are worth about $163,000, which puts about $38,000 back in one morning and leaves the account about $76,000 below the record. Six days ago the board’s chair, Harvey Jones, said the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” President Trump urged the board to rehire Huang early Monday, The Washington Post reported, and Nvidia’s release followed at 8:55 a.m. ET. Besides the job title, the release makes three changes. A new board committee. Nvidia is forming a National Security and Export Control Committee made up of independent directors. Export rules already decide which chips Nvidia may sell in China, and that subject now gets its own group of directors. For shareholders, the thing to watch is who sits on it. A chief compliance officer, still to be hired. Nvidia is searching for a new chief compliance officer who will report to the board’s Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. Jones said on Nov. 17 that Huang resigned “after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” The person who enforces that code will now answer to directors. Until someone takes the job, it is a promise. An investigation with no verdict yet. A committee of independent directors is examining reporting that Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The release says that work continues “to conclusion” and that Huang supports it and will cooperate. Nvidia also said it “will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.” Reuters reported on Nov. 20 that Securities and Exchange Commission enforcement staff were examining potential accounting issues at the company, which we covered that day in “Nvidia Stock Just Lost $900 Billion in Its Worst Week Since 2008.” An inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing. So the holder with 1,000 shares owns a company with its founder back and two sets of unanswered questions: the board’s and the government’s. I looked for public companies where a former boss returned while an investigation was still running. Three fit. Each stock move is measured from the last close before the news of the return. Dell. Michael Dell took back the CEO job on Jan. 31, 2007, with an SEC inquiry from 2005 and an audit committee investigation from 2006 both open. The stock closed at $24.22 that day and rose about 4% after hours on the news. Six months later the audit committee concluded that four fiscal years of results “should no longer be relied upon.” Dell spent $260 million on the investigations over two fiscal years. In the last weeks of the fiscal year that ended Feb. 1, 2008, the company was buying back its own shares at an average of $21.39, about 12% below the price on the day he returned. The SEC case ended in July 2010, about three and a half years after his return. Dell paid $100 million and Michael Dell paid $4 million, neither admitting nor denying the SEC’s claims, and he kept the job. WWE. Vince McMahon retired in July 2022 during a board investigation of payments he had made. In December 2022 the board told him a return “would not be prudent from a shareholder value perspective” while SEC and federal prosecutors’ investigations were pending. He controlled the vote and put himself back on the board on Jan. 6, 2023. The stock rose 17% that day and stood 40% higher when WWE merged into TKO eight months later, against 18% for the S&P 500 fund (SPY). McMahon resigned from TKO in January 2024, a day after a former employee sued him. The SEC case ended in January 2025, two years after his return, with McMahon paying about $1.7 million. His lawyer said in February 2025 that federal prosecutors had dropped their investigation. UnitedHealth. Stephen Hemsley, CEO from 2006 to 2017, returned on May 13, 2025, the day the company suspended its 2025 forecast. The stock fell 18% that day. The next day The Wall Street Journal reported a Justice Department criminal investigation of the company’s Medicare Advantage business, and in July 2025 UnitedHealth said it was complying with criminal and civil requests from the department. The stock hit its low on Aug. 1, 2025, 37% below its level before Hemsley’s return. On Friday, 18 months on, it was still 10% below that level, while the S&P 500 fund gained 18%. I found no announcement that the investigations have ended. The three cases share one thing. The investigation outlasted the first reaction by a long way: two years at WWE, about three and a half at Dell, and 18 months and counting at UnitedHealth. One of the three stocks was above its starting price at the last reading. Three cases are a small sample, and none of them involved a national security question. Monday’s jump prices in Huang’s return. The open items come later. Three answers will show how the risk is closing: who the board names to the new committee, who it hires as compliance chief, and whether the investigation’s conclusion is made public. passages: Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO on Monday morning, and the same press release says the board’s investigation of him will continue “to conclusion.” The stock was at about $163 in the first minutes of trading, up about 30% from Friday’s close of $125.53.

Bringing Huang back before that investigation ends reads as a message to shareholders that the board decided it would not wait for the final report, and it leaves the question that cost him the job 12 days ago still open. The limit of that reading is the board’s own account: it voted unanimously, it said it was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA,” and it said input from “senior levels of the United States government” left it confident his return “poses no national security risk.”
Is NVIDIA a Buy After Jensen Huang's Departure? Plus 3 New Buys and the RSI Race Heats Up

Take a retiree who has held 1,000 Nvidia shares for years. The shares were worth $239,240 at the record close on Oct. 6 and $125,530 on Friday. At $163 they are worth about $163,000, which puts about $38,000 back in one morning and leaves the account about $76,000 below the record.

Six days ago the board’s chair, Harvey Jones, said the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” President Trump urged the board to rehire Huang early Monday, The Washington Post reported, and Nvidia’s release followed at 8:55 a.m. ET.
Besides the job title, the release makes three changes.

A new board committee. Nvidia is forming a National Security and Export Control Committee made up of independent directors. Export rules already decide which chips Nvidia may sell in China, and that subject now gets its own group of directors. For shareholders, the thing to watch is who sits on it.

A chief compliance officer, still to be hired. Nvidia is searching for a new chief compliance officer who will report to the board’s Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. Jones said on Nov. 17 that Huang resigned “after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” The person who enforces that code will now answer to directors. Until someone takes the job, it is a promise.

An investigation with no verdict yet. A committee of independent directors is examining reporting that Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The release says that work continues “to conclusion” and that Huang supports it and will cooperate. Nvidia also said it “will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.” Reuters reported on Nov. 20 that Securities and Exchange Commission enforcement staff were examining potential accounting issues at the company, which we covered that day in “Nvidia Stock Just Lost $900 Billion in Its Worst Week Since 2008.” An inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing.
So the holder with 1,000 shares owns a company with its founder back and two sets of unanswered questions: the board’s and the government’s.
I looked for public companies where a former boss returned while an investigation was still running. Three fit. Each stock move is measured from the last close before the news of the return.

Dell. Michael Dell took back the CEO job on Jan. 31, 2007, with an SEC inquiry from 2005 and an audit committee investigation from 2006 both open. The stock closed at $24.22 that day and rose about 4% after hours on the news. Six months later the audit committee concluded that four fiscal years of results “should no longer be relied upon.” Dell spent $260 million on the investigations over two fiscal years. In the last weeks of the fiscal year that ended Feb. 1, 2008, the company was buying back its own shares at an average of $21.39, about 12% below the price on the day he returned. The SEC case ended in July 2010, about three and a half years after his return. Dell paid $100 million and Michael Dell paid $4 million, neither admitting nor denying the SEC’s claims, and he kept the job.

WWE. Vince McMahon retired in July 2022 during a board investigation of payments he had made. In December 2022 the board told him a return “would not be prudent from a shareholder value perspective” while SEC and federal prosecutors’ investigations were pending. He controlled the vote and put himself back on the board on Jan. 6, 2023. The stock rose 17% that day and stood 40% higher when WWE merged into TKO eight months later, against 18% for the S&P 500 fund (SPY). McMahon resigned from TKO in January 2024, a day after a former employee sued him. The SEC case ended in January 2025, two years after his return, with McMahon paying about $1.7 million. His lawyer said in February 2025 that federal prosecutors had dropped their investigation.

UnitedHealth. Stephen Hemsley, CEO from 2006 to 2017, returned on May 13, 2025, the day the company suspended its 2025 forecast. The stock fell 18% that day. The next day The Wall Street Journal reported a Justice Department criminal investigation of the company’s Medicare Advantage business, and in July 2025 UnitedHealth said it was complying with criminal and civil requests from the department. The stock hit its low on Aug. 1, 2025, 37% below its level before Hemsley’s return. On Friday, 18 months on, it was still 10% below that level, while the S&P 500 fund gained 18%. I found no announcement that the investigations have ended.

The three cases share one thing. The investigation outlasted the first reaction by a long way: two years at WWE, about three and a half at Dell, and 18 months and counting at UnitedHealth. One of the three stocks was above its starting price at the last reading. Three cases are a small sample, and none of them involved a national security question.

Monday’s jump prices in Huang’s return. The open items come later. Three answers will show how the risk is closing: who the board names to the new committee, who it hires as compliance chief, and whether the investigation’s conclusion is made public.

Those answers will arrive after this story, and The Daily Profit, our free weekday email, will follow each one as it lands, alongside Eric Bleeker’s $1 million AI Investor Portfolio. Get it free here , along with our Top 10 Stocks to Buy Right Now report.

For the retiree with 1,000 shares, the question is size. A position that was worth $125,530 on Friday and about $163,000 early Monday can swing a retirement account by itself. A day when the price is up 30% is a calmer day to decide how much of a retirement account should ride on one company with an investigation still running.

Nvidia has its founder back, and the board has said in writing that its investigation is unfinished, that a new committee will oversee national security and export rules, and that a compliance chief is still to be hired. At Dell, WWE and UnitedHealth, the open investigation ran from 18 months to three and a half years after the boss returned, and one of the three stocks finished above its starting price. sources.title: Prediction markets put Jensen Huang’s odds of returning at 11% on Sunday night—hours later he was back as Nvidia CEO - Fortune
passages: Prediction markets have proved prescient when it comes to forecasting elections and other events, but in the case of Jensen Huang’s abrupt return as Nvidia’s CEO, they appeared as much in the dark as everyone else.
A look at contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket tied to the company’s next CEO reveals an abrupt swing from long shots to near certainties when the board reinstated him Monday morning.
As of Sunday evening, Nvidia insider Ian Buck led with roughly 13%, followed by Huang at roughly 11%, with finance chief Colette Kress and former Apple CEO Tim Cook trailing.
By early Monday morning, Huang’s odds had risen to roughly 19%.
They then jumped to 97% when Nvidia confirmed his reinstatement.
Another contract, on whether President Donald Trump would publicly call for Huang’s reinstatement, drew more than $330,000 in volume.
Bettors gave it a 38% chance of happening before January 2027 and a 20% chance before December 2026.
Trump made such a post on Truth Social on Sunday night, and the contract was resolved.
The odds for the January window jumped to 83% and those for the December window to 74%.
Because the call came before December, both contracts paid out on “yes.”
A third option, that Huang would return, was trading at about 16% before the news broke.
But the Nvidia outcome, where the platforms’ odds diverged significantly from reality, has weakened that case.

A look at contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket tied to the company’s next CEO reveals an abrupt swing from long shots to near certainties when the board reinstated him Monday morning. One Kalshi contract on whether Nvidia’s next CEO would be an internal or external hire drew nearly $100,000 in trading volume. At 5 a.m., traders gave an external hire roughly 57% odds and an internal one roughly 33%. A third option, that Huang would return, was trading at about 16% before the news broke. Traders then piled in, and it jumped to nearly 100% within minutes. Another contract, on whether President Donald Trump would publicly call for Huang’s reinstatement, drew more than $330,000 in volume. Bettors gave it a 38% chance of happening before January 2027 and a 20% chance before December 2026. They were wrong on both counts. Trump made such a post on Truth Social on Sunday night, and the contract was resolved. The odds for the January window jumped to 83% and those for the December window to 74%. Because the call came before December, both contracts paid out on “yes.” Polymarket saw even heavier trading. A contract on who would be Nvidia’s next CEO topped $11 million in volume. As of Sunday evening, Nvidia insider Ian Buck led with roughly 13%, followed by Huang at roughly 11%, with finance chief Colette Kress and former Apple CEO Tim Cook trailing. By early Monday morning, Huang’s odds had risen to roughly 19%. They then jumped to 97% when Nvidia confirmed his reinstatement. The misses come as prediction markets face growing attention over how well they forecast events, even as their popularity climbs. The platforms pitch themselves as a reference point for future events. Their case grew stronger after the 2024 election, when they called Trump’s return to the White House more accurately than traditional polls and surveys. Their most recent redemption came in this month’s midterms , when Kalshi and Polymarket correctly forecasted that Democrats would take control of both chambers of Congress. The platforms also called most House and Senate races correctly. But the Nvidia outcome, where the platforms’ odds diverged significantly from reality, has weakened that case. It wasn’t the first time they got an outcome wrong. During the midterms, prediction markets failed to foresee surprise victories like Democrat Annie Andrews’s win over Republican incumbent Darline Graham in South Carolina’s Senate race, and Democrat Gina Hinojosa’s win over Republican incumbent Greg Abbott in the Texas governor’s race. Before that, the markets also favored Flávio Bolsonaro over incumbent Lula da Silva in Brazil’s presidential runoff, where Lula eventually won.

Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday in a stunning reversal that comes less than two weeks after his shocking resignation amid a sex scandal involving a suspected Chinese spy, sending shares of the chipmaking giant soaring 34%. The company’s board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive and a director after receiving input from senior US government officials that left directors confident his return posed no national security risk. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” board chairman Harvey Jones said in a statement. “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said, adding: “I can’t wait to get back to work.” Nvidia said its independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation would continue despite his reinstatement. President Trump hailed Huang’s reinstatement Monday, declaring that Nvidia’s board had made the “correct and proper decision” and calling the billionaire executive a “Great Patriot and National Treasure.” “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the US government had no reason to believe Huang’s return posed a national security threat. “The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct,” Trump added, while urging Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with US export controls. Nvidia’s stunning reversal came without consulting the company’s senior executives, who learned of the decision to reinstate Huang only at the last minute, Bloomberg reported Monday , citing people familiar with the matter. The board reached its decision Sunday afternoon following pressure from President Trump, according to the report. Interim CEO Colette Kress and other top executives were excluded from the discussions, which unfolded over just a few hours. Complicating the search for Huang’s replacement, some prospective candidates had already withdrawn themselves from consideration, Bloomberg reported. Nvidia announced Huang’s comeback shortly before markets opened Monday, upending preparations for the company’s annual developer conference in Washington next week. The event, which executives had been planning without their longtime boss, is now expected to showcase his return. Huang’s reinstatement comes amid fresh r evelations about his affair with Alice Huang , a Chinese businesswoman who was in contact with an officer of Beijing’s top spy agency while romantically involved with the Nvidia founder, according to a New York Times report. US intelligence agencies determined that Alice Huang, who is no relation to the billionaire executive, maintained contact with an official from China’s Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 until fall 2026, a period that overlapped with their affair, the report said. American intelligence also uncovered evidence that her business partner, Kang Wei , whom she reportedly introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency, raising suspicions that Jensen Huang had been targeted in an espionage operation. The pair have also come under scrutiny over their alleged involvement in a network of Southeast Asian companies, including Singapore-based Megaspeed , suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of US export restrictions. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing, while Beijing has dismissed the espionage allegations as unfounded. Trump was briefed about Alice Huang’s suspected intelligence ties as early as June 2025, according to the report, but has publicly questioned whether she was a spy. The president repeatedly urged Nvidia to bring Jensen Huang back , arguing that the company and the American economy needed his leadership. The scandal deepened after revelations that Huang had also been romantically involved with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reportedly answered directly to him, according to the Times. The pair were spotted behaving affectionately during Nvidia’s annual developer conference in San Jose in March, the newspaper reported. Axios separately reported that Huang’s security team allegedly offered a nondisclosure agreement to a bystander who recorded an interaction between the two. Wall Street analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives said Nvidia’s board had little choice but to bring Huang back, arguing that losing the billionaire founder posed a greater threat to shareholders than the controversy surrounding his departure. “At the end of the day despite this Jensen saga the Board knew it had no choice but to bring him back,” Ives wrote in a Monday research note, citing Huang’s critical relationships with suppliers, major AI customers and technology partners. Ives said Nvidia could be worth $300 a share with Huang at the helm, compared with $225 without him, underscoring the importance investors place on his leadership of the chipmaking giant. Nevertheless, the analyst maintained his official $225 price target and “Outperform” rating, warning that the company’s internal investigation, government inquiries and unresolved questions about compliance with US export controls remain significant obstacles.

American intelligence also uncovered evidence that her business partner, Kang Wei , whom she reportedly introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency, raising suspicions that Jensen Huang had been targeted in an espionage operation.

The pair have also come under scrutiny over their alleged involvement in a network of Southeast Asian companies, including Singapore-based Megaspeed , suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of US export restrictions. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing, while Beijing has dismissed the espionage allegations as unfounded.
Trump was briefed about Alice Huang’s suspected intelligence ties as early as June 2025, according to the report, but has publicly questioned whether she was a spy.
The president repeatedly urged Nvidia to bring Jensen Huang back , arguing that the company and the American economy needed his leadership.

The scandal deepened after revelations that Huang had also been romantically involved with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reportedly answered directly to him, according to the Times.
The pair were spotted behaving affectionately during Nvidia’s annual developer conference in San Jose in March, the newspaper reported.
Axios separately reported that Huang’s security team allegedly offered a nondisclosure agreement to a bystander who recorded an interaction between the two.

Wall Street analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives said Nvidia’s board had little choice but to bring Huang back, arguing that losing the billionaire founder posed a greater threat to shareholders than the controversy surrounding his departure.

“At the end of the day despite this Jensen saga the Board knew it had no choice but to bring him back,” Ives wrote in a Monday research note, citing Huang’s critical relationships with suppliers, major AI customers and technology partners.
Ives said Nvidia could be worth $300 a share with Huang at the helm, compared with $225 without him, underscoring the importance investors place on his leadership of the chipmaking giant.

Nevertheless, the analyst maintained his official $225 price target and “Outperform” rating, warning that the company’s internal investigation, government inquiries and unresolved questions about compliance with US export controls remain significant obstacles.

extraction.body: In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy. The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk. Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET. In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security. Trump also said the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity. A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement. The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.” Just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones said they didn’t intend to reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement. Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones said the board believes Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of its stockholders, employees, partners, and customers. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.” In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. passages: In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy.

The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk.
Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET.

In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security.
Trump also said the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity.

A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement.

The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.”

Just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones said they didn’t intend to reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement.

Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones said the board believes Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of its stockholders, employees, partners, and customers.

“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.”
In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”

The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk. Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET. In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security. Trump also said the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity. A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement. The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.” Just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones said they didn’t intend to reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement. Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones said the board believes Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of its stockholders, employees, partners, and customers. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.” In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) asked the administration to identify which officials had given Nvidia’s board input and what they had said.
She also called for answers from Huang and the board about compliance with U.S. export controls.
The New York Times had reported on allegations about Huang’s personal relationships, including one with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care.
The board’s continuing investigation concerns a separate question: whether a foreign intelligence operation targeted Huang.
Huang’s departure had rattled an industry that had come to identify Nvidia with its co-founder, Bourne wrote in a statement emailed to Observer.
Huang is back, but he’s still facing scrutiny outside the company.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress took over as interim CEO.
It traded between about $62,900 and $63,600 over the next 20 minutes, while Nvidia shares were up about 27% in premarket trading and Nasdaq 100 futures were up more than 6%.

Apple’s latest smartwatch, the 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 with Wi-Fi and GPS connectivity, has dropped to a new all-time low of $299 ($100 off) at Amazon and Walmart, beating its most sale price by $30. For example, the watch can alert you when it detects sounds like a doorbell, alarm, or even a baby’s cry, while other upcoming features like Live Rewind and Siri Recap lets you look back at a transcript of the previous 15 seconds of conversation and get a high-level overview of the conversations you had that day. The Series 12 also features redesigned health sensors that can now track your heart rate every five seconds even when you’re not exercising, which is particularly help if you have a chronic condition and need to keep a closer eye on your heart rate. It also introduces a new readiness score to help you decide how prepared your body is for the day. Other highlights include easier navigation with simple pinch gestures, and faster charging, which helps to make up for the fact that battery life is rated at up to 24 hours on a single charge, just like the previous-generation model. In our testing, the watch went from 20 to 64 percent charge in just 20 minutes, making it relatively easy to top up while showering or getting ready for the day. Update, November 23rd: Updated to reflect current deal pricing, which is $30 lower than when we last published this article.

extraction.body: President Donald Trump said Monday that he personally convinced Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, revealing his direct involvement in the chipmaker's stunning leadership reversal less than two weeks after its co-founder's resignation. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview. "And I convinced them." Trump said Nvidia's directors sought assurances about whether Huang's reinstatement posed a national security risk. "And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot," he said. The president also revealed that he spoke with Huang on Sunday night, before Nvidia announced his return. The remarks follow Semafor's reporting that Trump personally dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang's reinstatement, citing a source familiar with the discussions. White House communications director Steven Cheung told the outlet that Trump was "totally involved" in the decision, adding, "We have to protect our geniuses." Trump separately celebrated Huang's return on Truth Social , calling the decision "correct and proper" and describing the Nvidia co-founder as a "Great Patriot and National Treasure." He said Attorney General Todd Blanche had confirmed that the federal government possessed no evidence Huang engaged in unlawful conduct. The president's intervention sheds new light on Nvidia's abrupt reversal after its board declared last Tuesday that it had no intention of reinstating Huang. The company announced his return Monday, saying it had received input from senior U.S. government officials before concluding his reinstatement posed no national security risk. Its independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation remains ongoing. passages: In its announcement, Nvidia’s board said it had received “input from senior levels of the United States government” that had led it to be “confident” that Mr Huang does not pose a national security risk, it said.
Mr Huang said he was “honoured” to return to Nvidia.
“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” he said in a statement.
“The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” he wrote.
Nvidia will appoint a new chief compliance officer who will oversee that work, it said, and it committed to co-operate with ongoing government investigations.

President Donald Trump praised the Nvidia board for its decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO , asserting that the United States government “has no reason to believe” that the tech icon’s return will compromise national security.
The Nvidia Board of Directors announced on Monday morning that Huang was returning to head the company despite having resigned amid reports of affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.

The president also added in a subsequent post, “Congratulations to NVIDIA on having made, what I consider to be, an absolutely GREAT decision!”
SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk also commented on the news in an X post, saying, “The mistake has been corrected.”
Following the board’s announcement, Nvidia stock has reportedly skyrocketed.

The president's intervention sheds new light on Nvidia's abrupt reversal after its board declared last Tuesday that it had no intention of reinstating Huang.

Trump separately celebrated Huang's return on Truth Social , calling the decision "correct and proper" and describing the Nvidia co-founder as a "Great Patriot and National Treasure." He said Attorney General Todd Blanche had confirmed that the federal government possessed no evidence Huang engaged in unlawful conduct.

In its announcement, Nvidia’s board said it had received “input from senior levels of the United States government” that had led it to be “confident” that Mr Huang does not pose a national security risk, it said.
Mr Huang said he was “honoured” to return to Nvidia.
“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” he said in a statement.
“The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” he wrote.
Nvidia will appoint a new chief compliance officer who will oversee that work, it said, and it committed to co-operate with ongoing government investigations.
Now, Nvidia says that its board has unanimously agreed that he should return.

Trump repeatedly backed his return, alongside other tech leaders such as Elon Musk , and a petition supporting him now has more than 200,000 signatures, including people claiming to be employees of and investors in Nvidia.
Multiple investigations of the company ​are ⁠underway, including by the US SEC and the Department of Justice , related to everything from potential accounting issues to alleged chip smuggling.
The two are close, and the president has repeatedly backed Mr Huang throughout the scandal.
In the wake of Mr Huang’s reinstatement, however, the company’s share price jumped back up.

“The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C Jones, its chair.
In the days that followed, Nvidia repeatedly denied that it was looking to bring him back.
“On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure,” Trump added.
Trump says the US government has ‘no reason to believe’ Huang’s return to Nvidia poses a national security risk.

“The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security,” the president said, adding that the attorney general also had no evidence that Huang had acted unlawfully.

“Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S.
“The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump posted on Truth Social.
Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct,” Trump continued.
“On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure,” Trump said.

extraction.body: President Donald Trump said Monday that he personally convinced Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, revealing his direct involvement in the chipmaker's stunning leadership reversal less than two weeks after its co-founder's resignation. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview. "And I convinced them." Trump said Nvidia's directors sought assurances about whether Huang's reinstatement posed a national security risk. "And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot," he said. The president also revealed that he spoke with Huang on Sunday night, before Nvidia announced his return. The remarks follow Semafor's reporting that Trump personally dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang's reinstatement, citing a source familiar with the discussions. White House communications director Steven Cheung told the outlet that Trump was "totally involved" in the decision, adding, "We have to protect our geniuses." Trump separately celebrated Huang's return on Truth Social , calling the decision "correct and proper" and describing the Nvidia co-founder as a "Great Patriot and National Treasure." He said Attorney General Todd Blanche had confirmed that the federal government possessed no evidence Huang engaged in unlawful conduct. The president's intervention sheds new light on Nvidia's abrupt reversal after its board declared last Tuesday that it had no intention of reinstating Huang. The company announced his return Monday, saying it had received input from senior U.S. government officials before concluding his reinstatement posed no national security risk. Its independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation remains ongoing. Start your Independent Membership today. Jensen Huang is returning to lead Nvidia after he left in the wake of a run of scandals , the company has said. Mr Huang resigned from the company he helped found on 12 November, after reports of a number of affairs, including with one woman accused of being a Chinese spy. In the time since, Donald Trump and many tech leaders called for his return and a petition supporting him gathered hundreds of thousands of signatures – leading Mr Huang to report that he would return to the company if its board asked him to. Now, Nvidia says that its board has unanimously agreed that he should return. The decision followed “a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang”, which left it satisfied with his “candour and ability to lead”, the board said. Nvidia’s announcement came after a pressure campaign from people including Donald Trump, who had said hours before the announcement that rehiring Mr Huang would be “the best thing for the company, and also, for the USA”. The two are close, and the president has repeatedly backed Mr Huang throughout the scandal. In a Truth Social post immediately after Nvidia announced the decision to reappoint Mr Huang, Trump said it was “the correct and proper decision”. “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” he wrote. “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” the post continued, citing attorney general Todd Blanche’s statements that the government “does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct”. “On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure,” Trump added. In its announcement, Nvidia’s board said it had received “input from senior levels of the United States government” that had led it to be “confident” that Mr Huang does not pose a national security risk, it said. Critics had argued that Mr Huang’s relationship with an accused Chinese spy could undermine the US’s work to keep its chips, which are central to today’s AI technology, could be acquired by China . “The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C Jones, its chair. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company.” Mr Huang said he was “honoured” to return to Nvidia. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” he said in a statement. Nvidia had previously announced that it had launched an independent investigation into accusations that Mr Huang had been successfully targeted by a “foreign intelligence effort”. That will continue to its conclusion and Mr Huang is committed to co-operate with it, Nvidia said. It has also recently formed a new committee that will oversee Nvidia’s compliance with trade rules and national security risks. Nvidia will appoint a new chief compliance officer who will oversee that work, it said, and it committed to co-operate with ongoing government investigations. Those investigations are examining a host of allegations that have dogged Nvidia for some time, and became more widely discussed in the wake of the scandal and Mr Huang’s departure. Multiple investigations of the company ​are ⁠underway, including by the US SEC and the Department of Justice , related to everything from potential accounting issues to alleged chip smuggling. After Mr Huang resigned on 12 November, Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, to run the company. But that decision was met with immediate criticism, and reports that Mr Huang did not have confidence in her as his successor. In the days that followed, pressure had mounted on Nvidia’s board to reappoint Mr Huang. Trump repeatedly backed his return, alongside other tech leaders such as Elon Musk , and a petition supporting him now has more than 200,000 signatures, including people claiming to be employees of and investors in Nvidia. Last week, five days after his departure, Mr Huang posted his first public statement on the scandal. He said that he had seen “an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO” and that he would be “honoured” to return if the board decided it was in the best interest of the company and the country. In the days that followed, Nvidia repeatedly denied that it was looking to bring him back. In its quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, for instance, Ms Kress said that it was “business as usual” and Mr Jones, the chair of its board, confirmed that Nvidia was not considering bringing back Mr Huang. But Nvidia’s share price continued to fall, and has dropped more than 20 per cent since those earnings were announced. That provoked fears that concern about Nvidia and its falling share price could undermine the investment in the US’s AI industry, which in turn could have dramatic effects on the US economy. In the wake of Mr Huang’s reinstatement, however, the company’s share price jumped back up. Nvidia’s share price was up 31 per cent in the moments after the announcement. Jensen Huang is returning to lead Nvidia after he left in the wake of a run of scandals , the company has said.
Mr Huang resigned from the company he helped found on 12 November, after reports of a number of affairs, including with one woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

In the time since, Donald Trump and many tech leaders called for his return and a petition supporting him gathered hundreds of thousands of signatures – leading Mr Huang to report that he would return to the company if its board asked him to.

Now, Nvidia says that its board has unanimously agreed that he should return. The decision followed “a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang”, which left it satisfied with his “candour and ability to lead”, the board said.

Nvidia’s announcement came after a pressure campaign from people including Donald Trump, who had said hours before the announcement that rehiring Mr Huang would be “the best thing for the company, and also, for the USA”. The two are close, and the president has repeatedly backed Mr Huang throughout the scandal.

In a Truth Social post immediately after Nvidia announced the decision to reappoint Mr Huang, Trump said it was “the correct and proper decision”. “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” he wrote.

“The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” the post continued, citing attorney general Todd Blanche’s statements that the government “does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct”.
“On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure,” Trump added.

In its announcement, Nvidia’s board said it had received “input from senior levels of the United States government” that had led it to be “confident” that Mr Huang does not pose a national security risk, it said. Critics had argued that Mr Huang’s relationship with an accused Chinese spy could undermine the US’s work to keep its chips, which are central to today’s AI technology, could be acquired by China .

“The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C Jones, its chair. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company.”
Mr Huang said he was “honoured” to return to Nvidia. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” he said in a statement.

Nvidia had previously announced that it had launched an independent investigation into accusations that Mr Huang had been successfully targeted by a “foreign intelligence effort”. That will continue to its conclusion and Mr Huang is committed to co-operate with it, Nvidia said.

It has also recently formed a new committee that will oversee Nvidia’s compliance with trade rules and national security risks. Nvidia will appoint a new chief compliance officer who will oversee that work, it said, and it committed to co-operate with ongoing government investigations.

Those investigations are examining a host of allegations that have dogged Nvidia for some time, and became more widely discussed in the wake of the scandal and Mr Huang’s departure. Multiple investigations of the company ​are ⁠underway, including by the US SEC and the Department of Justice , related to everything from potential accounting issues to alleged chip smuggling.

After Mr Huang resigned on 12 November, Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, to run the company. But that decision was met with immediate criticism, and reports that Mr Huang did not have confidence in her as his successor.

In the days that followed, pressure had mounted on Nvidia’s board to reappoint Mr Huang. Trump repeatedly backed his return, alongside other tech leaders such as Elon Musk , and a petition supporting him now has more than 200,000 signatures, including people claiming to be employees of and investors in Nvidia.

Last week, five days after his departure, Mr Huang posted his first public statement on the scandal. He said that he had seen “an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO” and that he would be “honoured” to return if the board decided it was in the best interest of the company and the country.

In the days that followed, Nvidia repeatedly denied that it was looking to bring him back. In its quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, for instance, Ms Kress said that it was “business as usual” and Mr Jones, the chair of its board, confirmed that Nvidia was not considering bringing back Mr Huang.

But Nvidia’s share price continued to fall, and has dropped more than 20 per cent since those earnings were announced. That provoked fears that concern about Nvidia and its falling share price could undermine the investment in the US’s AI industry, which in turn could have dramatic effects on the US economy.
In the wake of Mr Huang’s reinstatement, however, the company’s share price jumped back up. Nvidia’s share price was up 31 per cent in the moments after the announcement.

Jim Himes of Connecticut, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, added, "We expect to see him on Capitol Hill next week." The Senate Banking Committee also sent out a notice Monday announcing that Huang would still appear before the panel to testify on Dec.

The board's move, for which President Trump claimed some credit, sent shockwaves through the political sphere, with lawmakers on both sides of the aisle expressing concern, and threw into question whether the congressional hearings would proceed. Huang is set to appear for a transcribed interview with a trio of panels on Dec. 1, including the House Intelligence and Foreign Affairs committees, along with the Select Committee on China. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter voluntarily agreed to appear before the committees on Dec. A spokesperson for the House Intelligence Committee told CBS News that the reinstatement "changes nothing.""When Jensen was CEO, our three committees were demanding answers. When he was removed and no longer CEO, we were still pursuing the facts," the spokesperson said. "The fact that he has been reinstated as CEO, changes nothing. There are serious questions on national security implications that still need answers. Seems like the only thing that is consistent these days on this issue is our three Committees' commitment to oversight."Rep. Jim Himes of Connecticut, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, added, "We expect to see him on Capitol Hill next week." The Senate Banking Committee also sent out a notice Monday announcing that Huang would still appear before the panel to testify on Dec. Lawmakers from both parties expressed alarm Monday about Huang's reinstatement, which is taking place as the focus shifts to questions about the chipmaker's compliance with export restrictions.Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer vowed that Democrats "will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives." And Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, the top Democrat on the Banking Committee, said in a statement that Huang's reinstatement "does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers." She went on to say that Huang's return to Nvidia's top job only "increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk." House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who's set to become House Speaker in the new Congress next year, called Nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang "indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible" and vowed a "swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation" into any potential misconduct by the company and by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. "Congress must come together in swift bipartisan action and demand answers immediately."On the GOP side, Sen. John Cornyn of Texas questioned the rationale behind the Nvidia board's conclusion that Huang's return poses no national security risk, as did Sen. John Curtis of Utah, who pointed to the board's claim that it received input from "senior levels of the United States government.""I have some questions," Curtis said in a post on X. Huang was right to step down when the affair came to light. Just 11 days after Nvidia announced his departure, the board brought him back while its own independent investigation was still underway. "It also doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips. Huang coming to the Senate in December."A representative for Huang declined to comment about Huang's appearances before Congress.

extraction.body: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday hosted his third cryptocurrency gala for top holders of his meme coin, $TRUMP, which has plummeted to below $1 a coin after reaching a high of $75 the day before Trump's second inauguration, on Jan. 19, 2025. The dinner, held at the Trump National golf club in Sterling, Virginia, comes as some Democrats say they will investigate potential conflicts of interest and accuse Trump of using the presidency to boost his personal wealth. At Sunday's dinner, Trump maintained that his support for cryptocurrencies was to boost American economic competitiveness. "I'm doing it for the United States ... If we don't do it, China's going to do it," he told attendees, The Guardian reported. The event also featured speeches from boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, "Shark Tank" investor Kevin O'Leary and NBA champion Tristan Thompson. A total of 185 "wallets" met the criteria for entry to the gala, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just 130 wallets. The wallets listed on the leaderboard held $8.6 million in $TRUMP tokens, a sharp decline from the May 2025 gala, which featured 220 attendees holding a combined $148 million. Crypto billionaire Justin Sun's wallet alone held $18.5 million at the 2025 event — more than the combined holdings of this year's attendees. Eligibility was based on time-weighted holdings of Trump's meme coins from Sept. 30 to Nov. 16, according to the organizer's website. The top 29 holders were invited to a VIP reception with the president, with the top four receiving an 18-karat, Trump-branded gold watch. More than half of the wallets that qualified for the event were linked to crypto exchanges that bar U.S.-based users, according to data gathered by consumer advocacy group Public Citizen for Reuters , suggesting they belong to foreign nationals. The $TRUMP token has earned the Trump family at least $635 million, according to the president's June financial disclosure. Including the meme coins, the Trump family has earned $2.3 billion from its four main crypto-related businesses since the president's second term began, through to April of this year, according to a Reuters report. This is despite the ventures' falling value, which, according to the report, they invest little to no money in. Trump's stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group , is worth about $430 million as of Friday's close. Bitcoin climbed back to over $61,000 on Monday in line with the U.S. stock futures bounce , after an AI-related stock sell-off spilled over into other riskier assets last week. Bitcoin fell as low as $55,130 on Saturday, its lowest level since September 2024. The sell-off wiped out $1.8 billion in leveraged crypto positions, largely from bets on prices rising. Leveraged buyers were forced out as prices fell, then returned after the price stabilized. The world's largest cryptocurrency is still trading at less than half of its October 2025 value.
