extraction.body: Concerns over presidential financial interests intensified after Donald Trump hosted a private cryptocurrency dinner Sunday, November 22, 2026, at Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia. The gathering brought together major holders of his $TRUMP meme coin as its market value dropped below $1, attracting scrutiny over foreign investors and access to the US president.According to CNBC, the token previously reached more than $75 on January 19, 2025, one day before Trump's second inauguration. Its dramatic decline contrasts with the financial benefits the cryptocurrency venture has generated for the president's family.The event was the third gala organized for major $TRUMP token holders. CNBC reported that 185 cryptocurrency wallets qualified for admission, although the official leaderboard displayed only 130 wallets holding a combined $8.6 million in tokens.That figure represents a substantial decline from the May 2025 dinner, when 220 attendees collectively held $148 million in $TRUMP cryptocurrency. The organizer calculated eligibility using time-weighted token holdings between September 30 and November 16, 2026.The top 29 holders received invitations to a VIP reception, while the four highest-ranked participants qualified for 18-karat Trump-branded gold watches. Other VIP guests received Trump-branded watches and Trump Victory perfume, according to CBS News.During his address, Trump defended his cryptocurrency agenda by connecting digital assets with American economic competitiveness and technological leadership."We have to remain number one in everything we do. If we are not going to do it, China is going to do it," Trump told attendees, according to CBS News.He also discussed artificial intelligence, semiconductor technology and the importance of maintaining oversight of the rapidly expanding industry."There should be some checks and balances," Trump said about the AI industry.His remarks included comments about prominent technology executives. Trump expressed support for Jensen Huang returning to Nvidia's leadership and described Elon Musk as an unusually talented individual. He also praised Anthropic's chief executive.Beyond the public remarks, the composition of the guest list raised questions about international participation. A CBS News investigation found that more than half of the wallets associated with qualifying attendees used cryptocurrency exchanges that prohibit US customers.Reuters separately reported that data collected by consumer advocacy organization Public Citizen indicated a similar concentration of wallets connected to exchanges serving customers outside the United States.One attendee identified as Addy, who leads Singapore-linked company FastX, described her organization's cryptocurrency holdings before the gathering."We are the number one Trump holder now. We have over 2 million tokens," Addy said in a video published on X before the event.She also described the planned VIP appearance as an important occasion for the company and its community."So later this month our team will attend a VIP reception with President Trump. So it's a big moment for us and the FastX community," she said.CBS News traced FastX's promotional video to an office building in Singapore but found neither Addy nor other company representatives there. The company did not respond to requests for comment.Corey Frayer, an investor protection specialist at the Consumer Federation of America, questioned whether the arrangement adequately separated presidential responsibilities from private financial interests."He's not making choices about public policy and what's in the best interest of the United States. He's making choices about what is most profitable to him," Frayer told CBS News.Trump previously addressed concerns about his family's cryptocurrency activities during an interview with 60 Minutes. He said his sons manage the businesses through a trust while he concentrates on presidential responsibilities."My sons run the company. It's hard to say to them, 'Don't do anything anymore for four years because I'm president,'" Trump said.According to his June financial disclosure, the $TRUMP token issuer had generated at least $635 million for the Trump family. A Reuters report cited by CNBC estimated that the family's four principal cryptocurrency-related businesses generated $2.3 billion between the beginning of Trump's second term and April 2026.Meanwhile, cryptocurrency markets experienced significant volatility. Bitcoin recovered above $61,000 on Monday, November 23, after falling to approximately $55,130 on Saturday, its weakest level since September 2024.CNBC reported that the decline eliminated $1.8 billion in leveraged cryptocurrency positions. US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds also recorded $1.24 billion in withdrawals during the previous week, marking their third consecutive week of outflows.The White House, FastX and Fight Fight Fight LLC, the company organizing the gala, did not respond to CBS News requests for comment. The event's website stated that attendees would not receive private meet-and-greet sessions with Trump.

extraction.body: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday hosted his third cryptocurrency gala for top holders of his meme coin, $TRUMP, which has plummeted to below $1 a coin after reaching a high of $75 the day before Trump's second inauguration, on Jan. 19, 2025. The dinner, held at the Trump National golf club in Sterling, Virginia, comes as some Democrats say they will investigate potential conflicts of interest and accuse Trump of using the presidency to boost his personal wealth. At Sunday's dinner, Trump maintained that his support for cryptocurrencies was to boost American economic competitiveness. "I'm doing it for the United States ... If we don't do it, China's going to do it," he told attendees, The Guardian reported. The event also featured speeches from boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, "Shark Tank" investor Kevin O'Leary and NBA champion Tristan Thompson. A total of 185 "wallets" met the criteria for entry to the gala, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just 130 wallets. The wallets listed on the leaderboard held $8.6 million in $TRUMP tokens, a sharp decline from the May 2025 gala, which featured 220 attendees holding a combined $148 million. Crypto billionaire Justin Sun's wallet alone held $18.5 million at the 2025 event — more than the combined holdings of this year's attendees. Eligibility was based on time-weighted holdings of Trump's meme coins from Sept. 30 to Nov. 16, according to the organizer's website. The top 29 holders were invited to a VIP reception with the president, with the top four receiving an 18-karat, Trump-branded gold watch. More than half of the wallets that qualified for the event were linked to crypto exchanges that bar U.S.-based users, according to data gathered by consumer advocacy group Public Citizen for Reuters , suggesting they belong to foreign nationals. The $TRUMP token has earned the Trump family at least $635 million, according to the president's June financial disclosure. Including the meme coins, the Trump family has earned $2.3 billion from its four main crypto-related businesses since the president's second term began, through to April of this year, according to a Reuters report. This is despite the ventures' falling value, which, according to the report, they invest little to no money in. Trump's stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group , is worth about $430 million as of Friday's close. Bitcoin climbed back to over $61,000 on Monday in line with the U.S. stock futures bounce , after an AI-related stock sell-off spilled over into other riskier assets last week. Bitcoin fell as low as $55,130 on Saturday, its lowest level since September 2024. The sell-off wiped out $1.8 billion in leveraged crypto positions, largely from bets on prices rising. Leveraged buyers were forced out as prices fell, then returned after the price stabilized. The world's largest cryptocurrency is still trading at less than half of its October 2025 value. extraction.body: The president tells CNBC he provided national security assurances to directors, saying he spoke with the board “directly and indirectly” President Donald Trump said Monday that he personally convinced Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, revealing his direct involvement in the chipmaker’s stunning leadership reversal less than two weeks after its co-founder’s resignation. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC’s Eamon Javers in a phone interview. “And I convinced them.” Trump said Nvidia’s directors sought assurances about whether Huang’s reinstatement posed a national security risk. “And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot,” he said. The president also revealed that he spoke with Huang on Sunday night, before Nvidia announced his return. The remarks follow Semafor’s reporting that Trump personally dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang’s reinstatement, citing a source familiar with the discussions. White House communications director Steven Cheung told the outlet that Trump was “totally involved” in the decision, adding, “We have to protect our geniuses.” Trump separately celebrated Huang’s return on Truth Social , calling the decision “correct and proper” and describing the Nvidia co-founder as a “Great Patriot and National Treasure.” He said Attorney General Todd Blanche had confirmed that the federal government possessed no evidence Huang engaged in unlawful conduct. The president’s intervention sheds new light on Nvidia’s abrupt reversal after its board declared last Tuesday that it had no intention of reinstating Huang. The company announced his return Monday, saying it had received input from senior U.S. government officials before concluding his reinstatement posed no national security risk. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC’s Eamon Javers in a phone interview. “And I convinced them.”

Trump said Nvidia’s directors sought assurances about whether Huang’s reinstatement posed a national security risk. “And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot,” he said. The president also revealed that he spoke with Huang on Sunday night, before Nvidia announced his return.

The remarks follow Semafor’s reporting that Trump personally dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang’s reinstatement, citing a source familiar with the discussions. White House communications director Steven Cheung told the outlet that Trump was “totally involved” in the decision, adding, “We have to protect our geniuses.”

Trump separately celebrated Huang’s return on Truth Social , calling the decision “correct and proper” and describing the Nvidia co-founder as a “Great Patriot and National Treasure.” He said Attorney General Todd Blanche had confirmed that the federal government possessed no evidence Huang engaged in unlawful conduct.

The president’s intervention sheds new light on Nvidia’s abrupt reversal after its board declared last Tuesday that it had no intention of reinstating Huang. The company announced his return Monday, saying it had received input from senior U.S. government officials before concluding his reinstatement posed no national security risk. Its independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation remains ongoing.

President Donald Trump said Monday that he personally convinced Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, revealing his direct involvement in the chipmaker’s stunning leadership reversal less than two weeks after its co-founder’s resignation.
“I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC’s Eamon Javers in a phone interview. “And I convinced them.”

Trump said Nvidia’s directors sought assurances about whether Huang’s reinstatement posed a national security risk. “And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot,” he said. The president also revealed that he spoke with Huang on Sunday night, before Nvidia announced his return.

The remarks follow Semafor’s reporting that Trump personally dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang’s reinstatement, citing a source familiar with the discussions. White House communications director Steven Cheung told the outlet that Trump was “totally involved” in the decision, adding, “We have to protect our geniuses.”

Trump separately celebrated Huang’s return on Truth Social , calling the decision “correct and proper” and describing the Nvidia co-founder as a “Great Patriot and National Treasure.” He said Attorney General Todd Blanche had confirmed that the federal government possessed no evidence Huang engaged in unlawful conduct.

The president’s intervention sheds new light on Nvidia’s abrupt reversal after its board declared last Tuesday that it had no intention of reinstating Huang. The company announced his return Monday, saying it had received input from senior U.S. government officials before concluding his reinstatement posed no national security risk. Its independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation remains ongoing.

extraction.body: Returning Jensen Huang to Nvidia's top job was hailed in Silicon Valley as essential to the future of the AI trade, and on Monday his supporters got their wish. But the embattled CEO's road back to the job may prove easier than the one awaiting him in Washington. Huang's reinstatement comes less than two weeks after revelations of his relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative forced his resignation, setting off a political firestorm over Nvidia's dealings with China and its influence within the Trump administration. Now back atop the company he co-founded more than three decades ago, Huang faces a growing list of congressional inquiries, federal and state scrutiny, and lawmakers on both sides of the aisle demanding answers about whether his relationship compromised US national security. "All the questions that people have been raising in the press and in social media, all those questions are still out there," Martijn Rasser, vice president of technology leadership at the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP), told Yahoo Finance. "That aspect of the story is still very much in play," said Rasser, a former officer at the Central Intelligence Agency and former director of the technology and national security program at the Center for a New American Security. Nvidia's board of directors said on Monday that the decision to reinstate Huang came after they "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk." President Trump, who had pushed for Huang's reinstatement since his ouster on Nov. 12, confirmed that he had called the company's board of directors to personally lobby for Huang, telling CNBC that he had been speaking to the board "directly and indirectly" and had offered assurances on national security. The president noted in a Truth Social post that the US government "has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," and that "the Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." Lawmakers, including prominent members from the president's own party, have disputed those assertions. Republican Sen. John Cornyn, who sits on the Senate Foreign Affairs Committee and the Select Committee on Intelligence, wrote shortly after the news broke Monday, "No national security risk? Based on what?" Republican Representatives Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter last week requesting Huang's testimony before their respective House committees, saying that "recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information." Democrats made similar calls on Monday, following on prior statements condemning potential national security violations at Nvidia ( NVDA ). "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and NVIDIA still owe Congress answers," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, wrote on Monday . "Huang's return only increases the urgency to pass bipartisan export control bills and make sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk." In a similar tone to Cornyn, Delaware Democratic Sen. Chris Coons wrote on X , "No national security risk? The guy who was having an affair with a Chinese spy while working relentlessly to help China get access to as many AI chips as possible? Really?" Calls for change at Nvidia came from inside the White House as well, despite the president's statements. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News last week that Nvidia's board needed to "go outside the company" as it searched for a new leader, arguing that the company needed a "dramatic shake-up." Bessent, however, softened his tone in interviews on Sunday. Republicans have also pushed on wider questions surrounding the US government's involvement with Nvidia, including coming congressional interrogations of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whom Huang has called "the person I talk to most in the administration." "If Howard Lutnick wanted my support, perhaps he should have responded to my many letters warning about these Chinese communist front companies and, more importantly, taking the threats of communist China more seriously," Arkansas Sen. Tom Cotton said in an interview with the Wall Street Journal. Nvidia has said in multiple quarterly reports that it projects no compute revenue from China in forward-looking estimates, stating in its fiscal second quarter report, "Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for wide distribution in China's data center market with the approval from both the USG and the Chinese government." Huang's first major test will come next week on Dec. 1, when he is scheduled to appear before three House committees investigating his ties to the suspected Chinese operative, Alice Huang, and the potential diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to China. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is also set to face questioning alongside senior Commerce Department officials responsible for enforcing restrictions on chip exports. An inquiry by the Commerce Department into Singapore-based Megaspeed — the company Alice Huang was once associated with — over alleged violations of US semiconductor export controls was transferred to the Justice Department after Teter asked the Commerce Department for information on the investigation, The New York Times reported." Huang has separately agreed to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3, setting up an appearance alongside Lutnick, who has also agreed to testify and is facing scrutiny over reports he slowed investigations into companies suspected of funneling controlled semiconductors into China. Amid a feud with Lutnick that has spilled into public light over the past two weeks, Bessent said investigators would need to ask about any potential export control violations by Nvidia or its customers such as Megaspeed, were they "a low-level fail, was it in the middle, or was it up in the C-suite? Who knew?" The controversy has also drawn investigators beyond Capitol Hill. California's attorney general has subpoenaed Nvidia as part of an investigation connected to Huang's affair. The Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating Nvidia over accounting violations , per Reuters. Proposed national legislation could also present further complications for Nvidia's business. The so-called AI Overwatch Act would tighten export controls on shipments of advanced dual-use AI chips to foreign nations such as China, while the Chip Security Act would impose new verification measures on the locations of chips exported abroad. The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act would impose more restrictive export controls on the equipment needed to make advanced AI chips. "I think the news of the past few weeks has underscored in the mind of many legislators on Capitol Hill that not enough is being done to ensure that critical US technologies stay out of the hands of our adversaries," SCSP's Rasser told Yahoo Finance. As Huang prepares to appear before Congress, he will have an important ally in Trump, who has repeatedly referred to Huang as a close associate. The president said on Monday that he personally weighed in on the Nvidia board's decision to reinstate Huang and believes his intervention was "very important" to the decision, telling CNBC, "I convinced them." "If I thought he did something wrong, I wouldn't be recommending to his board to hire him," Trump said. Follow Jake Conley on X @byjakeconley or email him at jake.conley@yahooinc.com .

Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia has triggered a political fight over how closely he worked with President Donald Trump and how much access the United States should allow for advanced artificial intelligence chips to reach China. Huang “met with Trump on multiple occasions, traveled with him to the United Kingdom, and in May accompanied him on Air Force One during his visit to China,” placing his role at the center of Washington’s export-control debate. U.S. intelligence suspicions have focused on Alice Huang, and the BBC reported that “U.S. intelligence suspects Alice Huang has ties to Chinese intelligence,” while Beijing rejects the allegations.
Nvidia’s board has denied any compromise, and the BBC said “there is no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised.”

The BBC described the export-control responsibility of U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick and said his department was “pressured to act on concerns about Megaspeed, a Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China.”
Lutnick “received a highly classified memorandum” and “resisted taking action against the company,” a decision now under scrutiny.
The Washington Post said Rubio’s intervention “helped topple” a corporate voice on China, and it tied that shift to momentum for “tougher restrictions” on advanced technology reaching Beijing.

The BBC reported that Republicans also questioned the government’s approach and that pressure is mounting politically as House members demand explanations. A continuing gap in export controls has been described, with Senator Elizabeth Warren saying Huang’s resignation does not absolve him and urging Lutnick to explain why there are still gaps in export controls. The Washington Post linked the controversy to the administration’s China policy direction, describing how Huang’s access and “blessing” for chip sales to China became a flashpoint for officials pushing to keep powerful technology out of Beijing’s hands.

The campaign centers on a commercial question with national-security weight: whether Nvidia can sell advanced AI chips to China. Huang and the company's lobbyists sought to secure that right, the report says. On its official site , Nvidia presents itself as a leader in AI computing, a position that depends on access to large markets. Reader reactions, summarized by an AI tool attached to the report, were critical of Donald Trump and Huang. Commenters accused both of prioritizing personal gain over national security. The summary warned that it was AI-generated, could make mistakes, and was not a replacement for reading the comments. That caveat matters. The same product sits at the center of both calculations. Advanced chips are not ordinary components. They are the hardware behind large language models and other AI systems, and governments treat them as strategic assets. Export controls on advanced semiconductors have become a central tool in U.S. technology policy. Companies facing restrictions seek licenses, exemptions or revised rules, and those requests draw scrutiny from security hawks. extraction.body: Returning Jensen Huang to Nvidia's top job was hailed in Silicon Valley as essential to the future of the AI trade, and on Monday his supporters got their wish. But the embattled CEO's road back to the job may prove easier than the one awaiting him in Washington. Huang's reinstatement comes less than two weeks after revelations of his relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative forced his resignation, setting off a political firestorm over Nvidia's dealings with China and its influence within the Trump administration. Now back atop the company he co-founded more than three decades ago, Huang faces a growing list of congressional inquiries, federal and state scrutiny, and lawmakers on both sides of the aisle demanding answers about whether his relationship compromised US national security. "All the questions that people have been raising in the press and in social media, all those questions are still out there," Martijn Rasser, vice president of technology leadership at the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP), told Yahoo Finance. "That aspect of the story is still very much in play," said Rasser, a former officer at the Central Intelligence Agency and former director of the technology and national security program at the Center for a New American Security. Nvidia's board of directors said on Monday that the decision to reinstate Huang came after they "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk." President Trump, who had pushed for Huang's reinstatement since his ouster on Nov. 12, confirmed that he had called the company's board of directors to personally lobby for Huang, telling CNBC that he had been speaking to the board "directly and indirectly" and had offered assurances on national security. The president noted in a Truth Social post that the US government "has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," and that "the Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." Lawmakers, including prominent members from the president's own party, have disputed those assertions. Republican Sen. John Cornyn, who sits on the Senate Foreign Affairs Committee and the Select Committee on Intelligence, wrote shortly after the news broke Monday, "No national security risk? Based on what?" Republican Representatives Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter last week requesting Huang's testimony before their respective House committees, saying that "recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information." Democrats made similar calls on Monday, following on prior statements condemning potential national security violations at Nvidia ( NVDA ). "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and NVIDIA still owe Congress answers," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, wrote on Monday . "Huang's return only increases the urgency to pass bipartisan export control bills and make sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk." In a similar tone to Cornyn, Delaware Democratic Sen. Chris Coons wrote on X , "No national security risk? The guy who was having an affair with a Chinese spy while working relentlessly to help China get access to as many AI chips as possible? Really?" Calls for change at Nvidia came from inside the White House as well, despite the president's statements. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News last week that Nvidia's board needed to "go outside the company" as it searched for a new leader, arguing that the company needed a "dramatic shake-up." Bessent, however, softened his tone in interviews on Sunday. Republicans have also pushed on wider questions surrounding the US government's involvement with Nvidia, including coming congressional interrogations of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whom Huang has called "the person I talk to most in the administration." "If Howard Lutnick wanted my support, perhaps he should have responded to my many letters warning about these Chinese communist front companies and, more importantly, taking the threats of communist China more seriously," Arkansas Sen. Tom Cotton said in an interview with the Wall Street Journal. Nvidia has said in multiple quarterly reports that it projects no compute revenue from China in forward-looking estimates, stating in its fiscal second quarter report, "Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for wide distribution in China's data center market with the approval from both the USG and the Chinese government." Huang's first major test will come next week on Dec. 1, when he is scheduled to appear before three House committees investigating his ties to the suspected Chinese operative, Alice Huang, and the potential diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to China. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is also set to face questioning alongside senior Commerce Department officials responsible for enforcing restrictions on chip exports. An inquiry by the Commerce Department into Singapore-based Megaspeed — the company Alice Huang was once associated with — over alleged violations of US semiconductor export controls was transferred to the Justice Department after Teter asked the Commerce Department for information on the investigation, The New York Times reported." Huang has separately agreed to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3, setting up an appearance alongside Lutnick, who has also agreed to testify and is facing scrutiny over reports he slowed investigations into companies suspected of funneling controlled semiconductors into China. Amid a feud with Lutnick that has spilled into public light over the past two weeks, Bessent said investigators would need to ask about any potential export control violations by Nvidia or its customers such as Megaspeed, were they "a low-level fail, was it in the middle, or was it up in the C-suite? Who knew?" The controversy has also drawn investigators beyond Capitol Hill. California's attorney general has subpoenaed Nvidia as part of an investigation connected to Huang's affair. The Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating Nvidia over accounting violations , per Reuters. Proposed national legislation could also present further complications for Nvidia's business. The so-called AI Overwatch Act would tighten export controls on shipments of advanced dual-use AI chips to foreign nations such as China, while the Chip Security Act would impose new verification measures on the locations of chips exported abroad. The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act would impose more restrictive export controls on the equipment needed to make advanced AI chips. "I think the news of the past few weeks has underscored in the mind of many legislators on Capitol Hill that not enough is being done to ensure that critical US technologies stay out of the hands of our adversaries," SCSP's Rasser told Yahoo Finance. As Huang prepares to appear before Congress, he will have an important ally in Trump, who has repeatedly referred to Huang as a close associate. The president said on Monday that he personally weighed in on the Nvidia board's decision to reinstate Huang and believes his intervention was "very important" to the decision, telling CNBC, "I convinced them." "If I thought he did something wrong, I wouldn't be recommending to his board to hire him," Trump said. Follow Jake Conley on X @byjakeconley or email him at jake.conley@yahooinc.com .

extraction.body: After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.” “You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate. It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director. “There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC. Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air. Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility. Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.” But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration. The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation. The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added. Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the Nvidia CEO — worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. But on Sunday evening, Trump still argued for Huang’s return and managed to continue flipping Nvidia’s board in his favor after a weekend’s worth of efforts. If the board maintained any hang-ups about bringing Huang back as CEO, Trump’s power over the executive branch — and the pressure he could exert with it — might have offered a compelling counterargument. The Securities and Exchange Commission had previously opened an investigation into whether Nvidia “misled investors,” according to The Wall Street Journal. But in a post on Truth Social Monday, Trump said that the attorney general “has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” Reached for comment, the DOJ did not provide an on-the-record response in line with The Verge’s editorial policy. Key Democrats have indicated that both Nvidia and the Trump administration will be under fire when the new Congress is sworn in — and momentum has built behind GPU export controls, which Huang lobbied extensively to loosen. “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.” Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said in a post on X, adding they’d work “on a bipartisan basis to continue advancing policies that stop the flow of our most powerful technology to the Chinese military and other adversaries.” Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) called the board’s decision “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible” and pledged to investigate “business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce.” He called for “traditional Republicans” to join in the effort.

extraction.body: US President Donald Trump has publicly backed Jensen Huang's reported bid to return to Nvidia's top leadership, even as allegations involving a woman linked to the former CEO and a suspected Chinese espionage network bring the company under increased scrutiny. In a post on Truth Social, Trump urged Nvidia's board to reconsider Huang's position, saying his return would benefit both the company and the United States. “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A,” Trump said. The endorsement comes amid a report by *The New York Times* alleging that Alice Huang, described as a suspected Chinese spy, maintained contact with an official from China's Ministry of State Security for more than a year while she was reportedly involved in a secret relationship with Jensen Huang. Alleged links to China's intelligence network Citing multiple people familiar with US intelligence reports, The New York Times reported that Alice Huang was in contact with China's Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 until autumn 2026. The report also alleged that her business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, had worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. The allegations have prompted scrutiny from US authorities. Director of US National Intelligence Jay Clayton has confirmed that investigations into Alice Huang and her company, Megaspeed, are underway. In an interview with Fox News, Clayton said investigations into both the individual and the company were progressing alongside regulatory proceedings. He also said he expected Nvidia's board to examine the matter. “There is an investigation into her company, and there is an investigation into her. That is going to play out,” Clayton said, adding that the American public would receive answers as the process moves forward. Nvidia board faces pressure over leadership decision Trump's public support comes at a time when Nvidia's leadership and the company's board are facing questions over the reported developments. Huang is expected to testify before three House committees on December 1, adding to the scrutiny surrounding the matter. However, the Nvidia board and interim CEO Colette Kress have reportedly ruled out his reinstatement at the top of the company. With congressional attention growing and investigations continuing, Trump's endorsement may not be enough to secure Huang's return. The board's position and the outcome of the ongoing proceedings are likely to remain central to any decision on the company's leadership.

extraction.body: Washington — President Trump says that he spoke to Nvidia's board and helped win Jensen Huang's reinstatement as the company's CEO. He told CNBC in a phone interview Monday about his call to the board. "I spoke to them and I convinced them," he said. "And it was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week ago." The president also claimed in a Truth Social post Monday that the U.S. government "has no reason to believe" that Huang's return to Nvidia as CEO "poses any risk to national security," although he did not elaborate. His social media comment went up shortly after Nvidia announced its board had reinstated Huang. Huang resigned less than two weeks ago over an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies suspected of spying for China. The president said Nvidia's board asked "for assurance on the national security threat" and he gave them "assurance." The president told CNBC he believes his intervention was essential to getting Huang reinstated. Trump told CNBC Huang "did nothing wrong."He also said in the interview that he spoke with Huang Sunday night "after the deal was done" and told him to "work hard."Mr. Trump said in Truth Social his post that U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." A Justice Department official told CBS News that Mr. Trump did speak to Blanche over the weekend, and the official said the has no evidence of any wrongdoing by either Jensen Huang or Nvidia.Mr. Trump has been a vocal proponent of returning Huang to the company, after Nvidia's stock tanked in the wake of his resignation. Since his reinstatement was announced Monday morning, the stock has surged over 30%.Huang has built Nvidia into one of the world's most valuable companies, with its high-powered chips emerging as integral to the race for AI dominance between the U.S. and China. A White House official told CBS News on Monday that the decision to reinstate Huang "will preserve America's technological edge over China, strengthen our national security" and ensure the future of AI will be built in the U.S. "The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO," Mr. "The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.""On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," he continued. "Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security."Huang had publicly advocated for his return to Nvidia, along with others in the tech industry, including SpaceX's Elon Musk. Republicans and Democrats are applying increasing pressure to make Huang testify about Nvidia chips making their way into Chinese hands. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.” “You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate.
It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so.

News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility.
“We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.” But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence.

Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.

Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the Nvidia CEO — worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency.
In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air.
Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker.
Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return.

US President Donald Trump has publicly backed Jensen Huang's reported bid to return to Nvidia's top leadership, even as allegations involving a woman linked to the former CEO and a suspected Chinese espionage network bring the company under increased scrutiny.
“I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang.

Alleged links to China's intelligence network Citing multiple people familiar with US intelligence reports, The New York Times reported that Alice Huang was in contact with China's Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 until autumn 2026.
With congressional attention growing and investigations continuing, Trump's endorsement may not be enough to secure Huang's return.
It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A,” Trump said.
He also said he expected Nvidia's board to examine the matter.
However, the Nvidia board and interim CEO Colette Kress have reportedly ruled out his reinstatement at the top of the company.
Huang is expected to testify before three House committees on December 1, adding to the scrutiny surrounding the matter.

extraction.body: After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.” “You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate. It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director. “There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC. Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air. Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.” But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration. The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation. The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added. Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the Nvidia CEO — worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. But on Sunday evening, Trump still argued for Huang’s return and managed to continue flipping Nvidia’s board in his favor after a weekend’s worth of efforts. If the board maintained any hang-ups about bringing Huang back as CEO, Trump’s power over the executive branch — and the pressure he could exert with it — might have offered a compelling counterargument. The Securities and Exchange Commission had previously opened an investigation into whether Nvidia “misled investors,” according to The Wall Street Journal. extraction.body: US President Donald Trump has publicly backed Jensen Huang's reported bid to return to Nvidia's top leadership, even as allegations involving a woman linked to the former CEO and a suspected Chinese espionage network bring the company under increased scrutiny. In a post on Truth Social, Trump urged Nvidia's board to reconsider Huang's position, saying his return would benefit both the company and the United States. “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A,” Trump said. The endorsement comes amid a report by *The New York Times* alleging that Alice Huang, described as a suspected Chinese spy, maintained contact with an official from China's Ministry of State Security for more than a year while she was reportedly involved in a secret relationship with Jensen Huang. Alleged links to China's intelligence network Citing multiple people familiar with US intelligence reports, The New York Times reported that Alice Huang was in contact with China's Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 until autumn 2026. The report also alleged that her business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, had worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. The allegations have prompted scrutiny from US authorities. Director of US National Intelligence Jay Clayton has confirmed that investigations into Alice Huang and her company, Megaspeed, are underway. In an interview with Fox News, Clayton said investigations into both the individual and the company were progressing alongside regulatory proceedings. He also said he expected Nvidia's board to examine the matter. “There is an investigation into her company, and there is an investigation into her. That is going to play out,” Clayton said, adding that the American public would receive answers as the process moves forward. Nvidia board faces pressure over leadership decision Trump's public support comes at a time when Nvidia's leadership and the company's board are facing questions over the reported developments. Huang is expected to testify before three House committees on December 1, adding to the scrutiny surrounding the matter. However, the Nvidia board and interim CEO Colette Kress have reportedly ruled out his reinstatement at the top of the company. With congressional attention growing and investigations continuing, Trump's endorsement may not be enough to secure Huang's return. The board's position and the outcome of the ongoing proceedings are likely to remain central to any decision on the company's leadership.

Several other factors also set the stage for Huang's return and accelerated discussions with him over the weekend, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal deliberations close to Nvidia's board. A sharp stock price drop after his resignation and questions about the leadership of interim CEO Colette Kress also spurred the board's decision, the people said. "I convinced them," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview Monday morning , shortly after Nvidia announced Huang's return. "I made the deal," the president said. "It was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago. Trump said Nvidia's board asked for guarantees that Huang, who resigned less than two weeks ago, was not a threat to national security. "And we gave them assurances, at least with everything we know," the president said. "We believe he's fine. He's absolutely fine." Senior Trump administration officials reached out to the board overnight Friday to inform them that Huang had not violated U.S. national security laws, people familiar with the board's actions said. After the White House outreach, the board contacted Huang, who joined meetings on Saturday and Sunday to discuss his potential return, the people said. Huang's spokesman did not respond to a request for comment when asked about his contact with the board and other events leading up to his return. The Nvidia founder resigned on Nov. 12 after reports that he had an affair with an Nvidia employee and with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is suspected of being a spy for China. A report of an affair with a second Nvidia employee broke right after he quit. Nvidia's board named Kress, the company's chief financial officer, as the interim CEO while it searched for a permanent successor. But within days of Kress taking over, some employees and investors who spoke to CNBC questioned her stewardship, as many of them clamored for Huang's return. Kress' performances at an all-hands company meeting on Wednesday and on Nvidia's earnings call with analysts a day earlier were seen by some investors as uninspiring and underwhelming. As the board faced those concerns amid a stock drop of more than 25% over the past week, Huang was aggressively working the phones with major tech CEOs who wanted to see him return to Nvidia, according to sources close to Huang. In the days after he resigned, Huang spoke with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , OpenAI President Greg Brockman , and Elon Musk , CEO of SpaceX and Tesla , one of the sources said. On Nov. 17, less than a week after quitting, Huang issued a public statement saying he was open to returning as CEO. "I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," he said. "NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company," he added. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO." On the same day, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, Harvey Jones, told analysts on the company's earnings call that the board did "not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Kress, the following day, told company employees at the all-hands meeting, "Let's move forward." Nvidia's public stance against Huang returning came as members of Congress moved ahead with plans to interview him at hearings and as criticism grew over the company's business in Asia. The Department of Justice and the Commerce Department, in an unusual joint public statement on Nov. 17, said they were investigating Megaspeed for possible diversion of advanced Nvidia semiconductor chips to China in violation of U.S. export control law. "Sensitive technologies like semiconductors are among the most valuable and strategic assets of the U.S. economy," the departments said. But days later, senior Trump administration officials contacted Nvidia's board to tell them that Jensen Huang himself was not a risk, according to the sources. The Department of Commerce added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist later Monday. Trump, during his interview Monday with CNBC, was asked what Attorney General Todd Blanche had told him about potential criminal liability for Huang and the question of whether Nvidia chips had ended up in China in violation of U.S. export laws. "They did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he, himself, was exonerated," Trump said . The person said Trump and Vance were briefed on the national security elements of the situation and saw no evidence that Huang did anything illegal or untoward in that regard. Trump believes his administration's close working relationship with Huang gives the U.S. its best opportunity to protect national security and prevent cutting-edge AI chips from reaching banned customers, according to the person. Trump said he spoke with Huang on Sunday, after Nvidia had voted unanimously to reinstate him. "I called him up, and I said: 'I ask you to do one thing, Jensen. Work hard,'" Trump said. President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday morning that he spoke directly to Nvidia’s board and urged them to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang.

“And I convinced them,” the president said. “I made the deal.”

Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Huang came less than two weeks after he resigned. Huang had stepped down after admitting he cheated on his wife and amid claims his affairs included one with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees.

Huang’s relationship with the suspected spy, Alice Huang, and her role as an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed raised concerns that she was facilitating the diversion of Nvidia’s most advanced semiconductor chip to China.
Trump said Nvidia’s board “did ask for assurance on the national security threat,” Trump said.

extraction.body: US President Donald Trump has called on Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as its CEO. Trump's appeal adds to growing calls for Huang's return, including a petition with more than 200,000 signatures that Elon Musk has signed. Huang, who co-founded the AI chip giant in 1993, is due to answer lawmakers' questions in Congress on 1 December. "I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the company, and also, for the U.S.A.," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform on Sunday. Trump has stepped up his support over the past week for Huang's return. Last Monday, he said he "would not mind" seeing Huang reinstated. On Friday, he told reporters at the White House that he "would love to see Jensen be given a second chance". Huang resigned on 12 November after it emerged that he had two extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy. Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations and US authorities said they have not reached a conclusion. The "Stand with Jensen" petition, an open letter to Nvidia's board, had more than 206,000 signatures as of Monday morning, according to its website. More than 10,000 signatories claim to be current Nvidia employees. The letter asked the board to "bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts". It also highlighted that Nvidia and Huang have not endorsed it. "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too," Musk wrote on X on 13 November. Tobi Lütke, CEO of e-commerce platform Shopify, and Tim Sweeney, CEO of Fortnite developer Epic Games, have also signed it. Huang said on 17 November that he would be "honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO" if the board judged that best for the company, its staff, its shareholders, and America. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on 15 November that Nvidia needed "a dramatic shake-up" and a CEO from outside the company. However, in an interview with CBS on Sunday, he stated: "I said they should go to the outside, but he's on the outside now". Thus far, Nvidia's board does not plan to bring him back. Chair Harvey Jones told analysts during the company's earnings call last Tuesday that the board had "unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO". Colette Kress, Nvidia's finance chief, has taken over as interim CEO during the search for a permanent replacement. An outside law firm is currently undertaking an investigation. Nvidia's shares closed around $125.5 on Friday, representing a 48% collapse since their intraday all-time high price of roughly $243.3 on 6 October. They lost over 20% just last week, their seventh weekly decline in a row and the longest losing streak since 2008. The slide continued despite Nvidia beating earnings forecasts last Tuesday. Friday's 14% drop followed a Reuters report, citing two people briefed on the matter, that the Securities and Exchange Commission, the US markets regulator, was examining possible accounting issues at Nvidia. Huang will answer questions from three House committees behind closed doors on 1 December: Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party. The committees are looking into the possible diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese businesses. The session will be a transcribed interview and will not be open to the public. Huang's public testimony will come before the Senate Banking Committee, according to the office of its chair, Republican Senator Tim Scott. No date has been set, though Scott had originally asked for 3 December. Two Nvidia shareholders, the investment firms Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management, have asked the board to keep Huang's return open and to hold off on a permanent CEO until all the facts are known.

extraction.body: The stunning decision by Nvidia 's board to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO was sealed by a personal promise from President Donald Trump on Sunday that Huang had not broken national security laws, three people familiar with the board's thinking told CNBC. Several other factors also set the stage for Huang's return and accelerated discussions with him over the weekend, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal deliberations close to Nvidia's board. A sharp stock price drop after his resignation and questions about the leadership of interim CEO Colette Kress also spurred the board's decision, the people said. "I convinced them," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview Monday morning , shortly after Nvidia announced Huang's return. "I made the deal," the president said. "It was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago. Trump said Nvidia's board asked for guarantees that Huang, who resigned less than two weeks ago, was not a threat to national security. "And we gave them assurances, at least with everything we know," the president said. "We believe he's fine. He's absolutely fine." Senior Trump administration officials reached out to the board overnight Friday to inform them that Huang had not violated U.S. national security laws, people familiar with the board's actions said. After the White House outreach, the board contacted Huang, who joined meetings on Saturday and Sunday to discuss his potential return, the people said. Huang's spokesman did not respond to a request for comment when asked about his contact with the board and other events leading up to his return. The Nvidia founder resigned on Nov. 12 after reports that he had an affair with an Nvidia employee and with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is suspected of being a spy for China. A report of an affair with a second Nvidia employee broke right after he quit. Nvidia's board named Kress, the company's chief financial officer, as the interim CEO while it searched for a permanent successor. But within days of Kress taking over, some employees and investors who spoke to CNBC questioned her stewardship, as many of them clamored for Huang's return. Kress' performances at an all-hands company meeting on Wednesday and on Nvidia's earnings call with analysts a day earlier were seen by some investors as uninspiring and underwhelming. As the board faced those concerns amid a stock drop of more than 25% over the past week, Huang was aggressively working the phones with major tech CEOs who wanted to see him return to Nvidia, according to sources close to Huang. In the days after he resigned, Huang spoke with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , OpenAI President Greg Brockman , and Elon Musk , CEO of SpaceX and Tesla , one of the sources said. On Nov. 17, less than a week after quitting, Huang issued a public statement saying he was open to returning as CEO. "I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," he said. "NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company," he added. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO." On the same day, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, Harvey Jones, told analysts on the company's earnings call that the board did "not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Kress, the following day, told company employees at the all-hands meeting, "Let's move forward." Nvidia's public stance against Huang returning came as members of Congress moved ahead with plans to interview him at hearings and as criticism grew over the company's business in Asia. The Department of Justice and the Commerce Department, in an unusual joint public statement on Nov. 17, said they were investigating Megaspeed for possible diversion of advanced Nvidia semiconductor chips to China in violation of U.S. export control law. "Sensitive technologies like semiconductors are among the most valuable and strategic assets of the U.S. economy," the departments said. But days later, senior Trump administration officials contacted Nvidia's board to tell them that Jensen Huang himself was not a risk, according to the sources. The Department of Commerce added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist later Monday. Trump, during his interview Monday with CNBC, was asked what Attorney General Todd Blanche had told him about potential criminal liability for Huang and the question of whether Nvidia chips had ended up in China in violation of U.S. export laws. "They did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he, himself, was exonerated," Trump said . Both Trump and Vice President JD Vance became convinced that Huang was a singular figure who is preventing closed-source model AI companies, such as Anthropic, from getting too powerful, according to a person familiar with the matter, who spoke on condition of anonymity to disclose private discussions. The person said Trump and Vance were briefed on the national security elements of the situation and saw no evidence that Huang did anything illegal or untoward in that regard. Trump believes his administration's close working relationship with Huang gives the U.S. its best opportunity to protect national security and prevent cutting-edge AI chips from reaching banned customers, according to the person. Trump said he spoke with Huang on Sunday, after Nvidia had voted unanimously to reinstate him. "I called him up, and I said: 'I ask you to do one thing, Jensen. Work hard,'" Trump said. "He knows what to do and what not to do," Trump said. "But I just said work hard because if you work hard, there's nobody that can capture what you've done. Nobody, nobody close." — CNBC's Kevin Breuninger and Kif Leswing contributed to this article.

Trump's appeal adds to growing calls for Huang's return, including a petition with more than 200,000 signatures that Elon Musk has signed. Huang, who co-founded the AI chip giant in 1993, is due to answer lawmakers' questions in Congress on 1 December. "I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the company, and also, for the U.S.A.," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform on Sunday. Trump has stepped up his support over the past week for Huang's return. Last Monday, he said he "would not mind" seeing Huang reinstated. On Friday, he told reporters at the White House that he "would love to see Jensen be given a second chance". Huang resigned on 12 November after it emerged that he had two extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy. Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations and US authorities said they have not reached a conclusion. The "Stand with Jensen" petition, an open letter to Nvidia's board, had more than 206,000 signatures as of Monday morning, according to its website. More than 10,000 signatories claim to be current Nvidia employees. The letter asked the board to "bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts". It also highlighted that Nvidia and Huang have not endorsed it. "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too," Musk wrote on X on 13 November. Tobi Lütke, CEO of e-commerce platform Shopify, and Tim Sweeney, CEO of Fortnite developer Epic Games, have also signed it. Huang said on 17 November that he would be "honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO" if the board judged that best for the company, its staff, its shareholders, and America. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on 15 November that Nvidia needed "a dramatic shake-up" and a CEO from outside the company. However, in an interview with CBS on Sunday, he stated: "I said they should go to the outside, but he's on the outside now". Thus far, Nvidia's board does not plan to bring him back. Chair Harvey Jones told analysts during the company's earnings call last Tuesday that the board had "unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO". Colette Kress, Nvidia's finance chief, has taken over as interim CEO during the search for a permanent replacement. An outside law firm is currently undertaking an investigation. Nvidia's shares closed around $125.5 on Friday, representing a 48% collapse since their intraday all-time high price of roughly $243.3 on 6 October. They lost over 20% just last week, their seventh weekly decline in a row and the longest losing streak since 2008. The slide continued despite Nvidia beating earnings forecasts last Tuesday. Friday's 14% drop followed a Reuters report, citing two people briefed on the matter, that the Securities and Exchange Commission, the US markets regulator, was examining possible accounting issues at Nvidia. Huang will answer questions from three House committees behind closed doors on 1 December: Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party. The committees are looking into the possible diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese businesses. The session will be a transcribed interview and will not be open to the public. Huang's public testimony will come before the Senate Banking Committee, according to the office of its chair, Republican Senator Tim Scott. No date has been set, though Scott had originally asked for 3 December. Two Nvidia shareholders, the investment firms Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management, have asked the board to keep Huang's return open and to hold off on a permanent CEO until all the facts are known.

"I convinced them," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview Monday morning , shortly after Nvidia announced Huang's return.

Trump, during his interview Monday with CNBC, was asked what Attorney General Todd Blanche had told him about potential criminal liability for Huang and the question of whether Nvidia chips had ended up in China in violation of U.S. export laws.
Trump said he spoke with Huang on Sunday, after Nvidia had voted unanimously to reinstate him.
